## locks & concurrency

- [ ] **[HIGH PRIORITY] Lock hygiene umbrella — prevent avoidable locks, auto-recover the unavoidable ones** — across the relay/git toolchain, lock-related stalls keep costing manual intervention. Two goals: **(A) PREVENT avoidable locks** and **(B) AUTO-FIX/AUTO-RECOVER** the rest so a human never has to `rm` a lock or hand-clean a tree. Known lock surfaces to cover: (1) stale `.git/index.lock` left by a killed/OOM'd git process (cf. [[oom-local-model-session-kills]] — 6 sessions died at once) → blocks every subsequent git op until manually removed; a pre-op guard should detect a lock whose owning PID is dead (or older than a TTL) and clear it before retrying. (2) flock files — `.git-lock-push.lock`, `/tmp/claude-git-*.lock`, broker/append locks — the 30s flock timeout fails the op rather than diagnosing a dead holder; add PID-liveness + stale-age recovery and a clear error naming the holder. (3) the **fd-8 self-nesting deadlock** in `git-lock-push.sh` (a caller already holding the repo lock re-execs `8>` the same file → 30s deadlock) — id:3b18. (4) `claim.sh` leases that outlive a dead run (already TTL-expire, but verify no path leaves a permanent lease). (5) dirty-tree "soft locks" that block dispatch/integration: build-artifact false-positives (id:6366), `uv.lock` drift (id:bae5), orphan worktrees from un-`--force`d removal (id:d187). The deeper structural fix for write contention is worktree-per-session + flock'd merge (id:3558). **This item is the umbrella**: triage which lock surfaces are *avoidable by design* (eliminate) vs *need auto-recovery* (build a shared stale-lock reaper: PID-liveness + mtime-TTL, used by git-diary-workflow, relay integrator, append.sh, broker), then either close via the existing point-items or spawn new ones. Observe-before-preventing applies (cf. design heuristics) — but the manual-cost evidence already exists across the cited ids. Trigger: 2026-06-21 `/relay --afk` session (user request). <!-- children:3b18,6366,bae5,d187 --> <!-- id:d2cd -->

## mechanization (all skills)

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`memory-index.py`: warn per-ENTRY on an oversized `hook:`, not just on the aggregate index size** — today `size_warning()` fires only when the whole `MEMORY.md` blows its ceiling, so an individual bloated hook is invisible until it surfaces months later as index overflow. Measured 2026-08-12 on the dotclaude-skills memory dir: the index had grown to 26,283 B / 115 entries, **past the ~24.4 KB harness truncation** — i.e. entries were silently not reaching sessions. Because `build_entries()` (`tools/memory-index.py:196-204`) orders by existing pointer order then appends new files, the truncated tail is the **newest** memories, inverting the value ordering. Root cause is drift in what a hook is for: pre-July hooks average ~165 B, post-mid-July ~290 B, worst was 784 B (a hook narrating its own diagnostic history) — hooks became session summaries rather than recall triggers, and nothing enforced the stated ~200-char guidance. **Fix:** emit a per-entry stderr WARNING when a hook exceeds ~250 chars (never a failure — same posture as the existing aggregate warning), so the next oversized hook is loud at write time. **Also reconcile the two ceilings:** the tool's `--ceiling` default is 17,100 B while the harness truncates near 24.4 KB; either document 17,100 as "harness limit minus safety margin" or raise it, so the warning threshold means something. Fable-agent recommendation 2026-08-12, owner-ratified. *(Observation, not approved scope: 22 memory files carry `hook:` nested under `metadata:` instead of top level, so every run prints 22 resolvable WARNINGs — noise that can mask a real one. Worth folding in if this item is picked up.)* <!-- id:d0c6 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Resolving an `[INPUT — decision]` item leaves its lane tag stale — the `/relay human` write-back must re-lane the source line, not just append the decision** (found 2026-08-01, `/meeting` ledger-hygiene sweep) — when `/relay human` captures an owner decision and promotes the item, it appends the decision prose and writes the ROADMAP twin, but never touches the TODO line's HEAD TAG. **Observed the same day, 15 minutes apart:** `id:8df5` was decided (build (B)) and promoted to `ROADMAP.md` as `[HARD]`, yet its TODO line still read `[INPUT — decision]`, so the very next `classify.sh` run reported it as pending human input — a decision that had already been made. The stale tag is not cosmetic: `[INPUT — decision]` is what keeps an item OUT of the pool's dispatchable set, so a resolved item stays invisible to the pool for as long as the tag survives. Fix in `relay/references/human.md`'s write-back step (§5): when a decision RESOLVES an `[INPUT — *]` item, the same `md-merge.py` call that appends the decision must also rewrite the head tag to the lane the resolution implies (`[HARD]`/`[ROUTINE]` if it became buildable, `[x]` if it closed) — and when the implied lane is not unambiguous, SURFACE it rather than guess (the never-silently-default-a-disposition rule). Acceptance: a fixture item tagged `[INPUT — decision]` that is resolved-and-promoted comes back from `classify.sh` in a dispatchable class, not `HUMAN`. Relates id:78ff (explicit lanes), id:968c (settled-but-open detection — this is the same family, caught at write time instead of by a later audit), [[mechanization-decision-rule-415b]]. <!-- id:c4b4 -->

- [ ] **[INPUT — meeting] Hard, mode-proof, un-gameable destructive-op containment for automated/subagent workflows** (user 2026-07-20) — the destructive-op guardrail is currently ONLY prompt-level (`permissions.ask`: `rm -f/-rf`, `git * --force`, `reset --hard`, `restore`, `checkout --`, `clean -f/-d`, now `stash drop/clear`) + CLAUDE.md prose. **Two proven holes:** (1) **`permissions.deny` is INERT under `permissionMode: auto`** (empirical, id:5937 2026-07-10: auto denies NOTHING across 12 classes; only OS DAC contains; `--disallowedTools` evadable via ToolSearch→Monitor) — and `auto` is the default for every unattended/afk relay run, and subagents inherit it → the guardrail is bypassed in exactly the automated context it's for (and `ask` prompts uselessly interrupt interactive automation while being equally bypassed under auto). (2) **A denylist blocks COMMANDS, not OUTCOMES** — the user's core concern: even a hard block on `git reset --hard` is gamed by reaching the same destructive end via `git restore` / `git checkout .` / `find -delete` / `shutil.rmtree` / `sh -c '…'` / **or an agent Edit-ing its own file back to fake a clean state** (id:373e faked-clean-tree). You cannot enumerate every syntactic path to a semantic outcome. **Design axes the meeting must weigh:** (A) enforcement layer — PreToolUse deny hook (fires regardless of permission mode, unlike `deny`; but still a syntactic blocklist, still evadable per id:5937) vs **OS DAC / the os-users sandbox** (id:13ae/d03d — structural: "can't destroy what you can't write"; the only layer id:5937 found actually contains) vs a combination; (B) recoverability as the real safety net — append-only / immutable canonical refs + reflog + worktree-per-session so a destroyed worktree never touches canonical history; (C) post-hoc DETECTION of the gamed outcome (id:9b9b commit-history audit, id:373e clean-tree check) accepting prevention is porous; (D) the "un-edit to game" vector specifically — how to detect/prevent an agent silently reverting its own work to fake state. **Also fold in:** the destructive `ask`/`deny` entries are HAND-MAINTAINED in settings.json with NO reproducible source (unlike the Bash *allow*-list which `make install-allowlist` generates via `tools/allowlist.py`) — they vanish on a settings reset; a generator/`make` target should own them. Relates id:5937 [[deny-probe-5937]], id:13ae/d03d [[os-users]], id:9b9b (commit-history integrity), id:373e [[force-free-cleanup-373e]], id:7a05/077d (hook framework — a PreToolUse guard would register here), [[enforce-contract]], the global CLAUDE.md §Destructive-op hygiene (the prose that gets ignored). — **UNATTENDED-STALL EVIDENCE + THE DESIGN LEVER, 2026-08-21 (owner-observed).** A background `id:81d5` executor reached for `git checkout -- .` mid-transform and ESCALATED A PERMISSION PROMPT into the parent session, which the owner answered once. In a fully unattended `--afk` pool run there is no answerer, so the run blocks. **The mechanism is NOT auto-mode leniency — it is CONFIGURED, and the two configured mechanisms differ exactly where it matters:** `permissions.deny` (8 entries, all `rm -f`/`-rf`/`--force` variants) FAILS CLOSED — a hard block with an error, no prompt, works unattended (verified live this session when an `rm -rf` was refused outright); `permissions.ask` (12 entries: `git push --force*`, `git * --force*`, `reset --hard*`, `restore *`, **`checkout -- *`**, `clean -f*`, `clean -d*`, `stash drop*`, `stash clear*`) PROMPTS in every mode, so each is an unattended stall BY CONSTRUCTION. That is this item's 'ONLY prompt-level' problem restated as a measured consequence rather than a risk. **Option space this opens:** (a) promote selected `ask` patterns to `deny` — safest unattended, but removes the interactive escape a human legitimately wants; (b) a HOOK, which fails closed like `deny` AND can be context-aware (an unattended run is identifiable — `RELAY_RUN_ID` is set and the heartbeat is live), so the same op can block for a pool child and prompt for a human — the shape `id:3a09` is being built in; (c) an `--afk` settings OVERLAY promoting `ask`→`deny` for the duration of an unattended run, leaving interactive sessions untouched. (b) and (c) are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives. **Partial coverage worth not rebuilding:** a prompt-blocked loop stops making progress, so it stops beating the `id:e149` heartbeat and the `id:98f0` outage watchdog notices — but it NOTIFIES, it does not unblock, so it converts a silent stall into a known one. **Lane tag converted `[HARD — meeting]`→`[INPUT — meeting]` in this same edit** — the pre-commit lane-vocab ratchet correctly BLOCKED the append, because touching a line re-stages it as added and the old venue-keyed vocabulary is banned for added lines. Relates id:3a09, id:5218, id:5937. <!-- id:9320 -->

- [ ] **[ROUTINE] Sudo-elevation ATTRIBUTION: make the askpass prompt say WHICH session/agent is asking and for WHAT** (user 2026-07-20; **RE-SCOPED from `[INPUT — meeting]` 2026-08-14 by owner decision, `/relay human .`**) — the current `SUDO_ASKPASS=/usr/lib/ssh/ssh-askpass sudo -A` (global CLAUDE.md §Sudo) has two failure modes now that many parallel sessions + background agents exist: (1) **no attribution** — an askpass popup is anonymous; you can't tell WHICH claude session/agent is asking for sudo, nor for WHAT command/why, so you can't judge whether to grant it; (2) **keyboard-grab / no context query** — `ssh-askpass` grabs keyboard input exclusively and is a bare password box, so there's no chance to inspect the task, see the pending command, or answer contextually. Design a replacement: a custom askpass helper that surfaces the requesting session id + the exact command + a task/why line (candidates: read `$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`/cwd/command from the sudo context, route through a non-modal channel — notification + the meeting/relay broker pattern, or a statusline/desktop-notification prompt — rather than a modal keyboard-grab). Needs a design call: what metadata is available to an askpass hook at elevation time, and which surfacing channel (broker IPC / notify-send + reply / a queue the human drains) fits. Relates the global CLAUDE.md §Sudo, `hooks/`, `meeting/broker.py` (IPC pattern), `statusline/`. **OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-14 (`/relay human .`): RE-SCOPE to the attribution half and build it NOW; do not hold a meeting first.** `orphan-scan --shipped` had flagged this item's gating clause as **24 days** stale (>=14d threshold) — the age reflected that no design session ever happened, not that the problem went away. Failure mode **(1) — an askpass popup is anonymous, so you cannot tell WHICH session/agent is asking, nor for WHAT command or why, and therefore cannot judge whether to grant it — is concrete and buildable without a design session**, so it is carved out and re-laned `[ROUTINE]`. Failure mode (2) and the broader mechanism-replacement question are NOT part of this item any more. **Acceptance**: an askpass prompt that names the requesting session id, the agent/mode if any, and the command being elevated; degrade each field to `-` rather than failing the prompt. Do NOT change WHETHER elevation is granted — attribution only, no policy change. Whether a `/meeting` is still warranted for the REST is deliberately deferred until this ships and is used: that reassessment is `id:18ce`, gated on this item. <!-- id:6c6e -->

- [ ] **[INPUT — meeting] A shared "reasoning-fallacy checkup" step for `/relay` and `/meeting`** (user 2026-07-17: "add TODO for /relay and /meeting: a not-invented-here (and other fallacies?) checkup step"). Both skills already encode anti-fallacy rules as **scattered prose the model may or may not recall** — CLAUDE.md's no-NIH rule, "verify before asserting", "observe before preventing", "constraint archaeology", "prefer dissolving over guarding", the id:415b determinism gate. There is no point at which any of them is *checked*. **EVIDENCE FROM ONE SESSION (2026-07-17), which is why this is not hypothetical — the same session both violated and honoured these rules, with no mechanism deciding which:** (a) **NIH, violated by the apex**: counting own repos, I ran a `~/src/*` glob — exactly what [[use-existing-tools]] bans ("relay.toml is THE own-repo set; never re-derive it from a `~/src/*` glob"). It silently included vendored clones (manim, whisper.cpp, alsa-ucm-conf) and missed the zkm plugins, producing a wrong figure I nearly argued from. `lib-own-repos.sh` existed the whole time. (b) **NIH, honoured by an executor**: id:34c2's child chose to shell out to the real `todo-conformance.sh` rather than copy its regex, so the two definitions of "conforming line" cannot drift. (c) **NIH, honoured by another executor**: id:1102's child factored a *third* copy of the `relay_FILES` awk parser into one shared function. (d) **VERIFY-BEFORE-ASSERTING, violated twice by the apex on ONE item**: id:1102 was filed with root cause "the hand-maintained list drops files" (FALSE — both files were listed) and then "make status is per-skill not per-file" (FALSE — it prints the exact file). Each check took **one command**. Had an executor been dispatched on either, it would have faithfully built the wrong thing. **THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH FALLACIES AND WHERE — do not just bolt on a checklist:** candidates are NIH (is there an existing tool? did I grep `scripts/`, the skill's Shared-resources list, the stated source-of-truth?), **assert-before-verify** (the session's most expensive failure — is this claim checked, or inferred?), symptom-vs-root-cause, premature abstraction / gold-plating, and confirmation bias in diagnosis (I kept finding causes that fit my first frame). **Design tensions the meeting must resolve:** (1) **a checklist is prose too** — the very failure mode is "prose the model doesn't recall", so a prose checkup may not beat the prose rules it replaces; what is *mechanizable* here (a `grep` for existing tooling before a new script? a "name the command that proves this" gate on root-cause claims?) versus what is irreducibly judgement — CLAUDE.md mechanize-first says mechanize what can be, and make the residual fail LOUDLY. (2) **per-prompt ctx multiplier** — /relay and /meeting are heavy already; a checkup step multiplies by session count (the CLAUDE.md ctx-budget rule for mandatory steps). (3) **where does it fire** — at handoff (before a spec is written), at review (before a verdict), at meeting decision points, or all three? A check that fires after the spec is written is too late; (d) above shows the damage lands *in the spec*. (4) **the id:de36/id:1102 lesson applies to this item itself**: a checkup nothing invokes is not a checkup. Relates [[use-existing-tools]], [[mechanization-415b]], [[no-labels]], [[mechanize-reliab]], CLAUDE.md §"Use existing tools; ask when unsure" + "Verify before asserting" + §Design heuristics. See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-07-17-1541-semver-trigger-and-fleet-changelog.md` (session context). <!-- id:0e56 -->

- [ ] **[/meeting] REVIEW_ME box freshness vs the ledger — a stale "RUN /meeting" box re-surfaced a settled item** (observed 2026-07-14) — the no-subject `/meeting` audit adds a synthetic Class-3 candidate for open REVIEW_ME boxes and treats a box's "RUN /meeting on id:X" text as a live request. A box can go STALE: id:9fdb's 2026-07-13 "RUN /meeting" box survived a 2026-07-14 TODO re-lane that settled the item (`[INPUT — meeting]`→`[HARD — pool]`, "meeting already held, mtg 1239 D4"), because nothing reconciles a REVIEW_ME box against the referenced id's CURRENT decision/lane state in TODO/ROADMAP → a redundant-meeting recommendation (caught this session only by reading the ratified source). The id:37ab classify fix closes the CLASSIFIER vector but NOT this REVIEW_ME-box vector. **Directions:** (a) when surfacing an open box that references `id:X`, cross-check X against TODO/ROADMAP — if X is now `[x]`, or re-laned off a meeting lane, or carries a DECIDED/RE-LANED note dated after the box, flag it `possibly-stale` and DON'T recommend a meeting off it; (b) mechanize a box↔ledger freshness lint in `orphan-scan.sh`; (c) accept the reviewer-prune cadence as the only guard + document it. Observe-first: FIRST observed instance — prefer the cheap surface-flag (a) over building (b) now. Instance of the "check a derived doc against its ratified source before a pre-registered rule fires" heuristic. **OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 (relay human): PRIORITIZED — the observe-first gate is now DISCHARGED; this is no longer a single instance.** A 5-classifier `/relay human --all` sweep produced **hard recurrence evidence across 4 repos in one pass**: of 6 tier-(a) auto-answers, **3 were stale-box closures rather than verdicts** — cyclotomic-projection `REVIEW_ME:122` asserted "ROADMAP is DRAINED (0 open items)" when `grep -c '^- \[ \]' ROADMAP.md` = **2** (and "11 un-promoted" when the real count was 13); collaib `REVIEW_ME:254` asserted "14 orphan header stubs" when only **3** headers exist and 4 of its 14 listed ids have zero occurrences; cyclotomic `REVIEW_ME:148` asked to confirm a default-flip the owner had already REVERSED and shipped (id:e52d). Two classifiers independently named the pattern unprompted ("reviews are minting boxes faster than they prune them"). **The measurable shape is that a box asserts COUNTS/STATE that are cheaply re-derivable and go wrong silently** — which is what makes direction (b) mechanizable: a lint that re-checks a box's own asserted counts against the live ledger would have caught all 3. Recommend (a)+(b) together now rather than (a) alone; (c) is refuted — the reviewer-prune cadence is exactly what failed here (these boxes survived multiple review passes). Sibling vector: the 2026-07-16 sweep also found a box's file:line SHIFTS under a concurrent review rewrite (yinyang `3709` moved :45→:75 mid-sweep), so any mechanized check must anchor on the id, never a line number. <!-- id:2e5c -->

- [ ] **New skill: `rebrand-project` — atomically re-brand/rename a project across git remote + local + Claude state** (user 2026-07-01, motivated by the truncocraft→loderite **rebrand** done semi-manually). "Rebrand" (not just "rename") is the better frame: truncocraft→loderite was a public-NAME/brand change ([[nomi]] naming meeting), so the skill covers ALL brand surfaces — repo name, package/module name, in-app/UI strings, docs & README, domain/handle — not only the filesystem path. A project rename is a multi-surface manual chore that easily strands dangling links; mechanize it. Given `<old> <new>`: (1) rename the git REMOTE (fievel bare `src/<old>.git`→`src/<new>.git`, and GitHub via `gh repo rename`) and update the local remote URL(s); (2) rename the local dir `~/src/<old>`→`~/src/<new>` and fix worktree/ref paths; (3) MOVE the Claude project state so memories + sessions stay linked to the NEW location — the per-project dir is keyed by a path-slug (`~/.claude/projects/-home-tobias-src-<old>` → `-home-tobias-src-<new>`), so rename `projects/<slug>/` (memory/, MEMORY.md, sessions/transcripts) to the new slug and fix absolute-path refs inside; (4) update `relay.toml` `[repos.<old>]`→`[repos.<new>]` (+ any `# path:` override) and cross-repo inbox `routed:`/`[<old>]` targets; (5) grep the wider tree for stale references (diary `-p` path pointers, meeting-note project paths, ROADMAP/TODO cross-links). ## Relay

- [x] [ROUTINE] **Base-ref resolution must use the repo's ACTUAL checked-out branch — never a hard-coded `origin/main` → `main` → `master` guess** (owner ruling 2026-08-26, stated as a general invariant: *"clearly always the actually checked-out branch must be used, never a hard-coded 'use main, try master'"*). **FIRED LIVE** in run `relay-20260826-122101-7415`: `integrate:git-annex` failed with `MECH-ERROR exit=2 — stranded-branch-scan.sh: base ref 'main' does not resolve in '/home/tobias/src/git-annex'`, handing back a `contract_met:true` unit (21/21 tests green, commit `7727d71eab`) that had to be merged by hand. git-annex is a fork of the upstream project: its refs are `master` (upstream mirror, BEHIND), `annex-dotgit` (the real checked-out working branch) and `backup-pre-e49a`; `origin` is a private LAN host with no `origin/HEAD` symbolic ref. Note a `master` fallback would NOT have fixed it — it resolves, but to the stale mirror, so the scan would have silently reported against the wrong base instead of failing loudly. That is why the ruling is checked-out-branch, not an extended guess-list. **The invariant is already RATIFIED and IMPLEMENTED on the integrate path as id:8739** — `integrate.sh:455-465` uses the canonical checkout's current `HEAD` *as a sha, not a name* ("no branch-name guess, no remote round-trip") and explicitly REFUSES to fall back to `verify-isolation.sh`'s `origin/main` default, which id:4d44 froze. So this item is PROPAGATION of an existing decision, not a new design. **Two remaining offenders:** (1) `relay/scripts/stranded-branch-scan.sh:68-74` — `origin/main` → `main`, then hard `exit 2`; this is the one that fired, and it is permanently fatal for git-annex (every future pool run fails its integrate identically). (2) `relay/scripts/verify-isolation.sh:78-91` — tries `origin/main`, then `origin/HEAD`, then still lands on a hard-coded `"main"`; masked in practice ONLY because integrate.sh always passes `--base` per id:8739, so any direct caller still hits it. Fix both to derive from `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` (or the passed `--base`), keeping id:8739's fail-CLOSED posture — an undeterminable base must hand back loudly, never silently pick a plausible-looking ref. Blast radius verified 2026-08-26: git-annex is the ONLY one of 62 own repos with no resolvable `main`. Also fix the misleading handback text — `RELAY_STATUS.md` recorded `integrate.sh produced no merged= line (unparseable integrator output)`, the downstream symptom, sending a reader after an integrator parsing bug; the real cause existed only in the workflow journal. — DONE 2026-08-26: covered by tests (`tests/test_base_ref_resolution_758a.sh` + the pre-existing RED spec `tests/test_base_ref_checked_out_branch_758a.sh`, both green); commit `478d70d2`; full suite 502/0/1. <!-- id:758a -->
- [x] [HIGH PRIORITY] [ROUTINE] **`mechanical` verdict is a SILENT DEAD END — the pool declares work is "for the host daemon" but nothing ever writes the recipe, and the daemon has been idle since 2026-07-13.** `RELAY_STATUS.md` routes `trAIdBTC`, `isochrone` and `llm-from-scratch` as `verdict=mechanical (pool-inert: pure-compute work for the host daemon, A3-gated; never dispatched by the LLM pool)` — which READS as a routing decision and IS, in practice, a drop. Verified 2026-08-26: `mechanical-daemon.path` + `.service` are installed and enabled, path-activated on `PathModified=~/.config/relay/recipes/pending`; the daemon WORKS (last tick 2026-07-13 17:33 processed its queue `ran=1 deferred=0 rejected=0`, 5 recipes in `done/` with matching `artifacts/`); but `pending/` has been EMPTY since 2026-07-13 and **`grep -c 'recipes/pending|mechanical-daemon|recipe' relay/scripts/relay-loop.js` returns 0** — the pool has ZERO wiring to the drop-dir. The `.path` unit's own comment says *"a relay reviewer session is the only writer (recipe-manifest.md whitelist invariant)"*, so the recipe write is a REVIEWER-session step that the autonomous pool never performs. Net effect: every `mechanical` unit the pool classifies is announced as routed and then silently goes nowhere, indefinitely — the exact [[relay-builtgreen-but-unreferenced]] shape (built + tested + green + unreferenced), and the anti-pattern the mechanize-first rule names (a deterministic detector whose resolution silently no-ops). Decide the owner-facing question first: SHOULD the pool write recipes itself (needs the whitelist invariant honoured from an unattended context), or is `mechanical` meant to be a HUMAN-relay handoff — in which case it must surface in the human queue / decision queue instead of reading as dispatched. Until then the honest status line is "not routed anywhere", not "for the host daemon". **OWNER DECISION 2026-08-26 — option A ratified: WIRE THE BUILT DRAFT LOOP + SURFACE.** The pool does NOT author recipes into `pending/` (that was considered and NOT chosen — it would weaken the id:64d3 whitelist boundary the 2026-07-02-1924 meeting ratified against Riku's objection, since an unattended `--afk` pool is not the 'human-authored intermediate artifact' the invariant exists to guarantee; re-opening it needs a fresh owner ruling, not an inference from the old wording). Scope as ratified: (1) call `relay-doctor.sh` check-12 (id:1bd1) / `mechanical-orphan-draft.sh` (id:8a6b) from the pool or review path so an orphaned `[MECHANICAL]` item auto-drafts a skeleton into `drafts/`; (2) SURFACE the pending drafts ('N mechanical drafts awaiting promotion') in `RELAY_STATUS.md` and the human/decision queue; (3) the promote step `drafts/`→`pending/` STAYS HUMAN — that is the trust boundary and it is deliberately unchanged. Both scripts already exist and have ZERO callers (`grep -c` in relay-loop.js = 0 for each), so this builds nothing new: it adds call sites and one status section. Drafts stay non-executable by construction (`est_wall` is a string placeholder that `recipe-validate.sh` hard-rejects), so wiring the drafter cannot itself trigger execution. Also fixes the misleading status line — `verdict=mechanical (pool-inert: ... for the host daemon)` announces routing that does not exist; it must read as awaiting-recipe. TIMING: owner chose to let the running pool drain first (dotclaude-skills was under an execute lease), then edit directly. **CADENCE RATIFIED 2026-08-26: the drafter runs PER POOL ROUND, not only in the review path.** Rationale: check-12 is pure bash over `ROADMAP.md` + the drop-dir (no LLM, no agents), so a per-round call is free; and a repo that never receives a review pass would otherwise never draft its orphans — which is exactly how the 7 current orphans accumulated unseen. Review-path-only was considered and rejected on that coverage gap. **CORRECTION 2026-08-26 (my own framing was wrong — verified against the live artifact).** This item called the mechanical verdict a **SILENT** dead end. That is FALSE and I should have checked before writing it: `relay-status-publish.sh:96-100` already renders a live `## Mechanical orphans / drafts (id:8a6b)` section, the loop calls that script in 4 places, and `RELAY_STATUS.md:175` has been carrying the full orphan list — with the exact remedy text (*'no recipe anywhere; author one + promote drafts/ -> pending/ (it will never run)'*) — all along. The DETECTION half was never silent; it was loud and correct. Corrected count too: **13 orphans, not 7** — my 7 came from checking only the three repos the pool labelled `mechanical` verdict, but `ai-codebench` (×5: bde7/fadb/0ce2/8c1d/3ee7) and `loderite` (1ae5) also carry orphaned [MECHANICAL] items without being classified `mechanical` (they had other work). Full set: isochrone 11c3; trAIdBTC 3a50; llm-from-scratch e868/cf0d/e617/a477/9e89; ai-codebench bde7/fadb/0ce2/8c1d/3ee7; loderite 1ae5. **What IS genuinely missing (unchanged, and still the whole point of this item): the DRAFTING.** `mechanical-orphan-draft.sh` had ZERO callers, `drafts/` has been empty since 2026-07-31, and the daemon has been idle since 2026-07-13 — all independently verified. So the accurate framing is: detect ✓ (loud), draft ✗ (built, never wired), promote ✗ (nothing to promote), execute ✓ (daemon works). That is still the mechanize-first anti-pattern — a detector whose RESOLUTION no-ops — but 'silent dead end' overstated it, and the honest value of wiring the drafter is turning 'author a recipe from scratch' into 'fill in the TODO fields of a pre-built skeleton', not 'make the invisible visible'. The `[HIGH PRIORITY]` tag is left as-is for the owner to re-judge on this corrected basis. — DONE 2026-08-26 (wiring + surfacing, the ratified scope): covered by tests (`tests/test_mechanical_orphan_draft_wiring_391b.sh`) AND verified end-to-end independently of that test — a real drafter run wrote 13 skeletons, `recipe-validate.sh` hard-rejects one, `pending/` stayed 0. - [x] [ROUTINE] **Repeat-handback ALERT (id:1432) did not fire on two repos that each handed back twice in one run** — `RELAY_STATUS.md`'s `## Repeat-handback ALERTs (id:1432 — >=2× this run, a bug signal)` printed `_(none)_` while the Blocked section of the SAME file listed `lean4btc` twice (worktrees `…-hard-repo-0` and `…-hard-repo-1`, reasons `integrate.sh produced no merged= line`) and `it-infra` twice (identical prompt-size-gate reason). On the section's own stated threshold both should have alerted. Observed run `relay-20260826-122101-7415`, 2026-08-26. Determine whether the counter keys on a unit identity that differs between retries (e.g. the per-attempt worktree suffix `-0`/`-1`) rather than on `(repo, mode)` or `(repo, reason)` — if so the detector can only ever fire for a literally identical unit key, which is the case least likely to recur. The whole point of id:1432 is catching a repo that keeps failing the same way, and it is currently blind to exactly that. Cross-check against [[relay-builtgreen-but-unreferenced]] before assuming the counter is wired at all. **HYPOTHESIS REFUTED, REAL CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-26 (delegated; claims re-verified independently).** This item guessed the counter keys on a per-attempt identity (the `-0`/`-1` worktree suffix). **That is WRONG.** `trackHandback()`'s key is `${repo}:${verdict}` (`relay-loop.js:1364-1369`) — the classifier verdict, which does NOT change between retries; the `-0`/`-1` suffix is threaded only into the worktree PATH and BRANCH name via `unitKey`/`worktreePathFor`/`branchFor`, never into the tracker key. Two handbacks of the same repo+verdict already shared one key. **The actual cause is far larger: `relay-loop.js` had ELEVEN distinct `state.handbacks.push(` sites — one per handback class (null-report/context-death, contract_met=false, sibling-branch, landed-unfinished, integrate no-merged-line, durable-followup-failure, INTENSIVE fail-closed, stranded-dispatch, prompt-size gate, provision-failed, integrator-threw) — and only ONE of them called `trackHandback()`.** Verified on the pre-fix blob: `grep -c 'state.handbacks.push('` = 11, `grep -c 'trackHandback(handbackTracker,'` = 1. BOTH observed reasons (`integrate.sh produced no merged= line`, and the prompt-size-gate reason) came from unwired sites, so the detector could not have fired for either — another [[relay-builtgreen-but-unreferenced]] instance: the accumulator and its renderer were built and correct, and 10/11 producers simply never fed them. FIXED: all 11 push sites now pair with a `trackHandback()` call (11/11 verified). Two sites are extracted stand-alone by existing hermetic tests that don't carry `handbackTracker` in scope, so those calls are guarded `typeof trackHandback === 'function'` — safe, but it means those two paths are NOT exercised by the extracted tests. KEY KEPT as `(repo, verdict)`: `(repo, reason)` would systematically UNDER-count, because reason strings embed volatile detail (byte counts, truncated stdout) that legitimately differs between two occurrences of the same failure — recreating this bug in a new guise. Known miss of `(repo, verdict)`: if id:907e reclassifies a repo between handbacks for the same blocker, the two land under different keys; out of scope (both observed repos handed back under the same verdict twice). — DONE 2026-08-26: covered by tests (`tests/test_repeat_handback_wiring_7354.sh`, negative control observed failing against the unfixed logic); commit `01ce9b9c`; 11/11 push sites now paired, verified by grep on the pre- and post-fix blobs. <!-- id:7354 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`integrate.sh`'s exit code conflates "I did my job and refused" with "I could not reach a verdict" — a correct handback renders as ✗ FAILED in the Workflow** (owner observation 2026-08-26: *"shouldn't the integrator doing its job exit 0 and only the git-annex issue non-zero?"* — yes). `integrate.sh` defines 15 distinct non-zero handback codes (`EX_CLEAN_TREE=20` … `EX_RATIFY=35`, lines 218-236) and `exit 0` only on full success (line 1256). The mechanical proxy turns ANY non-zero exit into `MECH-ERROR exit=<N>` (`relay-loop.js:928,943`), and the Workflow progress UI keys its ✗ purely on that — so THREE materially different outcomes render identically. Observed in run `relay-20260826-122101-7415`: (i) **genuine failure** — git-annex, `exit=2`, base ref unresolvable, no verdict ever reached, work stranded until hand-merged; (ii) **landed-but-unfinished** — yinyang-puzzle, `EX_RETIRE=28`, merge COMMITTED+TAGGED+PUSHED and only post-land worktree-retire failed, i.e. it succeeded at everything that matters yet shows ✗; (iii) **unparseable verdict** — lean4btc ×2, `exit=2`/`exit=255`. The relay's OWN accounting already draws the right line — `agent-failures=0` is defined (id:06a1, `relay-loop.js:493`) as *"failed with NO handback"*, deliberately excluding handbacks because a handback IS the mechanism working — so the Workflow ✗ and `RELAY_STATUS.md` disagree by design, and neither alone answers "was work lost?". **Proposed contract:** exit 0 when integrate.sh REACHED a verdict and executed it (merged, or legitimately refused — the verdict already travels in stdout as `merged=`/`handback=`/`landed=`, which the loop parses); reserve non-zero for genuinely UNDETERMINABLE outcomes. Decide explicitly what (ii) should be — exit 0, or a distinct `partial` code — since `landed=true` with incomplete cleanup is neither success nor failure. NOTE the step-identity currently carried by the exit code must not be lost: move it wholly into the parsed stdout contract before flattening the codes, or handback attribution regresses. **CORRECTION 2026-08-26 (run completed; the workflow's own failure report contradicts my first attribution).** The run ended reporting exactly THREE agent failures, all identical: `[integrate:git-annex] failed: There's an issue with the selected model (bash)` and `[integrate:lean4btc] failed: <same>` ×2. That message is the `model:"bash"` 404 signature — the proxy's `_command_allowed()` REFUSED the hop's command shape and FAILED OPEN to the real API, which has no model named `bash`. So for those three, **`integrate.sh` never executed at all**: there was no stdout, which is exactly why the handback reads `integrate.sh produced no merged= line (unparseable integrator output)`. That is NOT an integrate.sh exit code and NOT a verdict — it is a hop that never ran. Consequences for this item: example (i) git-annex and example (iii) lean4btc ×2 are **re-attributed** and do not evidence the exit-code conflation; example (ii) yinyang-puzzle (`EX_RETIRE=28`, landed+tagged+pushed, only post-land retire failed) STANDS and is still a genuine integrate.sh non-zero exit rendering as ✗. The conflation claim itself is unchanged — 15 non-zero handback codes still collapse into one ✗ — but it now rests on (ii) plus the code reading, not on three live examples. **The three 404s belong to id:2e7a / id:5552 instead** (the preflight probes the TRANSPORT, not the COMMAND SHAPE), and are strong live evidence for them: the launch preflight reported `proceed` AND `current` (proxy pid 2750 holding the on-disk allowlist), yet three integrate hops still 404'd — so a healthy socket + a current allowlist still does not imply a given fenced command survives `_command_allowed`. NOTE the failure was LOUD (an agent error, surfaced in the run's failure list), not a silent LLM-on-the-critical-path: nothing merged. Also note the earlier `stranded-branch-scan.sh: base ref 'main' does not resolve` MECH-ERROR is a SEPARATE, real failure of a different hop (id:758a) — both were true, and conflating them was my error. <!-- id:2c2a -->
- [ ] [HARD] [INPUT — decision] **The pool's round barrier is artificial: discovery should re-scan and queue continuously for every repo NOT currently in flight, instead of waiting for the whole wave to drain** (owner design call 2026-08-26). `relay-loop.js:4478` is `while (round < MAX_ROUNDS) { await runRound() }`, and `runRound()` is documented at `:1203` as *"one re-discover → dispatch wave → **drain**"* — a strict barrier. Observed live in run `relay-20260826-122101-7415`: round 2 dispatched 32 units; 26 completed and 7 blocked within ~45 min, then the ENTIRE pool sat idle for 45+ more minutes behind ONE slow unit (leAIrn2learn handoff, blocked on a long pytest), with 61 other repos unscanned and zero dispatch capacity used. This is precisely the barrier/pipeline anti-pattern the Workflow tool's own guidance names (*"barrier latency is real … a barrier wastes the fast agents' idle time"*) — the pool uses `parallel()`-with-barrier semantics where `pipeline()` fits. **The cost objection does not hold, and the cheap path already exists:** `classify-repo.sh` is a MECHANICAL hop — deterministic, zero agents (the Drain-mode ratification records `ambiguous:false`) — and relay-loop already calls it directly at `:1625` (chain-end re-ask) and `:1820`. Round discovery additionally fans out LLM `discover-shard` classifiers (Sonnet, `meta.phases`), but those are signature-cached per repo (id:c3a6, `discover-sig.sh`), so an unchanged repo re-scans for free. So continuous re-discovery over non-in-flight repos is close to free TODAY. **Design questions for the owner, not settled here:** (a) does a repo become re-scannable the moment ITS unit lands, or only when nothing is in flight for it — the in-flight repo must stay excluded to avoid double-dispatch (the id:d530 `--priority` note records that a repo's own discovered unit must never double-dispatch); (b) how do the round-scoped accumulators behave when rounds stop being discrete — `RELAY_STATUS.md` sections already have MIXED temporality ([[relay-status-accounting-temporality]]), and `round=` becomes meaningless as a counter; (c) the two-consecutive-dry-discoveries termination and `MAX_ROUNDS` seatbelt both key on round identity and would need re-expressing; (d) interaction with the dispatch-scoped `--once`/`--after N` caps (id:a615) and the STOP sentinel, which are already dispatch-scoped rather than round-scoped and so may FIT this model better than the current one. Prior art to reuse, not reinvent: the off-Workflow drain (`drain-driver.mjs`, id:cd7a) already re-classifies per round via `classify-repo.sh` with no Workflow discovery agents at all. <!-- id:79fd -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Live include/exclude of repos in an ALREADY-RUNNING pool** (owner request 2026-08-26) — today `--exclude`/`--priority`/`--only` are LAUNCH-time only (`args.excludeRepos`/`priorityRepos`/`onlyRepo`, consumed once before sharding), so changing a running pool's repo membership is impossible: the only levers are `/relay stop` (ends the run) or `TaskStop` (kills in-flight children and orphans their worktrees). The concrete need: an operator wants to work a repo BY HAND while the pool is live — this session hit it exactly, wanting to edit `dotclaude-skills` relay scripts while the pool held a `dotclaude-skills` execute lease, where the only options were 'wait' or 'stop the whole run'. **Prior art to reuse, not reinvent: the STOP sentinel family** (id:c012 / id:cd94 / id:a615) already solves every hard part — a per-`runId` TARGETED sentinel file (`~/.config/relay/STOP.<runId>`, never a global one, because parallel pools are the normal case and an unscoped file gets STOLEN by whichever pool reaches the check first), checked at **every dispatch decision** rather than only at a round boundary (a chaining round never reaches one — run `relay-20260822-154630-17003` made 14 dispatches all stamped `round=1`), consumed fail-safe with removal as the LAST act, and logged with `scope=`/`run=` so 'which pool did this affect?' is answerable after the fact. A `~/.config/relay/MEMBERSHIP.<runId>` sentinel (or an `inject.sh`-style control channel — id:baf1/354f already has a take-at-discovery hop) should follow that exact shape rather than invent a second protocol. **Semantics to settle:** (a) does a live-exclude take effect only at the next DISPATCH decision (leaving an in-flight unit for that repo to drain — almost certainly right, mirroring `/relay stop`), or must it also refuse the pending integrate; (b) does live-INCLUDE re-add a repo dropped at launch, or only one excluded live — re-adding a launch-excluded repo means it was never sharded/classified, so discovery must re-enumerate it; (c) does an unknown repo name LOUD-reject as the launch-time flags do (it should — id:d530's precedent); (d) does it write `relay.toml`? **It must NOT** — both `--exclude` and `--priority` are explicitly per-run and never mutate the registry, precisely because a session-kill would otherwise leave a silent permanent exclusion. Interacts with id:79fd: once discovery is continuous rather than round-barriered, a live membership set becomes MORE load-bearing, since there is no round boundary at which a relaunch could have applied a new one. <!-- id:9459 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`claude-relay` should launch inside a tmux session when not already in one** (owner request 2026-08-26) — `tools/claude-relay.sh` currently `exec`s Claude directly in the calling terminal, so a long unattended run (`/relay --afk`, a chaining pool) dies with the terminal: closing the window, an SSH drop, or a laptop suspend kills the session and every in-flight child, parking their worktrees as `relay/orphan/*`. This is the same exposure the id:bde8 scope correction names — `/loop` retries early-exits but **dies with the session** — and the gap id:98f0's outage watchdog only *reports* after the fact. Wrapping the launcher in tmux makes the session survive the terminal and lets the owner reattach. Shape: if `$TMUX` is unset (not already inside tmux) AND `tmux` is on PATH, launch via `tmux new-session -A -s <name>` so a re-invocation ATTACHES to the existing session rather than starting a second Claude; if already inside tmux, or tmux is absent, run exactly as today (never nest, never hard-fail). Decide: the session name (fixed vs per-cwd — per-cwd avoids two repos fighting over one session), whether the proxy-healthy and proxy-direct branches both wrap, and whether an opt-out env var is wanted (the launcher is opt-in by design, id:e905). Keep it non-interactive-safe: `claude -p`/headless callers must not be wrapped. <!-- id:6c8c -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`relay-reconcile.sh` `classify_orphan` cannot detect SUPERSEDED orphans — and the gap is worst on the auto-integrating SAFE path** (found 2026-08-12 during `/relay reconcile --all`). `classify_orphan` (`relay/scripts/relay-reconcile.sh:316-334`) diffs the orphan against its OWN merge-base, which by construction says nothing about whether the work already landed on main another way: a superseded branch still shows a large non-empty merge-base delta. Its only supersession guard is the `empty diff → already integrated` case, which catches just the trivial form. **Measured:** 5 of 6 parked orphans this sweep were provably redundant — loderite's `save-backup-ring.ts`/`worldgen/cave.ts`/`perf-variance.ts`/`docs/perf-budget.md` byte-identical to main (`git diff --numstat main:<f> <branch>:<f>` empty), dotclaude's `id:ef9e` shipped as `lint-embedded-literals.mjs` (the orphan carried a dead `.py` twin), `id:37f2` already in `discover-repo.sh:99-149` as a superset. **The severe end is SAFE, not JUDGMENT:** ledger-only orphans AUTO-INTEGRATE under `--auto` (live — `relay-loop.js` runs `--auto-restart` on every stale-heartbeat restart, id:7809/c14d), and ledger writes are the most staleness-prone content there is. Verified by replaying the real branch through the classifier logic: the parked `relay-20260731-174550-21952-review` (REVIEW_ME/ROADMAP/TODO only) returns **SAFE**, so `--auto` would have re-added two REVIEW_ME boxes whose items are now `[x]` on main (`id:1f8e`, `routed:c555`) plus a stale ROADMAP review note. It survived 12 days only because a dirty main tree defers integration — an accident, not a guard. The classifier's safety rationale ("ledger-only ⇒ nothing executable changed ⇒ gaming-scan/suite-green vacuously satisfied") is about TEST INTEGRITY and does not address STALENESS at all. **Fix direction:** add a supersession test against CURRENT main before the ledger-only SAFE verdict — per-file byte identity, `git cherry`/patch-id equivalence, and/or id-state lookup in `ROADMAP.archive.md`/`TODO.archive.md`; a superseded branch should classify as its own disposition (safe-to-DISCARD) rather than SAFE-to-integrate. Relates `id:7809` (`--auto`), `id:c14d` (`--auto-restart`). <!-- id:4174 -->

- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **`/relay hotfix` (or similar) — a legitimate "just fix this bug now" path for a relay-onboarded repo, that still lands in the contract** (owner 2026-07-24) — today a relay-managed repo has no sanctioned fast path: every route (`executor`/`review`/`hard`/`drain`) assumes the RED-spec-first discipline, so an urgent one-line bug fix either waits for a handoff to author a spec, or gets done off-contract and silently skips the ledger. Both are bad; the second is what actually happens. **WANTED:** a mode where the fix ships FIRST and the contract is satisfied AFTERWARDS, without that becoming a laundering channel. **The design tension to resolve in the meeting** — the executor contract's definition-of-done is "the item's *previously-failing* tests now pass" (contract rule 2), which a hotfix inverts: the test is written after the fix, so it can be written to fit whatever the fix happens to do. That is exactly the self-authored-spec hazard id:0c86/id:077d exist to catch (a spec its own author wrote proves only that the code does what the author decided). So a hotfix mode needs a *different* integrity story than "trust the executor", not a waiver of the existing one. **Questions the meeting must answer:** (1) what is the minimum tracked artefact at fix time — a minted id + a one-line RELAY_LOG entry, or a full ROADMAP item? (2) is the post-fact RED test *mandatory before the next integrate* (a debt the next `/relay review` refuses to pass over), or advisory? (3) how is the post-fact test kept honest — mutation-test it against the pre-fix commit (it MUST fail there), which is mechanically checkable and is the natural anti-gaming primitive here; (4) what stops scope creep — a declared one-item scope with any spill-over becoming a filed follow-up rather than a widened fix, and a diff-size or file-count tripwire that forces a handback; (5) does it route through REVIEW_ME (a box the next review must clear) or straight to ROADMAP as a `[ROUTINE]` debt item; (6) who may invoke it — human-only, or may the pool self-declare a hotfix? Prior art in-repo: id:b780's "a review child fixed a flaky test in-flight" was RULED OUT OF SCOPE 2026-07-19 precisely because a verifier that can fix the artefact it verifies can launder its verdict — a hotfix mode must not re-open that hole by the back door. Relates the executor contract (`relay/references/executor-contract.md`, bump `contract vN`), id:108e (refactor is unverifiable by construction → make it a LOUD self-report, not a fake gate — same shape of answer may apply here), id:22da (`/relay refactor`, the sibling "work that doesn't fit RED-first" mode), id:0c86/id:077d (provenance-of-tick enforcement). <!-- id:3f12 -->

- [ ] **Re-wire `--drain` (`/relay .`) back onto the Workflow substrate — constraint-archaeology reversal of the 2026-07-19 Amendment** — **[GO-FORWARD as of 2026-07-24, owner-directed — REDUCED SCOPE: the Workflow pool via `--only <cwd>` ALREADY implements the full drain contract inline (`isBlockedRound`/`isDryRound` id:4ca8, blocked-vs-drained, K=2 dry, review-loop breaker id:365b), so this item is now just: make bare `/relay .` and `--drain` route to `--only <cwd>` (revert the 2026-07-19 off-Workflow amendment) and delete the off-Workflow branch. `--drain` becomes a pure doc/discoverability alias — no engine, no drain-stop plumbing (id:9f1b + id:2ca6 RETIRED as moot; this REVERSES the 2b23-amendment "KEPT" on evidence). The routing/alias half is UN-gated (the `--only` pool works today); only the mechanical-hop conversion id:94b8 remains gated on the model:bash run. SUPERSEDES id:93fe; drain-driver.mjs kept as frozen headless fallback.]** GATED on a successful end-to-end **model:"bash" relay run** completing first (proxy interception proven live: id:4239 landed + a run launched via `claude-relay` so the mechanical hops transit the proxy). RATIONALE: the 2026-07-19 Amendment moved bare `/relay .` OFF the Workflow harness on the grounds that the per-round **discovery/mechanical agents** were pure waste for one repo — but that harness was ALSO the thing that structurally enforced the D3 verdict-class order (execute→review→hard→handoff) and the anti-gaming REVIEW gate. Removing it made the drain a loop-with-no-body whose review step is discretionary (apex-remembered, not engine-enforced), which already cost us real bugs — see the filed inbox items [[id:75b3]] (SEVERE: the loderite `0xff==cube` contract bug shipped TWICE through a body-less drain) and [[id:2da8]] (drain must handle ALL verdict classes, not just execute). Now that `model:"bash"` (mechanical-proxy id:176f) makes those per-round agents CHEAP (intercepted locally, zero real model calls), the constraint that justified going off-Workflow has LAPSED — so put `--drain`/`/relay .` BACK on the Workflow and regain the structural review-gate + verdict-class ordering for free. This is a design-direction REVERSAL (owner's to ratify): re-justify vs. the off-Workflow `drain-driver.mjs` (id:cd7a) before rewiring. Pairs [[id:75b3]], [[id:2da8]], [[id:79f2]]; fixes the class the drain inbox items describe. <!-- id:7488 -->
- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **`/relay --bg [handoff|exec|review|next|…]` — run the directed subcommand IN a spawned background agent, not inline on the orchestrator turn** (user 2026-07-23; fold into the id:931c/id:d03d agent-types meeting, do NOT spawn a parallel one). MOTIVATION: the directed modes (`handoff`/`review`/`next`/`human`) are currently driven by the apex/foreground turn hand-following `SKILL.md` prose — a "handwaving orchestrator" that can skip or reinterpret contract steps (the class behind [[id:75b3]]/routed:e2d6 body-less-drain review-gate, routed:d6be mechanize-role-boundaries, the "prose rule silently no-ops → enforce" cluster [[review-me-relay-discipline-cluster-16e3-3684]]). `--bg` makes the SPAWNED agent the one that actually runs `/relay <sub>`, keeping the apex turn lean ([[feedback-delegate-mechanical-to-background-agents]]) and letting the run's contract live in a constrained agent-def rather than an expensive judgment turn. **SENSIBLE/EFFICIENT SHAPE (recommendation, owner to ratify):** (1) The **default pool already runs as a background Workflow**, so `--bg` is redundant for bare `/relay` — it is meaningful ONLY for the DIRECTED subcommands the apex turn runs inline. (2) **Hard constraint:** `handoff`/`review`/`human`/`next` today call `AskUserQuestion`, which a background agent CANNOT invoke — so `--bg` must run the subcommand in a STRICTLY non-interactive posture: any point that would ask instead takes the `--afk` conservative surface-don't-act default and defers to `RELAY_STATUS.md`/REVIEW_ME (never guesses). (3) **Mechanism:** the front door, on `--bg <sub>`, calls the Agent tool with `run_in_background:true`, `subagent_type` = the codified relay agent-def for that subcommand (from [[id:931c]] — `relay-execute`/`relay-review`/`relay-handoff`), prompt = "invoke `/relay <sub>`, follow the executor/reviewer contract EXACTLY, non-interactive, report structured result"; the child invokes the Skill tool itself and returns; the foreground integrates on the completion notification (verify-before-merge unchanged). (4) **Scope caution:** cleanest for SINGLE-unit directed work (one repo / one item). A `--bg` agent that itself fans out a whole pool = nested background agents (depth/limit risk) — for fleet fan-out keep the Workflow path; don't nest. (5) **Not a security boundary:** a `--bg` agent's tool list is ergonomic-only, never containment (the id:5937/id:453a invariant from [[id:931c]] applies verbatim); real enforcement stays the integration-boundary guards + the OS-DAC/uid work (id:d03d). **Decision for the meeting:** which subcommands get `--bg`, the non-interactive-deferral contract, and whether `--bg` composes an agent-def per 931c or a generic agent handed the contract prose. Relates [[id:931c]], id:d03d, routed:e2d6/id:75b3, routed:d6be, [[relay-substrates]]. <!-- id:09a8 -->
- [ ] **Integrate Plan-agent backlog-tackling into the relay loop instead of per-round re-discovery?** — user 2026-07-23: observed ANOTHER loderite session use a **Plan agent** to tackle its backlog directly (plan → work the list), rather than the relay loop's re-discover→classify→dispatch-per-round cycle. Question to evaluate: could the relay loop (or drain-driver, id:cd7a) dispatch a Plan-agent that ingests the repo's ROADMAP/TODO backlog and produces an ordered work-plan ONCE, then executes down it — replacing or augmenting the per-round classify re-discovery (the biggest per-round cost, cf. id:24ec/id:9d97)? Weigh against: the re-discovery exists to catch cross-round churn + concurrent edits (why classify is per-round); a one-shot plan goes stale. Possibly a HYBRID: plan-once for a bounded drain, re-discover only on churn (sig-cache already gates this, id:c3a6). Relates id:24ec (discovery cost), [[relay-drain-apex-tasklist-decision]] (id:2b23 apex-driver drain + TaskList projection), id:cd7a (drain-driver). Likely `[HARD — meeting]` (design fork: replace vs augment vs hybrid). <!-- id:60b8 -->
- [ ] **Relay executor / worktree-reap leaks orphaned dev-server processes (`vite preview` etc.) — kill spawned servers on reap** — OBSERVED 2026-07-23: a loderite executor (worktree `~/.cache/relay/worktrees/loderite/exec-7453`) started `vite preview --port 4199` and never tore it down; the worktree was later reaped (de-registered) but the node process leaked and ran 2h47m+ orphaned (no owning session, no claim, port 4199 held). An executor that spawns a long-lived server (dev/preview/e2e host) for a test must guarantee teardown, and worktree-reap (`worktree-retire.sh` / id:3ac8 clean-reap / id:373e force-free cleanup) should kill any child processes rooted in the worktree path before removing it. DISTINCT from the git-lock-hygiene umbrella id:d2cd (that is `.lock`/index locks, not orphaned child PIDs). Directions: (a) executor contract rule — a spawned server MUST be backgrounded under a process-group the executor kills on exit (trap); (b) reap-time sweep — `pgrep -f <worktree-path>` → kill before `git worktree remove`; (c) a periodic orphan-process reaper (pairs with the outage watchdog id:98f0). Observe-first: FIRST logged instance, but the leak is silent + accumulates (port exhaustion, RAM). Relates id:3ac8, id:373e, id:d2cd, [[oom-local-model-session-kills]]. <!-- id:e8a0 -->
- [ ] [HARD — meeting] **Mechanize the wave-based parallel-execute-with-inter-wave-review orchestration into the relay loop / `--drain`** — user 2026-07-23 dispatched (by hand, via the apex turn) a "spawn parallel `/relay execute` for the ROADMAP items, as parallel as sensible re DEPENDENCY-CHAIN + MERGE-CONFLICT risk, run `/relay review` after every wave before the next, and once at the end" orchestration. Compare/integrate that PATTERN into the relay loop or drain-driver (id:cd7a) so it is a first-class capability, not a hand-driven apex prompt each time. Concretely: run `relay/scripts/archive-closed.sh --dry-run` across repos and eyeball it; nothing else blocks this item. — **⚠ THE 2026-08-26 VERDICT RECORDED ABOVE IS REFUTED. Read this before acting on any of it.** The claim *"the twin-safety rule that makes it safe is the same rule that makes it ineffective"* — and the "113 closed / 18 qualified / 16%" figure it rested on — was a **MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT of my own making**, not a property of the tool. A categorisation of every top-level `[x]` item across all 6 repos × 3 ledgers found the twin-open protection fired **ZERO times**, no-id items are archivable by design, heading rules held back nothing, and there are **zero nested `[x]` checkboxes fleet-wide** so no container case exists. Every genuine closed item qualified: a **100% qualification rate**. loderite's 113 were **110 already-archived STUBS + 3 genuine items**, and all 3 were archived. **PART (2) IS THEREFORE CLOSED AS REFUTED — there is nothing to relax.** Both candidate relaxations were examined and rejected on their merits, not merely for lack of instances: *"archive when the twin is closed OR the twin's own line is itself archivable"* is **vacuous by construction** (the guard fires only when the twin is an OPEN bullet, and an open bullet is never archivable, so the added disjunct is unsatisfiable exactly when it could apply); and archiving an open parent with all-closed children would assert a done-ness the ledger does not record — that is `children:` closure (`id:46f6`) and an owner ticking decision, not an archiving one. **WHAT THE INVESTIGATION FOUND INSTEAD — a real defect, now fixed in `cba2e778`:** `archive-closed.sh:77` was a divergent copy of `roadmap-archive.sh:111` that DROPPED the `.*` between the id marker and the stub suffix, the exact character the sibling documents as load-bearing (cartulary 2026-08-14, `routed:4a12`). Any stub with prose after its marker read as un-stubbed and was **re-archived every run, unboundedly**. My own real run duplicated ids in `ROADMAP.archive.md` 3→8 here and 1→16 in loderite — ~24 stubs, ~62 KB. Reverted and re-run corrected (306 items vs 329; the ~23 delta was pure spurious re-archiving). **PART (1) IS RE-SCOPED TO `REVIEW_ME` ONLY.** Measured relief by ledger: **REVIEW_ME 30.3–91.0%**; TODO 2.7–56.1%; **ROADMAP −0.5% to +3.0% — NET-NEGATIVE for two repos** (mathematical-writing −0.2%, yinyang-puzzle −0.5%), because the `id:cd9c` stub reproduces the header line verbatim, so for a single-line item the stub is LONGER than what it replaced. **ROADMAP.md structurally cannot shrink via archiving** — do not re-derive this. And the bloat this item was opened for is not archivable at all: dotclaude-skills' `TODO.md` is **96.8% OPEN items** (1,092,275 of 1,128,256 bytes across 612 of them), loderite's is 90.8% — so `id:35b7`'s prompt-size trap is **not an archiving problem** and no wiring here will fix it. **Open residue:** the id-less stub case (1 live instance, yinyang-puzzle `arc_etch`) is re-archived every run by BOTH scripts because `STUB_LINE_RE` requires an id marker; fixing it needs a coordinated grammar change across both scripts on a surface with an open owner decision (`id:2ab3`) — flagged, deliberately not touched. <!-- id:046a -->

- [ ] **`relay-events.jsonl` `ts` is NOT an event timestamp — it is a stale round-state snapshot** (observed 2026-07-10 while watching a live pool). `relay-loop.js:58` stamps every event with `state.ts`, the most recent **bash-produced** state timestamp, because the Workflow runtime forbids `Date.now()`/`new Date()` (noted at `relay-loop.js:53`). Consequences: (a) all events emitted within a round share one `ts`; (b) an `integrate` can carry an *earlier* `ts` than a `dispatch` that happened before it; (c) observed in the wild, two `integrate` lines in the same run disagreed on clock — one read `ts=12:43:00Z` beside `ckpt=relay-ckpt-…-1243` (local time, mislabelled `Z`), the other `ts=10:52:06Z` beside `ckpt=…-1251` (true UTC). Net: **event ordering and elapsed-time cannot be derived from `ts`**, and any future `--since` filter, burn-rate attribution, or forensic replay built on it is unsound. Fix options: mint the stamp in the shell producer that actually emits each event (`relay-state-write.sh event-append` already runs bash — stamp there, `date -u`, one clock), or add a monotonic `seq` counter per run and order by that. Audit every ISO stamp under `relay/scripts/` for `date -u` vs local-`date`+`Z` mislabelling while in there. Motivating incident: a monitoring predicate keyed on the event log matched six-day-old events; see the consumer's case notes. <!-- id:d484 -->

- [ ] **An injected unit consumed by `inject.sh take` but never dispatched is INVISIBLE** (observed 2026-07-10). `inject.sh add` mints a token and `take` consumes it in the discovery prelude, but **no event of any `kind` is written for either** (`grep -c '"kind":"inject' relay-events.jsonl` → 0, ever). So the only evidence that an injection was consumed is the token's *disappearance* from `inject.sh peek` — an absence, not a record. If the pool takes a unit and then drops it (verdict mis-mapped, filtered by an exclude/blocked path, lost across a round boundary), there is **no way to distinguish "consumed and dispatched" from "consumed and lost"**, and the user's work silently evaporates. Emit `{"kind":"inject-take","token":…,"repo":…,"verdict":…}` at consume time and carry the token onto the resulting `dispatch`/`integrate`/`handback` events so an injection is traceable end-to-end. Pairs with id:d484 — both are gaps in the relay's own observability, and both were found by a consumer trying to *watch* a pool rather than run one. <!-- id:f3a0 -->

- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **Continuous (streaming) dispatch — refill freed slots immediately instead of waiting for the whole wave's last straggler** (user 2026-06-30, "still not happy") — the self-feeding loop is **round-barriered**: `relay-loop.js` dispatches a wave of ≤`POOL_WIDTH` children, **awaits ALL of them** (a `parallel()`-style barrier), integrates, THEN re-discovers and dispatches the next wave. So one slow child idles the other 4 slots until it finishes — the pool drains to near-zero between waves instead of staying saturated. **Want:** as each child completes (and its integration drains), immediately pull the next-highest-priority unit and dispatch it, keeping ~`POOL_WIDTH` units in flight continuously — the Workflow `pipeline()` no-barrier-between-stages model rather than `parallel()` per wave. **Why it's non-trivial (design judgment → meeting):** (1) the **serialized integrator** must stay sequential (one push per repo per turn, D5/D6) — a streaming dispatcher needs a single integrator-consumer draining a completion queue, not N concurrent merges; (2) the **D3 anti-gaming verdict-class order** (execute→review→hard→handoff: unaudited work reviewed before fresh strong work) must still hold when *refilling* — can't stream a handoff for a repo whose review is still pending; (3) **per-repo lease** (id:0902) means never two in-flight units for the same repo — the refill picker must skip repos with a live child; (4) the round-boundary **stop/quota/two-dry-discovery checks** (and the STOP sentinel) must be re-expressed as streaming conditions (ties to id:0ee6 inotify wake + id:c3a6 sig-cache for cheap incremental re-discovery); (5) **fairness/starvation** — a steady stream of high-priority units shouldn't starve a low-priority repo forever. Likely a `[HARD — meeting]` to pick the scheduler shape (continuous picker + bounded in-flight set + single integrator drain), then a `[HARD — pool]` build. Payoff: no more 4-idle-slots-waiting-on-1-straggler; wall-clock tracks the *sum* of work over `POOL_WIDTH`, not the *slowest child per wave* × rounds. **MEETING 2026-06-30-1523 (id:4d8e) decided the SHAPE:** `relay-loop.js` is a Workflow script (sandbox — NO `require`/`import`), so npm job-queue libs (p-queue/bullmq/piscina) are RULED OUT; reuse the harness's own **`pipeline()`** (no-barrier) + the existing per-repo `integrationChains` Map (`:1719`, serialized integrator) — switch the dispatch wave from `parallel()` (`:1685` barrier). Each macro-iteration: cheap mechanical re-discovery (id:4d8e classifier) of all ready units → sort by D3 priority-class rank → feed `pipeline()`. Invariants fall out of existing machinery (serialized integrator = chains; per-repo lease = id:0902; D3 = pre-sort; stop/quota/two-dry = macro-boundary checks); **fairness/starvation is the only genuinely new design.** True mid-flight refill (raw Promise.race picker) = thin follow-on, gated on measurement showing the macro-boundary still idles slots.
