- [ ] **`inotifywait` (or similar) to make the empty-discovery round unnecessary** (user 2026-06-30) — the self-feeding pool loop ends on (among other conditions) **two consecutive empty discoveries** = it re-shards/re-classifies every own repo a final time just to confirm "nothing new", which is wasted classifier work (and on a `/loop` cadence, repeated every tick over a drained backlog). **Idea:** watch the inputs that a discovery actually reads — the own-repos' ledger files (`ROADMAP.md`/`TODO.md`/`REVIEW_ME.md`), the relevant git refs/`HEAD`, `inject.sh` queue, the shared inbox — with `inotifywait` (Linux; `fswatch` as the portable fallback) so the loop **blocks until something a discovery cares about actually changes**, instead of spinning a confirm-empty round. Turns the drained-pool tail from "poll N repos to find nothing" into "sleep until a real edit/commit/inject arrives". Ties to the **discovery signature cache** (id:c3a6, `discover-sig.sh` already hashes the superset of discovery inputs) — the inotify watch-set should be derived from the SAME input set the sig hashes, so the two can't disagree (a change that flips the sig must wake the watcher, and vice-versa). (NB: unrelated to "inflownistration" — that is a project-domain term, see glossary id:2a3d, not a watcher concept.) Design Qs: which exact paths to watch per repo (reuse the sig's input list), debounce coalescing, how it composes with the existing two-dry-discovery exit (replace it, or gate it), and whether it belongs in `relay-loop.js` (in-session) vs the outage-watchdog/`/loop` layer. Note the [[babysitter-durable-cron-no-op]] constraint: an in-session inotify wait dies with the session — it optimizes a *live* loop's idle tail, it is not an outage-survival mechanism (that's id:98f0). Likely `[HARD — meeting]`. **MEETING 2026-06-30-1523 (id:4d8e) decided + DE-PRIORITIZED:** inotify REPLACES the sleep-poll, NOT the two-dry exit (which stays the correctness condition); watch-set derives from `discover-sig.sh`'s input superset + the b444 decision-queue watchfile (id:de31/b444); fail-safe toward re-checking (overflow/doubt → poll). **GATED behind the classifier (id:4d8e) and de-prioritized — DP1 going mechanical already delivered the headline payoff (dry re-discovery is now near-zero-token bash).** Per user note: `git status` incl. worktree heads is the dominant change signal (already hashed by discover-sig), so it works with or without inotify — inotify is optional polish. Decide if the inotifywait dep is worth it only AFTER the classifier lands. <!-- id:0ee6 -->
- [ ] **Batch-review identical mechanical fan-out commits instead of one strong-turn review per repo** (flagged 2026-06-30 `/relay --afk`) — when one logical change cascades the SAME mechanical diff across N sibling repos, the classifier emits an independent `review` unit per repo and the pool spends one Opus review-child apiece on near-identical diffs. Observed: the Option B ledger migration (`docs(todo): promote to own ledger (Option B, zkm f98d)`) landed one byte-similar commit in 10 zkm-* plugins, each becoming its own `review` verdict (their first audit since the migration was done in-session "no live relay pool"). Same shape recurs on **zkm-version-cascade `uv.lock` bumps** (a parent bump rewrites every plugin's lockfile — see CLAUDE.md versioning). Real spend, low marginal risk: ten reviews of essentially one change. **Idea:** detect a fan-out cohort — commits since last ckpt across multiple repos sharing a near-identical diff / subject / `id:`/`routed:` token — and verify the cohort in ONE pass (review the canonical diff once, confirm each repo's instance matches, checkpoint all), instead of fanning out a review-child per repo. Must stay anti-gaming-safe: still audits every commit (D3), just amortizes the judgment over the cohort rather than re-deriving it N times. Open design Qs: how to recognize "same mechanical diff" robustly (token match? normalized-diff hash? subject prefix?), and where it slots (classifier cohort-grouping vs a review-child that takes a repo-list). Likely `[HARD — meeting]` once scoped. <!-- id:ded2 -->
- [ ] **Review re-derivation must verify conjunctive done-claims per-conjunct, and must NOT accept "tests green" as evidence for an un-encoded clause** (caught 2026-06-30 `/relay review zkm`; case study `chidiai/docs/cases/2026-06-30-done-claim-tests-green-untested-clause.md`). A reverse-handoff executor marked zkm ROADMAP `id:f1d7` ("unify `build_index` TOCTOU guard **+ surface dropped files**") `[x]`/"608 green" while the "surface dropped files" clause was implemented on only **1 of 2** code paths (incremental logged; full-rebuild dropped silently) and **no test encoded it**. The merge subject even hedged "**incremental** … log surface" yet ticked the whole item. The false `[x]` survived one full review cycle + sat as `ROADMAP[x]/TODO[ ]` cross-ledger drift before the next review caught it. **Two process gaps in `references/review.md` step "re-derive roadmap":** (1) a ROADMAP `[x]` whose acceptance text is **conjunctive** (`+` / "and" / "both" / a comma-list of deliverables) must be re-derived **per conjunct** against the diff — verifying the salient/tested conjunct and inferring the rest is the partial-truth trap in completion form; (2) "the suite passes" is **proxy evidence**, never proof of a clause **no test covers** — when a conjunct (esp. a "surface it / don't silently drop / no silent caps" requirement, which adds no happy-path behaviour) has no encoding test, the reviewer must either grep the diff to confirm it landed on **every** relevant path or DEMOTE the item to not-done. **Build surface:** (a) tighten the review reference's re-derivation checklist with the per-conjunct + untested-clause rules; (b) optional `roadmap-lint.sh`/doctor heuristic — flag a freshly-`[x]` item whose acceptance text is conjunctive AND whose touched files added no test, as a review-must-re-derive candidate (folds into id:09a3 grammar-lint / id:0907 doctor); (c) reinforce "separate the *promote* from the *verify*" — a reverse-handoff that promotes AND self-verifies in one pass is its own reviewer (the structural setup for the unverified `[x]`). Relates to the D3 anti-gaming invariant the relay already encodes. <!-- id:369c -->
- [ ] **Uniform scope-arg grammar across `/relay` sub-modes — `--all` | `<repo-list>` | current-only** (user directive 2026-06-23, hit during `/relay human --all`) — `/relay human --all` passed `--all` straight to `gather-human-backlog.sh`, which treated it as a **repo name** and printed `--all path not found (/home/tobias/src/--all) … skipped` then silently scoped to nothing; the no-arg form is what actually means "all own repos". The SKILL.md front-door advertises `--all` for human/review but the underlying collector doesn't parse it. **Directive:** every `/relay` sub-mode (`human`/`review`/`handoff`/`reconcile`/`next`) should accept a consistent scope grammar — **`--all` = all confirmed own repos, an explicit `<repo-list>` = those repos, otherwise imply current-repo-only** (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the review-default-flip convention) — **EXCEPT bare `/relay` (the autonomous loop/pool), which implies `--all` by design.** A bare `--all` token must NEVER be silently consumed as a repo path; an unrecognized scope token is a LOUD reject (id:415b grammar rule), not a silent empty scope. Fix surface: teach `gather-human-backlog.sh` (and the per-mode arg parsing in SKILL.md + the helper scripts) to recognize `--all`/`--current`/repo-list uniformly; add a test that `--all` scopes to all own repos and that bare `<repo>` / no-arg behave per the grammar. Natural fold into the relay-health/grammar work (id:09a3 lint, id:0907 doctor). <!-- id:a02c -->

- [ ] **Doctrine: direct-to-main hotfixes in relay-managed repos must leave an audit record** — gap surfaced 2026-06-29 (zkm, index TOCTOU crash). A main session fixed a live production blocker directly (zkm commit `6dc0132`, filed retroactively as zkm TODO id:f1d7) instead of going through executor→review; the fix was correct but landed *unaudited* and made review-worthy judgement calls (silent-skip vs log; sibling TOCTOU left unfixed) unilaterally. **Rule to encode:** bypassing the executor→review round for an active blocker is fine; bypassing the *record* is not — in the SAME push, file a REVIEW-flagged ledger item recording the commit, why review was skipped, and any unilateral judgement calls, so the next review pass verifies it. **Two-surface fix (per the where-analysis this session):** (1) **canonical doctrine** → add a short `## Direct-to-main hotfixes` section to `relay/references/executor-contract.md` (single source `/relay executor` loads + reviewers cite); (2) **reach the skill-less session** (the actual failure mode is a quick-fix session that NEVER loaded `/relay executor`) → one **self-gating** line in global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` Design heuristics: "Relay-managed repos (ROADMAP.md + RELAY_LOG.md present): a direct fix without loading /relay executor is OK for an active blocker, but file a REVIEW-flagged ledger item in the same push." **Rejected:** editing each relay repo's `## Relay contract` CLAUDE.md pointer — ~10 repos + a `v5→v6` stamp bump for one line; global+canonical gets the same reach for two edits, no stamp churn. **Open judgement call** (why this is filed, not self-applied): confirm the self-gating global line is worth the per-prompt ctx cost in EVERY non-relay project (the user's own "per-prompt ctx multipliers" heuristic) vs. accepting that only skill-loading sessions get the rule. Small enough for a task, but the global-CLAUDE.md cost-tradeoff is the one bit warranting a second opinion. <!-- id:7c41 -->
- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] ** Inter-session communication / coordination channel — let concurrent sessions notify each other about collisions** — user 2026-06-23, prompted by the observed `meeting-pool-claim-asymmetry-incident` (a loop pool held a trAIdBTC `review` claim + worktree while a parallel `/meeting` + manual `/relay review & handoff` edited the SAME repo's main-checkout ledgers; the collision was only caught because the *human* noticed and manually told the other session). **The gap:** today's coordination primitives are all PASSIVE/one-sided — `claim.sh` leases (id:0902/ebfb) record who holds a repo but only the relay pool acquires/honors them (a `/meeting` or manual main-checkout edit takes no claim, so the lease is asymmetric — see the incident memory); `RELAY_STATUS.md`/`relay-events.jsonl` are write-only logs nobody is *notified* from; the `/meeting`-hold consumer + `.meeting-deferred-writeback.json` (id:2c42) only defer, they don't *talk back*. There is no ACTIVE channel by which session A ("I'm about to review trAIdBTC") learns session B is mid-`/meeting` on it, or by which a human-initiated session announces intent to a running pool. **Discuss (→ /meeting):** (a) what's the right channel — a shared advisory claim that BOTH `/meeting`/manual relay AND the pool acquire+honor (closes the one-sided-lease asymmetry; cheapest, composes with existing claim.sh), a notify/inbox file sessions poll, a `PushNotification`/desktop-notify on contended-claim, or a richer message bus; (b) push vs pull (does the pool poll for "another session wants this repo", or does the claimant signal interrupt?); (c) what's actually worth communicating — repo-level intent, item-level (`id:`), "I'm about to push", "please yield"; (d) granularity vs noise (don't rebuild a chat system for a rare event); (e) human-in-the-loop — is the human the channel (as today, works but manual) acceptable until frequency justifies automation. **Observe-first (user's standing heuristic):** the claim-asymmetry incident is the FIRST logged instance — gate any build on ≥2–3 recurrences; this item is the DISCUSSION placeholder, not a build mandate. Relates [[relay-dispatch-safety-cluster]] (task-claim primitive + /meeting-hold), [[relay-local-parallelism-d2]] (id:c144 exempts /meeting ledger writes from the HARD lease — but exemption ≠ an advisory claim the pool honors; this is the missing half), id:0902 (lease), id:2c42 (deferred write-back), id:c012 (`/relay stop` — one concrete message a channel would carry), id:98f0/e149 (watchdog heartbeat — a related shared-state signal). **UPDATE 2026-06-23 (incident resolved):** the collision resolved with NO data loss — the pool's `execute` child detected the dirty main checkout and HANDED BACK (**id:aa93** dirty-main-checkout guard), refusing to clobber the `/meeting` edits; review still wasted work on a stale base. **Reframes urgency:** data-safety is ALREADY handled by id:aa93, so a coordination channel is about avoiding *wasted stale-base work* + surfacing intent (and saving the human from being the manual relay), NOT preventing corruption — a lower-priority bar. Strengthens observe-first: the backstop held. **SECOND INSTANCE 2026-06-23 (truncocraft — crosses the ≥2-recurrence gate → now build-warranted, not just a placeholder):** parallel `/meeting` saw octahedron.ts/chunkmesh.ts dirty in main; the WIP DIVERGED from the pool execute child's *committed* worktree branch (two different octant-mesher rewrites) and the child's process had DIED while its claim still read LIVE (fresh mtime + worktree-commits = id:7570 heuristic; claim.sh can't see a dead pid). Worse class — id:aa93 does NOT cover it (already committed to its branch) — resolved cleanly only by integrator timing. **Lease-not-exclude lesson (user course-correction):** to reserve truncocraft for a dedicated session, first reached for a `relay.toml` `excluded` edit; user "can't you just use the flock mechanism?" → used a `claim.sh` lease (`relay-reserve-da09-octant`) instead (non-destructive, avoids the id:d530 anti-pattern). Confirms the lease is the right substrate; the build = make `/meeting` + manual relay ACQUIRE+HONOR the same advisory claim + a contended-claim notify, AND solve the ~30-min-TTL durable-reservation gap. See truncocraft TODO id:da09; full detail in the incident memory. — **DECIDED 2026-07-11 (meeting 2026-07-11-1239, amendment A1):** build the bilateral honored-claim — the non-holder DEFERS its ledger write via the id:2c42 drop-file (replay on release); forbid raw-`Edit` ledger writes (flock'd `md-merge` only); symmetric meeting↔pool. **INTERIM GUARD (partial-supersession, corrected 2026-07-11):** id:5a39 (meeting-as-relay-producer) dissolves only the **`/meeting`-vs-pool ledger-write slice** of this item — it does NOT cover the broader coordination scope (manual `/relay review`-vs-pool collision, contended-claim notify, the ~30-min durable-reservation gap), which survives 5a39. So evaluate 5a39 before building the *meeting-ledger-write* enforcement, but 9000 is NOT fully gated on / superseded by 5a39 — its manual-relay + notify halves stand on their own (dissolve-before-guard applies only to the overlapping slice). <!-- id:9000 -->
- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] ** Item-level claim marker at pick-time (pre-worktree-branching) so concurrent sessions/agents don't double-pick the same TODO/ROADMAP `id:`** — user 2026-07-07, prompted by this session dispatching 4 background executors each on a specific `id:` (6f61/b67e/3558/c79e + b3ee): double-pick was avoided ONLY because the foreground held a *repo-level* meeting claim (`claim.sh acquire dotclaude-skills --mode meeting`), which is coarse — it blocks the whole repo for the duration. Now that id:3558 (worktree-per-session, SHIPPED 2026-07-07) makes per-item worktree branching cheap, finer-grained parallelism (N agents on N distinct items in the SAME repo) is attractive — but there is no ITEM-granularity reservation, so two sessions can branch worktrees for the same `id:` and duplicate the work (both 6f61/b67e turned out already-shipped for a *different* reason, but the double-pick hazard is real for genuinely-open items). **Proposal to discuss (→ /meeting):** extend `claim.sh` from repo-level to item-level — a session/agent acquires a claim keyed on `<repo>:<id>` BEFORE branching its worktree; peers `peek` and skip claimed ids. **Design axes:** (a) claim *substrate* — a `claim.sh` item-scoped registry entry (mtime+TTL, no ledger write — cheapest, composes with the existing primitive) vs a visible `<!-- claiming:runid -->` marker written onto the TODO/ROADMAP line (self-documenting but adds shared-ledger write contention, the very thing id:c144/148b/3558 fight); (b) liveness — reuse the id:e149 heartbeat + id:7570 dead-pid heuristic so a dead picker's item-claim auto-releases (don't strand an id like the truncocraft dead-child-live-claim incident); (c) granularity/noise — worth it only if intra-repo parallelism (id:ca87) is actually pursued; a repo-level claim is simpler when one session owns the repo. **This is the "(c) item-level" branch of the id:9000 coordination discussion made concrete** — fold into that meeting rather than deciding standalone. Relates id:9000 (coordination umbrella), id:3558 (worktree-per-session, shipped), id:ca87 (intra-repo parallelism), [[relay-dispatch-safety-cluster]] (task-claim primitive), id:9000's e149/7570 liveness refs. Observe-first: no double-pick has actually cost work yet (repo-claim has sufficed) — gate any build on intra-repo parallelism becoming real. <!-- id:5ac9 -->
- [ ] **Guard the relay dirty-check against build-artifact false-positives** — `discover-repos.sh:78` flags a repo `dirty=yes` on ANY `git status --porcelain` line, so the pool skips it from review/execute. 2026-06-18 false-positive: yinyang-puzzle (Tesserene, income) was skipped for review across two runs because its vendored submodules carried only build artifacts — tracked `.pyc` in `vendor/einstein_hat/.../__pycache__/` + an untracked `vendor/spectre_py/__pycache__/`, no real source edits. Had to hand-clean the artifacts to unblock it, then hand-inject the review (id:354f). Fix the guard so generated noise doesn't block dispatch: candidates — `git status --porcelain --ignore-submodules=dirty` (or `=untracked`) on the dirty probe, AND/OR treat lines matching pure-artifact patterns (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, …) as non-blocking, AND/OR a soft `dirty-artifacts-only` state that surfaces in RELAY_STATUS but still dispatches. Decide where the line sits (a genuinely dirty *source* tree must still block — D5 worktree safety). Keep it conservative: under-skip (dispatching a real-dirty repo) is worse than over-skip. <!-- id:6366 -->
- [ ] **Make relay.toml `income` non-binary** — today `income = true/false` is a single boolean used only for slot-contention tiebreaking. Richen it so income-relevant repos can be ranked/scheduled by more than a flag: e.g. estimated success **chance**, expected **value**, and **timeline/deadline** (a repo shipping for a fixed date should outrank an open-ended one), or a small set of **tags**. Decide the schema (structured sub-table vs tags), how the scheduler consumes it (weighting within the income class), and keep it back-compatible with the existing boolean. Motivating case: yinyang-puzzle (Tesserene wood puzzle) + puzzle-pwa both flagged income with a hard Christmas-2026 ship goal — a boolean can't express "funded, deadline-driven, high-value" vs "someday-maybe income". <!-- id:1ffc -->

- [ ] **Cross-repo routed action items never land in the target repo's tracking — `/meeting`'s "→ routed to <repo> inbox" is a dead letter** — observed 2026-06-18: toesnail's `/meeting` `docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-18-0729-veq-macro-verify-carrier.md` action item `routed:8587` ("→ routed to `mathematical-writing` inbox: design the `.mw` side of the carrier", fulfilling the earlier `routed:e4df` park) was written ONLY in the toesnail meeting note. **`.mw` had no `8587`/`e4df`/`veq`/`carrier` reference ANYWHERE** (TODO/ROADMAP/REVIEW_ME), and `.mw` has no `inbox` file at all — so the routed item was a dead letter for the gap between the meeting (2026-06-18) and a human noticing it. The `/meeting` skill writes the `routed:<id>` token into the SOURCE repo's note but has no mechanism to (a) create the item in the TARGET repo's ROADMAP/TODO, nor (b) surface "you have N inbound routed items pending ingestion" when the target repo is next worked. Same risk for every `routed:<id>` / `ref:<id>` cross-repo handoff (cf. `dotclaude-skills/TODO.md` already uses `ref:aae4` as a manual guard — that pattern is the workaround, not a fix). **Fix directions:** (1) `/meeting` (and `/relay`), when emitting a `routed:<id>` to another repo, should ALSO append a stub `- [ ] [INBOUND — routed:<id> from <repo>/<note>] <title>` into the target repo's TODO.md (flock'd `md-merge.py`), so the item exists in the target's tracking immediately; OR (2) a cross-repo "inbound routed" scanner (a `scripts/scan-routed.sh` greppable over all `own` repos' meeting-notes for `routed:<id>` whose target repo lacks a matching `id:`/`routed:` line) wired into `/relay` discovery / `/projects` dashboard so dead letters surface. (3) At minimum document the manual ingestion step in `/meeting`'s SKILL.md so the router doesn't assume "routed" = "tracked". This near-miss cost a full design item (`.mw` id:358f) sitting untracked; only caught because the owner manually asked "what about .mw's ROADMAP?". Relates to id:0a1e (auto-surface prior decisions on a known id) — both are "the ledger doesn't know about a decision recorded elsewhere". **LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-06-25 (this item is no longer hypothetical):** while shipping id:2dea (the repo-LOCAL un-promoted-backlog scan), a sweep of the shared inbox found a large stranded backlog — for **this repo alone, 12 open inbound `routed:` items target it yet NONE appear in its TODO/ROADMAP** (dead letters), and ~12 inbox lines are bare prose carrying **no `routed:` token at all**, so `append.sh inbox-done` can never resolve them and no scanner can correlate them (the same id-less blind spot id:2dea's `untracked` disposition closes repo-locally). id:2dea is the repo-LOCAL sibling (open TODO with no ROADMAP twin); **this (id:3947) is the cross-repo / inbox layer** — deliberately out of relay's repo-confirmed scope today (the inbox is "surface-only at `/meeting` step 7b + `/projects`", id:b30b), so do NOT just bolt the inbox onto `unpromoted-scan.sh` (it would couple this PUBLIC repo to the local-only `~/.claude/todo-inbox.md` and cross that boundary). Fix belongs at the `/meeting`+`/projects` layer per the proposals above; the `scan-routed.sh` (proposal 2) **must also flag inbox entries lacking a `routed:` token** (the rot found here), not only target-repo-missing twins. Cousin id:69f4 (cross-project mirrored-id sync). <!-- id:3947 -->
- [ ] **`loop-hint.sh` swallows the `--afk` nudge after a recent prior run (time-gap heuristic too aggressive)** — observed 2026-06-18: a manual `/relay . .mw --afk all \veq and related` printed NOTHING from `loop-hint.sh` (step 0a), so the "wrap this in `/loop` for unattended resilience" tip — the single most useful hint for someone who *just typed `--afk`* (= "I'm walking away") — was suppressed. Root cause: `loop-hint.sh` decides standalone-vs-loop-tick PURELY by time since the last run (`$STAMP` ≤ `GAP`=2700s → assume loop tick → silent). A manual re-invocation within 45 min of any prior `/relay` (very common during an interactive session) trips the suppression even though `--afk` is an EXPLICIT away-signal that should make the nudge fire. The script never even sees argv — the front door calls it with no args. **Fix direction:** pass the invocation's flags into `loop-hint.sh` (or set an env marker) so an explicit `--afk`/`--allow-intensive` **forces** the tip regardless of the time gap. **Nuance (the hard part, already noted in the script header):** a `/loop 20m /relay --afk` would then re-nag every tick, because a manual `--afk` and a loop-driven `--afk` are otherwise indistinguishable (the built-in `/loop` sets nothing observable). So the real fix needs a reliable in-`/loop` marker (env var the loop runner sets, or a sentinel the front door can detect) to separate "manual --afk" (print) from "loop tick of --afk" (suppress). Until that exists, weigh: (a) force-print on `--afk` and accept re-nag on afk-loops (the script already self-suppresses on plain `/relay` loop ticks, so only afk-loops re-nag), vs (b) shorten/condition `GAP` only when `--afk` is present. Low-severity (cosmetic — the nudge is advisory) but it defeats the entire purpose of the 2026-06-18 "surface it FIRST" directive. See `relay/scripts/loop-hint.sh` + SKILL.md step 0a. <!-- id:888a -->
- [ ] [HARD] **Gate-resolution detection: externally-resolving gates never auto-surface as actionable** — `gather-human-backlog.sh` re-derives gated items by grepping ROADMAP every run (nothing goes stale), and the relay pool's `discover-sig.sh` re-classifies on signature change — but there is NO active "external gate now satisfied → surface as actionable" detection. Gates that resolve *outside* the repo change nothing in-repo, so they keep re-emitting as "needs a /meeting" until a human notices: chidiai id:1e77 (≥50 outcome rows accumulate), proton-moresync id:5cc5 (first external user), zomni id:7cf2 (an OOM-kill / PSI-full stall fires), ai-codebench id:efc2 (the 244b GPU matrix run finishes). **Fix directions**: a per-item machine-checkable gate predicate the collector/discovery evaluates (flips gated_hard→actionable when met), or a periodic gate-recheck pass. - [ ] **`/loop /relay` re-fires blindly — no feedback from relay's exit reason (quota cap / pool drain) to suppress or postpone the next cron tick** — observed 2026-06-18: a `/loop 30m /relay --afk …` cron re-fires `/relay` every 30 min on pure wall-clock, regardless of WHY the prior run ended. Two wasteful cases: (1) **quota stop** — relay already knows the guilty bucket's `resetTime` (`quota-stop.sh` returns per-bucket `resetTime`/`pctRemaining`, surfaced in `RELAY_STATUS.md`), but nothing feeds it back, so ticks keep firing into a capped quota until the window happens to reset; the tick should be **postponed until the guilty bucket's reset** (or be a cheap no-op that re-checks quota and exits fast). (2) **pool drain** (two empty discoveries = backlog drained) — re-discovering every 30 min until new work appears is mostly wasted; the loop should back off (longer cadence) or self-terminate until new commits/items land. The hard part is the channel: the built-in `/loop`/cron fires a fixed prompt and has no hook to read relay's exit state — so this needs either (a) the front door writing a machine-readable "next-useful-at" / "stop-reason" stamp (e.g. into `RELAY_STATUS.md` or a sidecar) that an early step of the next `/relay` run reads to decide "exit immediately, nothing to do until T", or (b) a relay-aware loop wrapper that schedules its own next wake from the stop reason (cf. ScheduleWakeup dynamic mode) instead of a dumb fixed cron. Shares the "no reliable in-`/loop` marker" root cause with id:888a (loop-hint can't tell a manual `--afk` from a loop tick — same missing channel). Needs a small design note before building; low-cost-but-non-obvious. <!-- id:8602 -->

- [ ] **Quota decay only covers the 7-day bucket — no 5h-window (or generalized late-window) use-it-or-lose-it decay** — `RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_7D` interpolates the `seven_day`/`seven_day_sonnet` thresholds START→END against `seven_day.resets_at`, but the **5h bucket has no decay at all** (grep-confirmed 2026-06-18: zero `DECAY_5H`/`FIVE_HOUR` decay in `quota-stop.sh`). User intent (2026-06-18): permitted useup should be **higher late in a window than early** — the last hour of a 5h window / end of a day should allow spending more, since unused quota is lost at reset (back-loaded "0.10:0.70"-style). The existing knob is directional (back-loading already expressible), so the gap is: (1) add `RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_5H` (interpolate the `five_hour` threshold against `five_hour.resets_at`, mirroring the 7d path in `quota-stop.sh` + forward it through `relay-loop.js` envPairs + document in the knob table); (2) optionally generalize to a single per-bucket decay mechanism so any bucket can carry a `START:END`. Note the direction nuance: the current `RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_7D` docs/example front-loads (`0.70:0.10`, tighten late) — the user wants the OPPOSITE for use-it-or-lose-it, so document both directions clearly and pick a sensible default for the afk-loop case. Independent of id:8602 but compounding: a late-window-permissive 5h cap + a quota-aware loop tick is the full "spend the window down then sleep till reset" behavior. <!-- id:1ae7 -->
- [ ] **discover-sig.sh: `upstream` field read without a fetch → origin-behind under-invalidation** — audit id:401c Run 11 (`docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-17-1102-strong-model-audit.md`, finding 3.1a). The sig hashes `HEAD...@{upstream}` WITHOUT fetching, but the shard's SYNC-WITH-ORIGIN guard (id:c3f7) fetches+FF. If origin advances between rounds with the local tracking ref untouched, the sig is byte-identical → cached verdict reused, no fetch/FF until the next sig-moving event. Bounded (single pool run, self-healing) but a genuine under-invalidation — the one hazard class the CLAUDE.md gotcha warns about ("new signal → add to discover-sig.sh's blob"). LOW severity. **Needs a measured decision, not an inline edit** (a fetch-per-sig adds network cost to every discovery round) — weigh fetch-in-sig vs accept-the-bounded-staleness. <!-- id:4348 -->
- [ ] **Profile relative intensity of `[INTENSIVE]` tasks → resource-budget co-scheduling instead of blanket serial-alone** — the `[INTENSIVE — <resource>]` mechanism (id:8d52) treats EVERY intensive unit identically: it runs serially-alone after each round's parallel wave, holding an exclusive `resource:<name>` claim. That binary policy was built around the worst case — the OOM-risk local-LLM benchmarks from ai-codebench ([[oom-local-model-session-kills]]: 6 sessions killed when a 26B model ran). But intensive tasks are NOT uniformly heavy: observed 2026-06-22, a `leAIrn2learn` jax/optax ES task uses **one core and leaves plenty of RAM free**, while ai-codebench local-LLM runs are genuinely memory-heavy. Forcing the light one to run alone wastes the idle cores/RAM — the pool sat on a single task while 18 repos were blocked and resources were free. **Direction:** (1) profile/measure per-task footprint (peak RSS, core count, GPU?) — start with a logger that records actual resource use of each intensive run (observe-before-preventing, cf. design heuristics), keyed by repo/item so the data accrues; (2) replace the binary `resource:<name>` exclusive claim with a **resource BUDGET** (e.g. RAM headroom + core count) so light intensive tasks can co-run with each other and/or the normal parallel wave up to the budget, while a heavy one (GPU / large-model / measured high-RSS) still claims exclusivity. Lets `--afk` actually saturate the box instead of idling on one light task. Tag the relative intensity in the `[INTENSIVE — <resource>]` marker or relay.toml (`intensive = "<resource>"` could gain a weight) so the scheduler reads it rather than guesses. Relates id:8d52 (the serial-alone mechanism this refines), id:da26 (`hard` verdict), [[oom-local-model-session-kills]] (the worst case that must keep exclusivity), and the `--allow-intensive`/`--afk` path. Trigger: 2026-06-22 `/relay --afk` session (user observation: "if enough resources are available the loop shouldn't work only on a single task"). <!-- id:c7b6 -->

- [ ] **Relay discovery: record canonical repo path at confirm-time (deterministic, not default-path-assumed)** — relay.toml assumes each repo lives at `~/src/<name>`, but the 12 zkm-* plugin repos actually live at `~/src/zkm/plugins/zkm-<name>`. With no `# path:` override the discovery LLM agent was NON-DETERMINISTIC: the 2026-06-13 09:38 `-d` run reported them "missing at ~/src/zkm-*" and deferred them; the 09:54 run's agent improvised, found them under `plugins/`, and executed 7 of them. Same prompt, same config, different agent initiative. **Immediate fix applied 2026-06-13:** added explicit `# path: ~/src/zkm/plugins/zkm-<name>` overrides to all 12 plugin blocks in relay.toml. **Durable fix (this item):** when the orchestrator first confirms a repo (handoff/discover), resolve and persist its canonical path via `git -C <candidate> rev-parse --show-toplevel` into the relay.toml block, rather than relying on the `~/src/<name>` default + manual override. Removes the improvisation surface entirely. Also: discover-repos.sh should emit canonical paths, and the discover agent should treat a default-path miss as a hard "surface for path confirmation", never silently improvise OR silently defer. **UPDATE 2026-06-29 (user, during a `/relay handoff&review --all`):** the gap bit again at the *consumer* layer — a strong-turn ad-hoc cheap-scan improvised a `~/src/<name>` sweep and (a) missed the nested `zkm/plugins/zkm-*` repos and (b) hardcoded the `~/src/` layout. Lesson: **the own-repo set + paths must always be derived from `relay.toml` (honoring `# path:`), never from a `~/src/*` glob** — exactly how `gather-human-backlog.sh` / `relay-reconcile.sh --all` already resolve them. Two asks fold in here: (1) any relay-adjacent scan (incl. front-door cheap pre-scans) should resolve repos via a single shared relay.toml path-resolver, not a directory glob; (2) reconsider whether `# path:` should be a **proper TOML field** (`path = "…"`) rather than a comment-override — a comment is invisible to a naive TOML parse and is the thing that made the override "feel" optional. The durable canonical-path persistence above subsumes (2) if it writes a real field. <!-- id:f5d8 -->
- [ ] **Relay write-status agent leaks a literal `${HOME}/` dir into cwd** — the `writeRelayStatus` agent in `relay-loop.js` is told to write to `~/.config/fables-turn/RELAY_STATUS.md` "expand ~ to $HOME", but on the 2026-06-13 `-d` run it created a literal `${HOME}/.config/fables-turn/RELAY_STATUS.md` under the dotclaude-skills repo root (single-quoted `${HOME}` never expanded), polluting the working tree (showed as untracked `${HOME}/`). Same risk for any agent given a `~`/`${HOME}` path while cwd is a repo. Fix: have the write agent resolve `$HOME` itself (or pass an already-expanded absolute path from the script) and assert the target is absolute before writing. Low-severity (cosmetic + dirty-tree noise) but recurs every run whose cwd is a repo. **FIX SHIPPED 2026-06-13 (322ab59):** writeRelayStatus prompt now resolves via `os.path.expanduser`, forbids literal `$HOME`/`${HOME}`/`~` path components, aborts unless resolved path starts with `/`. Verified once (Opus review run wpgjvis34 produced no leak dir). Leave open until a second clean run confirms, then tick. <!-- id:c34a -->
- [ ] **Relay integrator leaves orphan worktrees when a child leaves untracked files** — the serialized integrator's step 5 ran `git worktree remove` (no `--force`), which fails on ANY untracked file in the worktree (e.g. a `uv.lock` a review/execute child generated by running `uv`/tests). Because it's `&&`-chained with `branch -d` and runs after a successful merge+tag+push, the failure silently orphans the worktree AND branch under `~/.cache/fables-turn/worktrees/` (found a helferli review orphan 2026-06-13). **FIX SHIPPED 2026-06-13:** step 5 now uses `worktree remove --force` (safe — the committed branch work is already integrated by that point; --force only discards incidental untracked build artifacts). Verify next multi-review run leaves no orphans, then tick. <!-- id:d187 -->
- [ ] **relay-burn.sh: harden the `report` `date -d "$reset"` awk-shellout against a crafted `resets_at`** — strong-model audit Run 9 (2026-06-16, `docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-16-0928-strong-model-audit.md`, Pass 2) found that `relay-burn.sh report`'s human-table path interpolates the JSONL `reset` field (sourced from `seven_day.resets_at`/`five_hour.resets_at` in `/tmp/claude-usage-cache.json`) directly into a shell command run via awk `getline` (`cmd = "date -d \"" reset "\" +%s …"`). A crafted `resets_at` would be a command-injection seam. **Risk accepted LOW** for now: `resets_at` is provider-controlled API data written by the statusline from `/api/oauth/usage`, and an attacker who can write the cache already has local code execution; the seam is also unexercised by any non-`--json` caller in the relay path. **Fix when convenient:** validate `resets_at` (e.g. `^[0-9T:+\-]+$` guard, or parse the epoch in jq inside `report`'s main jq pass) before any `date -d` shellout. Forward-robustness only. <!-- id:287b -->
- [ ] **Intra-repo parallelism — dispatch >1 unit in the same repo when writes are disjoint** — user 2026-06-15: today the pool parallelizes only ACROSS repos (`POOL_WIDTH` = distinct repos, one unit/repo; the lease `claim.sh` is whole-repo, and the integrator does one `--no-ff` merge + one push per repo per turn). The guardrail already *permits* "within a repo on disjoint paths" but nothing implements it. Motivating use case: **`/relay` scoped to the relay (meta) repo alone, at maximum parallelism** — when dotclaude-skills is the only confirmed repo there's currently nothing to fan out across, so the meta-work serializes. **User's write-disjointness model to validate:** the three relay actors touch shared ledgers in mostly-non-conflicting ways — `REVIEW_ME.md` is *append* by executors, *existing-box edits* by `/relay human`, *read + light tidy* by review; ROADMAP similarly (executors tick `[ROUTINE]` boxes, review re-derives, human/handoff define). So "clearly parallelizable" units (touching disjoint files, or disjoint code paths within one repo) should be safe to run concurrently in the same repo NOW. **Nuance/caveats to design around:** (i) these ledgers are NOT `merge=union` (checkbox `[ ]`↔`[x]` toggles can't union) — concurrent edits still need line-scoped flock'd writes (`meeting/md-merge.py`) and git surfaces residual conflicts (`orphan-scan.sh --cross-ledger`); RELAY_LOG.md *is* union (append-only), so it's the easy case. (ii) integration ordering — N worktrees in one repo all merging to the same branch needs a single-owner serialized merge (the D5/D6 "never two children pushing to the same remote" rule), so the parallelism is in the *work*, not the *push*. (iii) claim granularity must drop from whole-repo to sub-repo (path-set or unit-id) so two same-repo units don't refuse each other's lease. **Phasing:** start with the trivially-disjoint case (units whose file/path sets provably don't intersect — e.g. a doc edit + a test-only change + a script in different dirs), gated by a static path-overlap check; defer less-trivial in-repo parallelism (same-file disjoint hunks, semantic coupling) to a follow-up. **Likely wants a `/meeting`** — non-obvious tradeoffs (worktree-per-unit-within-repo vs single worktree + serialized stages, claim re-granularity, merge ordering, how the discovery classifier emits multiple units per repo and proves their disjointness). Relates to [[parallel-session-state-coordination]] (worktrees scoped to same-repo code edits), id:3558 (worktree-per-session flock'd merge), id:6a3c Axis B (write-contention coupling), and the dispatch-safety cluster. **User comment for the meeting (2026-06-15):** "Why does REVIEW_ME need flock when we're supposedly using worktrees?" — valid challenge: among worktree children flock IS redundant (each child has an isolated working copy; the single-owner serialized merge + git conflict-surfacing handle ordering). The flock'd `md-merge.py` exists for MAIN-CHECKOUT writers that do NOT use a worktree — `/relay human` and `/meeting`/manual edits write REVIEW_ME/ROADMAP/TODO directly in the main checkout, and a live `/meeting` racing a `/relay human` (or the integrator touching main) is a same-directory concurrency hazard. So the rule is: worktree work → serialized merge, NO flock; same-directory work → flock. The earlier framing of this item conflated the two. If intra-repo parallel units ALL ran in their own worktrees, flock is moot for them — which argues for "worktree-per-unit + serialized merge" as the clean design and reserves flock strictly for the non-worktree main-checkout actors. Also: the whole-repo lease is the obvious thing to re-granularize (sub-repo path-set / unit-id leases). <!-- id:ca87 -->
- [ ] [HARD] **Periodic test-integrity sanity-check on a cadence (not just on unaudited commits)** — user 2026-06-16: occasionally a repo should get a dedicated [HARD] sanity check verifying its commits carry red→green justification (test added red → impl change → green), independent of whether there are *new* unaudited commits to review. **Distinct from existing machinery:** `gaming-scan.sh` (mechanical: deleted tests / added skips / removed asserts) and `review.md §2` (resurrection check) only fire inside a `review` unit, i.e. when there ARE unaudited commits since the last ckpt — so a repo that's been quiet (or whose gaming slipped through earlier) is never re-swept. **Likely wants a `/meeting`** (user flagged it). Design qs: (a) cadence — what is "occasionally"? every N reviews / time-since-last-deep-audit (new relay.toml field, distinct from `last_review`) / probabilistic per round / weighted by repo income? (b) scope/depth — re-audit full history, or commits since a `last_deep_audit` marker? how far back? (c) reuse vs new checks — does it re-run gaming-scan §2 over a wider window, or add new checks (each commit pairs a test-change with an impl-change; commit message narrates red→green)? (d) verdict class — a new `audit` verdict or a flavor of `hard`; where it ranks in the scheduler (after review, like `hard`?). (e) anti-gaming the auditor — what's the done-check so the audit itself can't be rubber-stamped. Relates to id:401c (recurring strong-model audit), id:414a (Tier B gaming-canary harness), gaming-scan.sh (id:fa05), review.md §2 (id:dfaf). <!-- id:7b4d -->
- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **Pool busy-loops re-dispatching un-doable HARD units → never drains, burns an Opus child + an inject-take per round** — observed 2026-06-16 (run relay-20260616-063457-22124): after the backlog drained, ~15 repos' only open work is [HARD] items that are decision-gated (need a /meeting: isochrone id:b104, zkm-claude-ai id:107, zkm-photo, meeting-rpg) or too-large/cross-repo (zkm-scan id:02bd, zkm-eml id:ff0f). The `hard` classifier emits a unit for each, an Opus child sizes it and correctly HANDS BACK (C5 "don't half-do it"). **Bug:** `runRound()` returns `actionable: actionable.length` (relay-loop.js:1135) = units *dispatched*, not units that *did work*; a handed-back hard unit still counts as actionable, so `dry` resets to 0 every round (line 1159) and the drain-detector (`dry >= 2`) never fires. The loop re-discovers the SAME gated-hard set every round and spins to the `MAX_ROUNDS=30` seatbelt (or quota), re-spawning an Opus child per gated repo per round to re-derive the identical handback, and running one `inject.sh take` per round in the discovery prelude (id:9ed4) on an empty queue — the "mostly nothing + many inject-take dispatches" symptom. Real work still ships (7 checkpoints that run), but most rounds are pure churn. **Fix options:** (a) count only units that produced a checkpoint (or did NOT hand back) toward `actionable`, so an all-handback round is a dry round; (b) per-run memo: once a repo's top HARD item hands back as gated/too-large, suppress it from re-dispatch for the rest of the run (mark the repo "hard-exhausted this run"); (c) durably mark a decision-gated HARD item (e.g. relay.toml `hard_blocked_until` or a ROADMAP tag) so the classifier skips it until a /meeting clears it — surface in RELAY_STATUS Queued instead. (a)+(b) make the loop drain after ONE pass over the gated-hard set instead of 30; (c) stops re-deriving the gate every run. Likely (a) for the immediate bleed + (c) for the durable fix. **PARTIAL FIX SHIPPED 2026-06-16 (branch relay-observability):** (a) `runRound` now returns `produced` (checkpoints integrated this round) and the outer loop's drain counter keys on `produced===0`, so an all-handback round counts as no-progress → drains after 2 rounds instead of spinning to MAX_ROUNDS=30 (test_relay_loop_structure id:2d20 checks); AND the discovery classifier now applies an EXECUTABLE-HARD test — `[HARD — decision gate]` / under-a-Gated-section / acceptance-needs-/meeting / multi-session items are EXCLUDED from the `hard` verdict + openHard and SURFACED ("HARD backlog is gated — needs /meeting") instead of dispatched, so already-gated repos stop spawning an Opus child per round. **STILL OPEN (durable auto-closure, → meeting id:719e):** option (c) — when a strong child hands back a FRESHLY-discovered `[HARD — strong model]` item as too-large/gated, AUTO-re-tag it to `[HARD — decision gate]` (durable, in the ROADMAP via the integrator's main-checkout write path) so it never gets re-dispatched in a LATER run either. Forks: where the durable mark lives (ROADMAP re-tag vs relay.toml field vs sidecar), how it's invalidated when the item is re-scoped, REPORT-schema field for the child to signal it, and trusting the child's one-shot "too-large" verdict. Until (c) lands, a human (or the /meeting) re-tagging the item to `[HARD — decision gate]` durably stops re-dispatch today via the new classifier exclusion. <!-- id:2d20 -->

Also feeds the statusline runway/backlog work (id:15bd, routed:01ac) and the observability artifacts (id:c8b6). **MUST include the pool's gated-HARD-needs-/meeting list** (the `id:2d20` Blocked entries in RELAY_STATUS) so the human can see what's blocking the pool from one place — pairs with id:f6c9. <!-- id:ec9a -->
- [ ] **Injected unit + same-repo discovery unit in one round → concurrent same-repo units race the integrator → spurious dirty-tree handbacks (wasted strong children)** — observed live 2026-06-16 (run relay-20260616-112222-29307, round 5): an `inject.sh add dotclaude-skills --verdict hard` (id:f6c9) was dispatched in the SAME round dotclaude-skills also had a normally-discovered `review` unit (and an `execute` re-enqueue). All three ran concurrently in separate worktrees; the `hard` child won the integrator, merged + checkpointed (eaf95c6/2571e3f), but its mid-merge writes to the shared MAIN checkout (`~/src/dotclaude-skills`) made the OTHER two units' integration see a dirty tree → both handed back ("Working tree is dirty: relay/references/human.md … Cannot merge"). No corruption (the dirty-tree guard worked), no work lost (they re-dispatch next round) — but two strong/sonnet children were spent for nothing + confusing handback noise. **Root cause (relay-loop.js):** the stated invariant is "pool of distinct repos, one unit per repo" (L71), enforced via the per-repo lease `claim.sh acquire` (L808). BUT (a) the lease is keyed cross-SESSION by runId and `claim.sh acquire` is RE-ENTRANT for the same runId, so two units of the SAME run targeting one repo both acquire it (no sibling-lane serialization); AND (b) the injection merge step (`units.push(injectedUnits)`, ~L617) adds the injected unit WITHOUT deduping against a discovery unit already present for that repo this round. So injection is a backdoor to UNGUARDED intra-repo parallelism — the very thing id:ca87 says needs sub-repo claim granularity + single-owner serialized integration before it's safe. **Fix options:** (a) cheap/correct — dedupe units per repo per round at the merge step: if an injected unit's repo already has a discovery unit this round, either MERGE them into one unit (prefer the injection's verdict/prompt) or DEFER the injection to a later round (honors the one-unit-per-repo invariant; the injection is already consumed from inject.d so it must be re-enqueued, not dropped); (b) make `claim.sh acquire` NON-re-entrant within a run for distinct units (unit-id-keyed sub-lease) so sibling lanes serialize; (c) full id:ca87 intra-repo parallelism (sub-repo path-set leases + serialized single-owner merge) so same-repo units are genuinely safe to run concurrently. (a) is the immediate bleed-stop; (c) is the durable design. Severity moderate (token waste + handback noise, not data loss). Relates to id:ca87 (intra-repo parallelism safety), id:baf1 (injection path), id:ebfb (per-repo lease — note the same-run re-entrancy), id:6e9d (mid-round inject), id:719e (DMAIC: handback rework = waste). <!-- id:0547 -->
- [ ] **Light/incremental handoff for already-onboarded repos — full C1–C5 handoff is overkill** — user 2026-06-16. The `handoff` verdict (discovery classifier) fires when ROADMAP.md is missing OR every item is ticked while untracked new work exists; `references/handoff.md` then runs the full onboarding: C1 docs (CLAUDE.md/README) → C2 roadmap → C3 red tests → C4 BDD → C5 optional HARD. For a repo that's ALREADY onboarded (has CLAUDE.md, a ROADMAP.md with the marker, a test suite + BDD), re-running C1/C4 is redundant re-scaffolding — and handoff children are STRONG-model (Opus), so it's wasted Opus $ (cf. the relay-econ cost lens, id:1a75: ~71% of spend is Opus work). The common onboarded-repo trigger is the "all items ticked + untracked new work" branch — that repo doesn't need docs/BDD rebuilt, it needs the NEW work specced. WANTED: a LIGHT handoff path that detects existing scaffolding (CLAUDE.md present, ROADMAP has the marker, tests/ dir exists) and does only the INCREMENTAL work — qualify+spec the untracked new work as C2 roadmap items + C3 red tests, skip C1 docs and C4 BDD that already exist (verify, don't rewrite). Decide shape: (a) a branch inside handoff.md ("if already onboarded → incremental: C2/C3 for new work only, verify C1/C4 exist"), or (b) a distinct verdict between `handoff` and `execute` (e.g. `respec`). Note this overlaps `review` §5b reverse-handoff (which qualifies+sizes unqualified TODO/ROADMAP additions) — maybe the onboarded-repo "all-ticked + new work" case should route to a review-like reverse-handoff rather than full handoff. Relates to the discovery classifier handoff trigger, review.md §5b, id:1a75 (handoff cost). <!-- id:b14a -->

- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **[HUMAN] Encode "ROUTINE requires the test to gate the REAL goal" in the executor scope guard** — surfaced 2026-06-16 (toesnail /relay human, mirror fidelity id:0e63). The relay's `[ROUTINE]` (Sonnet-safe) vs `[HARD]`/human split implicitly assumes **tests-are-the-spec**; that breaks when part of the success criterion lives OUTSIDE the test (semantic fidelity, faithfulness, meaning, owner judgment). Concrete case: a `.mw` mirror shipped an UNFAITHFUL transcription yet its test was GREEN, because `.mw` keys DAG edges on regex symbol refs — green for faithful AND unfaithful RHS alike. An executor gated on "test passes" would re-ship green-but-wrong work. **Rule to add** to `references/conventions.md` (executor-contract block) and the handoff/review classification step: *before tagging a tooling item `[ROUTINE]`, ask "could this test be GREEN while the actual goal is wrong?" If yes (regex/structural/schema-shape/"it parses"/"it renders" checks guarding a semantic goal) → `[HARD]` + owner/strong re-confirm.* **Tagged [HUMAN] not [ROUTINE] — self-consistently:** this is a CONTRACT change governing ~36 repos with broad behavioral consequence and NO test gating its wording; the owner ratifies it (likely a `/meeting` — overlaps the rigor-bar meeting id:80d7 and the test-integrity sanity-check id:7b4d). Relates to id:80d7, id:7b4d, review.md §2 (anti-gaming). <!-- id:33c2 -->

- [ ] **MEETING-candidate: git-notes flag for un-runnable/sanity-violated commits → `git bisect` auto-skip** — user 2026-06-16 (side-note off toesnail mirror-fidelity thread). Idea: record a per-commit signal in git notes so a `git bisect run` wrapper auto-`125`s (skips) commits that can't be meaningfully tested, and so a stale-test/sanity-violated commit is marked. **Crucial nuance the user raised (the design hinge):** bisect runs the CURRENT/uncommitted test (the bug repro) against OLD source — it preserves untracked working-tree files across checkouts and `git bisect run <script>` lives outside the tree — so a "commit X gamed its OWN committed tests" flag is largely ORTHOGONAL to bisectability (bisect may never run X's tests). The signal that genuinely pays off is **runnability**: "this commit doesn't build / the harness can't execute here" → skip. The sanity-violation flag feeds bisect only insofar as a violation made the commit un-testable. **Substrate already exists:** the verify commit-hook writes ephemeral notes on `refs/notes/verify` (`status:pending findings:…`, toesnail id:8757) and `gaming-scan.sh` (id:fa05) is the mechanical sanity detector — a bisect-skip consumer is a natural extension. **Design qs for the meeting:** (a) carrier — extend `refs/notes/verify` with a `runnable:false`/`bisect_skip:true` field vs a dedicated `refs/notes/bisect-skip` ref (a new field bumps the just-FROZEN verify schema `{status,findings}`+`{triaged,processed,verdict,review_me}` — toesnail /relay human 2026-06-16, so it's a deliberate extension not a free add); (b) who writes it (the post-commit HARD tier? gaming-scan? a separate build-probe?) and when a commit is deemed un-runnable; (c) the `git bisect run` wrapper that reads the note and returns 125; (d) notes are local-only + lossy-on-rebase (toesnail D-decisions) — acceptable for a bisect aid, or does it need durability; (e) cross-repo vs per-repo. Likely ONE `/meeting`. Relates to toesnail verify-hook cluster (id:8757/d5f9/0e63), gaming-scan.sh (id:fa05), review.md §2, id:7b4d (periodic sanity-check), id:80d7 (rigor bar). <!-- id:872e -->

- [ ] **[skeleton L4] unitPrompt guardrail trim: de-duplicate inline rules against the loaded contract** — **EVALUATED 2026-06-18, DEFERRED as low-ROI + high-blast-radius.** `unitPrompt` fires on WORK dispatches (opus review/hard, sonnet execute) whose token cost is dominated by the actual work — the ~40-line skeleton is a negligible fraction, so trimming saves little. AND it touches the UNIVERSAL child contract: inline 'NEVER push/tag/diary' + lease rules apply to ALL verdicts, but review/handoff/hard load review.md/handoff.md (NOT executor-contract.md) — moving a rule into the wrong loaded file silently drops it for some verdict (catastrophic). Wants a canary/before-after + focused session, not an AFK trim. **Blocker cleared 2026-07-01 (shardPrompt DELETED, id:a0b6) — no longer 'pending shard-prompt work'; stays DEFERRED on intrinsic low-ROI + high-blast-radius grounds.** Not a haiku/target-drift concern (work agents are sonnet/opus). See 2026-06-18-0727-relay-skeleton-token-reduction.md. <!-- id:2895 -->

- [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **Relay broker: stop spawning one agent per mechanical shell command (WALL-TIME driver)** — user 2026-07-17, "all the Haiku agents waste so much wall time for basically mechanical tasks — I guess we should tackle the broker approach soon". MEASURED on run `relay-20260717-100452-13146` (`wf_5f223a67-ed2`, `/relay --intensive .` on loderite, 3 rounds, 30.6 min wall for ONE repo): 25 agents, of which only **4 did work** (1 sonnet execute, 1 fable review, 2 sonnet integrators) and **18 were haiku scaffolding** — 6× "run EXACTLY this one command", 3× discovery prelude, 3× discovery runner, 3× heartbeat refresh, plus quota-gate / `inject.sh take` / reconcile-on-restart / gaming-flags-log (~6 per round × 3 rounds). ROOT CONSTRAINT: the Workflow sandbox has **no shell, no filesystem, no Node API** — `agent()` is the ONLY shell escape hatch, so every `quota-stop.sh` / heartbeat / `inject.sh take` costs a full agent spawn: context load + model round-trip, **serialized on the critical path**. The 21 haiku agents burned 5.1M cache-read tokens ≈ **244k cached tokens EACH just to run one command**. NOTE THE FRAMING: this is a **wall-time** item, not a cost item — cost-wise the haiku scaffolding is minor (~7%) next to the single fable review child's 13.2M cache reads (~80%), and the user has explicitly said **the fable review is fine**; do NOT re-litigate it as a cost optimization. Corroborating prior measurement: `relay-econ.py` (id:08a3) already found across 36 runs that "status+scaffold are a bigger share of *wall-clock* than of *cost* (low concurrency → on the critical path)" — this run is a clean single-repo instance of exactly that. DIRECTION (design, NOT settled — this is why it is meeting-lane): a persistent local daemon executing the mechanical commands; precedent is the `/meeting` broker (`meeting/broker.py`, `broker-curl.sh`, `meeting-broker.service` — HTTP daemon, lazy-connect, idle-shutdown, port via `broker.json`), though that one exists to feed a renderer, not to execute commands. OPEN Q the design must answer: the workflow sandbox cannot `curl` either, so a broker still needs ≥1 agent hop per round — is the win (a) BATCHING all of a round's mechanical commands into ONE agent hop, (b) a genuinely persistent broker-client, or (c) collapsing rounds so fewer hops are needed? Also fold in the existing `echo-runner` agent type (the 2026-07-02 "relay-loop token-trim experiment" — a minimal Bash-only runner) as prior art on trimming per-hop context. Relates: id:08a3 (econ/wall-clock lens), id:c8b6 (event log), id:8419 (cheap interim), id:4416 (labels needed to measure any of this). <!-- id:3a1c -->

- [ ] **`journal.jsonl` records no labels — per-agent cost/wall attribution needs a hand-join** — user 2026-07-17, surfaced while measuring id:3a1c. A workflow's `journal.jsonl` line is only `{"type":"started|result","key":"v2:<sha>","agentId":"<id>"}` — **no `label`, no `model`, no `phase`, no prompt summary** — even though `relay-loop.js` passes `label`/`phase`/`model` to `agent()`. Consequence: answering "what did these 22 agents DO?" required joining `agent-<id>.meta.json` (has `model`, but empty `label`/`phase`) against the first user message inside each `agent-<id>.jsonl` to recover the prompt — a manual reconstruction, per run, to get facts the harness already had at spawn time. The Workflow tool's own diagnostics advertise the journal as the place to look ("one `{"type":"result",...}` line per completed agent with its full return value"), so this is a real gap in the documented path, not just an inconvenience. WANTED: persist `label`, `phase`, `model`, and a prompt digest on the `started` line (and duration/token counts on `result` if available). Note the likely split: `agent-*.meta.json` carrying `model` but EMPTY `label`/`phase` suggests the loss may be harness-side rather than relay-side — **establish which before designing a fix**; if harness-side, the relay-side fallback is to `log()` a label→agentId map per dispatch. Unblocks id:3a1c (can't quantify scaffold wall-time share per category without it) and sharpens `relay-econ.py` (id:08a3), which today re-derives categories heuristically. <!-- id:4416 -->

- [ ] **Single-repo scope: collapse per-round prelude + discovery runner + heartbeat into one agent hop** — 2026-07-17, cheap interim for id:3a1c (do NOT let this pre-empt the broker design; it is the do-now slice if the broker meeting slips). Under `args.onlyRepo` (id:7633) the discovery fan-out is already capped to 1 shard, but the round still spends SEPARATE agent hops on the prelude, the single discovery runner, and the heartbeat refresh — three serialized context loads to do what is, for one repo, one shell script's worth of work. Measured on `relay-20260717-100452-13146`: 3 rounds × ~6 scaffold agents = 18; collapsing prelude+runner+heartbeat would cut ~6–9 of them outright. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this overhead ratio is a **single-repo artifact** — on a 40-repo fleet run those same ~6 scaffold agents/round amortize across every repo, so this is NOT evidence the fleet design is wrong; the fix should be gated on `onlyRepo` being set and must not regress the fleet path. Gated on id:4416 only insofar as measuring the win needs labels. <!-- id:8419 -->

- [ ] **Collect failure reasons across relay children into a structured, queryable record (general failure ledger)** — user 2026-06-17. Today a unit's failure/handback reason lives only in the transient REPORT field and the RELAY_STATUS HANDBACK line for that run; there's no durable, aggregated record of WHY relay work fails over time. WANTED: a structured failure ledger that captures, per failed/handed-back unit, a categorized reason (e.g. `dirty-tree-race` id:0547, `gated-HARD-too-large` id:2d20, `interactive-auth-needed` id:a505, `Fable-unavailable`, `test-red`, `merge-conflict`, `quota-deferred`, `missing-dep`, `size-out`) plus repo/mode/model/run-id/timestamp — so recurring failure classes are visible and prioritizable (the DMAIC "Measure" substrate, cf. id:719e) instead of rediscovered run-by-run. Substrate already exists: the append-only `~/.config/relay/relay-events.jsonl` (id:c8b6) records dispatch/integrate/handback events — this likely extends the handback event with a `reason_category` + free-text, and adds a small reporter (`relay-failures.sh report` akin to `relay-burn.sh`/`relay-econ.py`) to roll them up by category/repo/time. Design qs: (a) closed enumeration of categories vs free-text + post-hoc clustering; (b) who classifies (the child self-reports a category in its REPORT schema vs the integrator infers from the handback reason); (c) reporter output + whether it feeds RELAY_STATUS / `/relay status` (id:ec9a) / the statusline. Pairs with id:a505 (auth-queue is one failure class) and id:719e (DMAIC waste/defect reduction). Relates to id:c8b6 (event log), id:08a3 (econ), id:2d20/id:0547 (specific failure modes). **SHARPENED 2026-07-26 (run relay-20260726-201109-29533) — the concrete missing primitive is CROSS-RUN handback memory, and it is a one-line structural fact: `relay-loop.js:850` declares `const handbackTracker = {}` fresh per invocation, so the id:1432 repeat-handback ALERT (`handbackAlerts(handbackTracker, 2)`, :2526) can only ever fire at >=2x WITHIN A SINGLE RUN. A unit that hands back exactly once per run, every run, forever, never trips it and silently burns one child per run.** Evidence this run: BOTH handbacks (zelegator id:c106 underspecified-N size-out; ai-codebench id:8bea 4h-GPU size-out) were first-occurrence-in-run, so `repeatHandbacks: []` — the alert was structurally incapable of firing, and nothing would have flagged them had they recurred every night. They only stopped re-firing because the id:3801 auto-gate happened to rewrite the ITEM (route:decision-gate / route:hard-split) — a DIFFERENT mechanism (child-writes-a-gate) that is not handback memory and does not fire when a child hands back WITHOUT writing a gate. So the ledger's first consumer should be: persist `{repo, verdict, item_id, reason_category, run_id, ts}` to `relay-events.jsonl`, then have the discovery prelude READ it and (a) surface "this repo/verdict has handed back N times across M runs" in RELAY_STATUS, and (b) at a threshold, suppress or downgrade the re-dispatch instead of re-spawning a child that will size out identically. Note the ledger must key on the ITEM id, not just repo+verdict — 8bea and bde7 are both `hard`+`INTENSIVE` on ai-codebench but are different failures. <!-- id:194e -->

## meeting skill

- [ ] **[HARD — meeting] Use the harness task-list tool (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate) for `/meeting` agenda items** (user 2026-07-20) — track each agenda item as a task (pending → in_progress at its discussion turn → completed once its decision is ratified), so the meeting's progress is live-visible and the closure gate can verify every agenda item reached a decision from durable task state, not the model's recollection. Natural fit: agenda item ↔ task, decision point ↔ completion, amendment session ↔ a re-opened/new task. Design Qs: (1) does it duplicate the plan-file transcript / meeting-note `## Agenda` (keep ONE SSOT — the note is durable, tasks are ephemeral session-progress)?; (2) the per-prompt ctx-budget rule — the Task tools are cheap, but only add if they earn their keep over the existing AskUserQuestion cadence; (3) interaction with the Fable-assisted flow id:7e87 (a Fable-review sub-step could be its own blocked task under each agenda item). Sibling of id:2b23 (same tool, /relay --drain). Relates id:7e87, `format.md` §Interactive mode, the closure gate (id:af5a). <!-- id:5c48 -->

- [ ] **BUG: /meeting (Opus) skipped two flow steps when invoked with a pre-formed subject arg** — observed 2026-06-16 (trAIdBTC id:abbf promotion meeting, routed in from `/relay human` which called the Skill tool with a long fully-formed subject string). Two omissions on the **Opus** path (the Fable inline-prose split is a SEPARATE known issue — not this): **(1) Adequate lenses not onboarded proactively.** Setup step 4 loads `personas.md`, but the subject-mode agenda ran with only the 3 standing personas (Archie/Riku/Petra) until the *user* asked "is there no additional lens to onboard?" — at which point 📈 Milo (the project's own quant-trading persona, registered from trAIdBTC) was obviously apt and materially changed the outcome (the n-dependence-of-the-firing-threshold argument). The skill should, for a subject-mode meeting, proactively scan the registry (esp. personas previously introduced *in this project*) and onboard topic-relevant ad-hoc lenses in the opening exchange, not wait to be prompted. **(2) Decision options not emitted in the SAME turn as the transcript.** `format.md` §Interactive default protocol (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku) is explicit: emit the transcript chunk AND call `AskUserQuestion` in the same response — "never end a turn on bare prose and send the question in a subsequent turn." At the first decision point I ended on bare prose (closing persona line) and the user had to type "Options?" to get the `AskUserQuestion`. That's the Fable inline-prose shape leaking onto the Opus path. **Hypothesised cause (user's):** invoking `/meeting` via the Skill tool with a big pre-formed `args` payload (vs an interactive `/meeting <subject>` typed by the user) led the model to compress/skip setup+protocol steps. WANTED: (a) make proactive project-persona onboarding an explicit, hard-to-skip step in the subject-mode flow (e.g. setup step 4 emits the candidate ad-hoc personas to onboard before the agenda); (b) reinforce the same-turn transcript+AskUserQuestion invariant so it holds regardless of how the skill was invoked (Skill-tool-with-args vs typed); (c) consider why a large args payload degrades step adherence. Relates to id:a6cb (other /meeting flow-omission bug). <!-- id:1d01 -->

- [ ] **BUG: /meeting can end without committing the implementation it just made** — observed 2026-06-16. A parallel `/meeting` session implemented id:689c (relay-loop.js orphan-park, D1) — it committed the RED spec (`tests/test_relay_orphan_park.sh`, 8044d2a) but ENDED leaving the matching `relay-loop.js` impl change UNCOMMITTED in the working tree. A sibling session found it dirty and committed it on its behalf (796e275) after verifying spec-green + structure-green. So /meeting's Class 1 dispatch (D7, "work as a /relay executor: append RELAY_LOG + commit") and/or the global post-prompt git-diary-workflow obligation did NOT commit the impl — only the spec landed. Possible causes: (a) Class 1 inline implementation didn't run git-diary-workflow before the session ended; (b) the session was interrupted between the spec-commit and the impl-commit; (c) the end-of-meeting steps don't assert a clean tree. WANTED: an end-of-meeting / end-of-turn guard that refuses to finish with un-committed working-tree changes the session itself made (or at least surfaces them loudly). Especially important for SHARED repos — a /meeting leaving dotclaude-skills dirty strands work for sibling sessions and risks a relay pool committing a half-finished spec file. Relates to the git-diary-workflow parallelity bug (claude-diary TODO) and the shared-repo attribution discipline (global CLAUDE.md Step 1c). <!-- id:a6cb -->

WANTED: cross-mode.md must either (a) ALWAYS re-dispatch to canonical `/meeting` (never conduct inline), or (b) explicitly carry the setup scaffolding (persona load + discoveries + profile) into the inline path. - [ ] **BUG: `/meeting --cross` INLINE meeting skips the EnterPlanMode→ExitPlanMode plan-approval gate** — observed 2026-06-23 (same session as id:74c7). The harness auto-exited plan mode after setup; the inline meeting then ran on per-decision `AskUserQuestion` picks alone and proceeded straight to end-of-meeting write-back (meeting note + ROADMAP annotations) **and committed/pushed** with no consolidated plan presented for approval first. - [ ] **INVESTIGATE: `/meeting` under Fable 5 now hard-refuses with `reasoning_extraction` — regression bisect** — observed 2026-07-19 (a loderite `/meeting <two-subject>` session). Fable returned a synthetic API-level refusal (`stop_reason: refusal`, `stop_details.category = reasoning_extraction`, explanation: "reverse engineering or duplicating model outputs"; user-facing "Fable 5's safeguards flagged this message… This sometimes happens with safe, normal conversations"). It fired at the FIRST generation right after the skill read `format.md` + `personas.md` — **before any dossier/subject content was loaded** — so the subject was irrelevant; the trigger is the meeting scaffolding itself. `reasoning_extraction` is an out-of-band Fable output classifier (NOT an in-context reminder), and Fable-5's own system prompt states it "includes additional safety measures for dual-use capabilities" that the Opus models (which ran every prior meeting) lack. **KEY SIGNAL: Fable previously conducted meetings fine** (cf. the Fable inline-prose path in id:1d01), so this is a REGRESSION — likely a recent `meeting/` change or a newly-onboarded persona lens that now pattern-matches "duplicating model outputs / externalizing reasoning". Prime suspects by date: `0490103` model-conditional plan mode (2026-07-18); persona onboarding/extension `366be55` (Dex/Lennart), `08792fa` (Lana), `2f666c7` (Cal) (2026-07-16/17). WANTED: (a) bisect `meeting/format.md` + `meeting/personas.md` + the model-conditional plan-mode change against Fable to find the minimal passing/failing scaffold; (b) determine whether a specific persona lens or the multi-persona-transcript instruction is the trigger; (c) decide a mitigation — model-gate `/meeting` to Opus when Fable is active, or reshape the persona-externalization format so it doesn't trip the classifier. Full transcript details + request-id in private loderite memory `fable-meeting-reasoning-extraction-block`. Relates id:1d01 (Fable meeting-path divergence). <!-- id:a4f5 -->

## worktrees / D-series

- [ ] **Nothing stops an executor child and its supervisor from running `make test` in the SAME worktree at once — and the resulting red is indistinguishable from a real one** — found 2026-07-16 during the id:7612 integration. The executor contract's done-check tells the child to run the full suite in its worktree; invariant 5 has the integrator **re-derive** that check before merging. Neither says anything about **overlap**, and the pool's lease (id:0902/ebfb) is per-REPO, not per-worktree — it does not serialize two suites inside one worktree. Observed here: the child ran `make test` and stalled waiting on it, so the supervisor ran `make test` on the same worktree concurrently → `247 passed, 1 failed`. Once the child's run ended the same command passed **3/3** (248/0, 248/0, 249/0). The failing assertion was a `grep` for a call site in a static file — which cannot vary unless something rewrote it mid-run — so **the mechanism is NOT established** and is deliberately not claimed; the correlation is 5 data points with no counterexample. **Why it matters:** a contaminated red is not just noise — it is *evidence-shaped*. It blocked a merge (conservative, fine) but sent the reviewer hunting `SRC_DIR`, `export DEST_DIR`, the `lint` prereq and stashing tests for a phantom, and it produced a confidently-wrong "deterministic, not flaky" verdict to the owner (chidiai case `2026-07-16-determinism-asserted-over-self-created-confound`). A red that means nothing costs more than no signal at all. **Fix candidates:** (a) **establish the mechanism first** — reproduce two concurrent suites in one worktree and find what actually varies (an observe-first spike; if nothing does, the correlation is wrong and this item dissolves); (b) a per-worktree test lock (`flock` on `<worktree>/.make-test.lock`) so a second suite waits rather than interleaves; (c) contract rule — the integrator does NOT re-run the suite while the child's own run may be live (needs a liveness signal the supervisor can read: the child's stall is currently only visible as prose in its final message); (d) cheapest and maybe sufficient — have the child report its suite result and the integrator re-derive **only after** confirming no live run (`pgrep`), treating a red under concurrency as UNKNOWN rather than FAIL. Prefer (a) before building any of (b)–(d) — [[observe before preventing]]. Relates id:0902/ebfb (per-repo lease), id:7612, the executor contract done-check, and [[mechanize-reliab]]. <!-- id:93bd -->

If yes, escalate to mechanical guard design (D5 follow-up). See: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-20-2105-todo-md-root-resolution-worktrees.md`. <!-- id:3507 -->

See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-04-1048-subagent-parallel-class1.md` and `docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-04-1144-worktree-per-session-d5.md`. <!-- id:cbb5 -->

## hooks / commit safety

- [ ] **`git-lock-push.sh` manifest mode silently no-ops against a chronically-dirty repo** — discovered 2026-06-19 building the quota sampler (id:d267): a manifest-mode call (`-f <file> -m <msg>`) on `~/src/claude-diary` (which is ~always dirty — DIARY.md edits in flight) **committed nothing yet returned exit 0**, so the caller logged "committed+pushed" while the file stayed untracked. Two compounding causes: (1) manifest mode stages+commits the listed paths (line 85) but then hits the **id:aa93 dirty-tree refusal** (line 123, the *other* unstaged files) and exits 0 non-fatally — yet in the observed run the listed-path commit ALSO didn't land (needs root-cause: is `git commit` partial-staging the manifest paths, or does an empty/failed stage slip through `set -e`?); (2) nesting matters — a caller already holding an flock on the repo's `.git-lock-push.lock` (fd 8) cannot call git-lock-push (it `exec 8>`s the same file → 30s deadlock). **Impact:** any automation trying to auto-commit ONE scoped file into a repo that carries unrelated dirty state can silently lose the commit while believing it succeeded. The sampler worked around it with an explicit scoped partial commit (`git commit -- <path>`) under the lock + opportunistic clean-tree-only push (see `tools/quota-sample.sh` §3). **Fix candidates:** (a) make manifest mode return NON-zero (or a distinct code) when the intended paths didn't actually commit, so callers can't false-log success; (b) document that manifest mode requires an otherwise-clean tree and is unsuitable for chronically-dirty repos; (c) offer a `--scoped-commit-only` mode that commits the listed paths and SKIPS the rebase/push when the rest of the tree is dirty (what the sampler reimplemented); (d) note the fd-8 self-nesting deadlock in the script header. Relates [[id:aa93 dirty-tree guard]], id:d267, id:3558 (worktree-per-session, the deeper fix). <!-- id:3b18 -->

- [ ] **Add a `make` target that installs the destructive-op guardrail into `settings.json`** (user 2026-07-15) — the auto-mode destructive-op guardrail (`autoMode.soft_deny` + `permissions.ask` for `rm -f`/`-rf`/`--force`, git force ops, and the destructive-non-force family `git reset --hard` / `restore` / `checkout -- ` / `clean -f`; documented in `docs/destructive-op-guardrail.md`) was added by hand to one machine's `~/.claude/settings.json` and is NOT yet in the install flow — a fresh `make install` (or a `settings.json` reset) on another machine wouldn't carry it. Add an **idempotent** `install-guardrails` (name TBD) merge target, wired into the top-level `install` target, mirroring `install-allowlist` / `install-relay-env` (which merge into `SETTINGS_JSON` via `tools/allowlist.py` / `tools/settings-env.py`). It must merge the `autoMode.soft_deny` rules (preserving `$defaults` and any existing entries) + the `permissions.ask` patterns without clobbering other settings, and be safe to re-run. Consider a source fragment (like `tools/allow-extra.txt`) for the rule set so it's reviewable/versioned here. Relates the settings-merge tooling, `docs/destructive-op-guardrail.md`. <!-- id:98fc -->

Contract: routes a bounded prompt to localhost:8080/v1, appends one log line per call, no silent truncation. See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-06-11-2235-subagents-local-llama-swap.md`. <!-- id:85d2 -->
