- [ ] **A fourth "model" tier = MECHANICAL EXECUTION (no real LLM) for pure-transport agents.** Motivated by the a0b6 classifier flip (2026-07-01): `relay-loop.js`'s `discover-run` runner and `discover-prelude` are now pure transport — they only run a fixed script recipe per item and relay the JSON verbatim (zero reasoning). A Haiku pilot ran `discover-run` correctly in exactly 3 tool calls (one `discover-repo.sh` per repo), so Haiku is the current floor — but even Haiku spends tokens + a model round-trip for work that is deterministic. The idea: inject a fourth tier alongside opus/sonnet/haiku that the Workflow `agent()` interface dispatches to but which executes the recipe DETERMINISTICALLY (no LLM). Constraint driving it: a Workflow script is sandboxed (no `exec`/subprocess), so `agent()` is the ONLY way to shell out — hence the tier can't be "nothing", it must be a real dispatch target. Candidate mechanisms: (a) revive the local-LLM-proxy (intercept `agent()` calls tagged `mechanical` and run the recipe via a local runner, returning schema-valid JSON — the [[local-llama-subagent-architecture]] proxy shape, spike id:95e3); (b) a local MCP "recipe-runner" tool the Workflow calls instead of `agent()`; (c) a harness primitive that runs a whitelisted command list and validates against the output schema. Anti-goal: do NOT reintroduce an LLM where determinism suffices (mechanize-first). Gate/relate: needs the `agent()`-injection-point question answered (is there a non-LLM dispatch target?); the parser-vs-proxy token-accounting spike; and the ToS/out-of-harness-billing tripwire ([[hermes-deferral-contract]]). First cheap step once unblocked: measure the Haiku-vs-mechanical per-round token+latency delta on `discover-run`/`discover-prelude` to size the win. Surfaced 2026-07-01 (user) right after the flip made the first genuinely-mechanical agents. **CHARACTERIZED + DEFERRED 2026-07-01 (background research agent, user-directed pilot-first):** the tier as-specified is **NOT buildable today** — confirmed against the harness that `agent()` has **no non-LLM dispatch target**; a "tier" is just a model-string mapped to a billed Anthropic model. All three candidate mechanisms fail their guardrails: (a) proxy = the already-REJECTED [[local-llama-subagent-architecture]] shape + pool-wide `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` alias poisoning + [[hermes-deferral-contract]] ToS tripwire; (b) MCP recipe-runner = a Workflow script **cannot call MCP directly** (only a spawned agent can) so it still spends the LLM round-trip — defeats the anti-goal; (c) whitelisted-command primitive = **doesn't exist** (an Anthropic feature request, file via `/feedback`). Given the sizing (post-a0b6 discovery is 1–3 short agent calls/round, sig-cached to fire only on churn), a mechanical tier would be **gold-plating** vs the real, already-de-risked win — which the agent found and **LANDED**: `discover-prelude` (:733) + `discover-run` (:849) still dispatched `model:'sonnet'` despite being pure transport → flipped **both to `haiku`** (the item's own "first cheap step"). The prelude flip needed a prompt hardening (emit **ABSOLUTE** paths — a literal `~` fed to `discover-sig.sh` yields an empty fail-open sig that silently disables the discovery cache; latent fragility, not haiku-specific); **re-piloted haiku = 50/50 non-empty sigs**, discover-run pilot = 3 tool calls; `test_discover_cache.sh` D1 pin updated sonnet→haiku; suite 151/0. **REMAINING = a parked forward-flag** on a future Anthropic mechanical/tool-runner dispatch primitive (`/feedback` filed if pursued); not executor-pickable. Measure residual haiku discovery cost only if it looks material after the flip. <!-- id:2ec4 -->

## Fable review 2026-07-08 — relay mechanization (verified findings; full trail in the 2026-07-08 diary entry)

- [ ] [HARD] ** mechanical-daemon hardening: running/ reaper, `.timer` retry companion, flock, wall-clock timeout, resource ACQUIRE not probe, single resource vocabulary, loud inject-failure** (Fable review 2026-07-08) — verified against `mechanical-daemon.sh`: (1) daemon death between `:109` (mv→running) and `:111` strands the recipe in `running/` FOREVER — no code anywhere scans running/ (recipe-manifest.md promises it's a recoverable marker; nothing delivers); add a startup-tick reaper (stale running/ → surfaced/requeued LOUDLY); (2) the only trigger is edge-based (`mechanical-daemon.path` PathModified on pending/) — a DEFERRED recipe doesn't modify pending/, so the documented "retried next tick" is actually "stalls until an unrelated write"; add a `.timer` companion; (3) no flock — a manual `run` racing the `.path`-fired service makes the loser's `mv` fail and abort the whole tick mid-batch under `set -e`; (4) `est_wall` gates launch but `bash -c` at `:110` has NO `timeout` — a hung cmd holds the oneshot active and blocks every future tick; wrap in `timeout <est_wall×k>`; (5) `:102` only PROBES the resource claim, never ACQUIRES it — two recipes (or recipe + concurrent pool job) both see "free" and launch together on one GPU; acquire via claim.sh for the run duration (relates the id:33d3 claim-liveness work); (6) `relay-intensity.sh:49` and `resource-probe.sh:35` disagree on the resource vocabulary and `recipe-validate.sh` checks against neither → a plausible `resource:"llama"` recipe defers FOREVER as resource-unavailable — a silent-forever-defer (id:4347 class); one vocab source, validate at intake; (7) inject failure after a successful run is a log-line swallow (`:114-116`) — a completed mechanical run never gets reviewed; escalate via the decision-queue (id:de31), never log-and-continue. TRUST BOUNDARY (meeting lane — folded into id:d0c0/ec23): `bash -c` runs recipe cmds verbatim as the user and the "only relay writes pending/" invariant is documented, not enforced (plain user-writable dir + auto-fire `.path`). <!-- id:1cb8 -->

## /batch — built-in parallel worktree command

- [ ] [HARD — meeting] **`drained` machine-verdict + `@wire`/`@manual` grammar split (folds in executor-no-own-RED + spec-completeness)** (meeting 2026-07-19-1058, from `routed:3684`-2/-4/-5; chidiai `2026-07-18-declared-loderite-drained-of-executor-actionable` (High, retro-corrected), `2026-07-18-instructed-relay-executors-to-author-their` (High), `2026-07-18-red-spec-verified-the-named-consumers-not-the-replay-path`) — a design meeting to mint: (a) a **`drained` verdict** in `classify-verdict.sh` (no open `[ROUTINE]`/`[HARD]` AND no open executor-doable wiring half) so reviewer prose may say "drained" only by quoting the machine output, and a routing headline may not contradict an in-context decomposition; (b) a **new grammar axis `@wire`** (executor-doable, host/e2e-verifiable) vs `@manual` (human tick only) — **including the re-label migration**: loderite's ROADMAP has ~103 `@manual` occurrences mislabelling executor-doable wiring that keep re-arming the false "drained". (c) **executor-must-not-author-its-own-RED-test** (folded from D4): the RED spec is the contract, authored by the strong side; an executor writing the test it is judged by is gaming (define-then-meet); a directly-dispatched executor with no prior RED spec triggers an **independent reviewer**, never self-verification; a flagged gap gets the *real* fix (moving spec authorship out of the executor), not cosmetic RED-first on a self-authored test; a close resting on self-marked verification is **provisional → reopen**. Land this with **at least a loud detector**, not prose-only (policy-without-enforcement reproduces the no-op). (d) **spec-completeness discipline**: even a handoff-authored RED spec is bounded by the consumers its author enumerated — require "enumerate every reader of the artifact". Cross-links id:2909 (gaming-detection), id:108e (triangulation). **DESIGNED 2026-07-19 (meeting `docs/meeting-notes/2026-07-19-1152-drained-verdict-wire-manual-grammar.md`) — stays OPEN as design umbrella; decomposed into children ac7f/bea2/0c86/78df. D1: `drained` = render-alias over `idle`, NO new verdict. D3: two-phase feature = two linked items (`@wire` executor + `gated-on:` `@manual` human), no re-tagging. D4: `@wire` = orthogonal RED-spec-backed marker, counts toward `actionable_routine_open`; `@manual` excluded. D5: flag-only detector here, 103-item re-label routed to loderite. - [ ] **Discover-speedup track (user-prioritized 2026-06-15: "discover always takes so long")** — the per-round discovery is ONE Opus agent (no `model:` override, relay-loop.js:425) sequentially scanning 30+ repos (fetch + sync-guard + worktree-reconcile/reap + classify + 8 per-repo fields) plus a global prelude (runId, `inject.sh take`, `claim.sh peek`). LLM-in-the-loop = the latency AND cost. Three composable levers, in build order: <!-- id:6788 -->
  - **(1) ✅ SHIPPED 2026-06-15 — parallel-shard the LLM scan** <!-- id:9ed4 --> (relay-loop.js: a once-only `discover-prelude` agent does runId + the consuming `inject.sh take` + `claim.sh peek` + own-repo list + non-own skipped; then N round-robin `discover-shard` classifiers fan out via `parallel(chunks.map(...))` and merge into the same discovery object. `DISCOVER_SHARDS` knob, default 6. `tests/test_relay_discover_shard.sh`, suite 44 green.) — split the per-repo classification across N cheaper agents instead of one sequential Opus pass. REQUIRES first extracting the **global prelude** (generate runId once; `inject.sh take` is *consuming* so it must run EXACTLY once; `claim.sh peek` once) out of the per-shard work, then fanning out shard agents (each given the shared runId + peek result + its repo subset), then merging `{units, surfaced, skipped}`. Biggest latency cut for least rewrite; ship first. Red test: assert the prelude (inject take / runId) runs once and discovery fans out over repo shards.
  - **(2) Incremental HEAD-keyed cache (the SAFE caching)** <!-- id:bc39 --> — cache per-repo `{HEAD, dirty-hash, claim-state}` from last round; a repo whose tuple is byte-identical reuses its cached verdict, only CHANGED repos are re-classified. Invalidation-keyed on actual git state, NOT time (this is why it's safe where id:22ef's reject-verdict-caching warning does not apply — that warned against *time/blind* caching). Skips the bulk of repeat work in steady state. Red test: a repo with unchanged HEAD/dirty/claim is not re-scanned; any change invalidates.
  - **(3) Deterministic scanner = the real fix** <!-- id:23fe --> — extend the EXISTING `scripts/discover-repos.sh` (already emits ownership/dirty/last-ckpt TSV in seconds) to emit the full verdict JSON (DISCOVER_SCHEMA): the 4 classification rules + the 3ac8 worktree reconciliation become tested shell, the LLM is left only the one irreducible NL bit (acceptable-dirt per relay.toml comment) or dropped. Removes the model from the hot path AND de-risks 3ac8's reaping into tested code. Same id as the Wiggum-agenda item. Red test: discover-repos.sh emits schema-valid verdict JSON matching the LLM classifier on a fixture repo set. **FOLD IN 2026-06-29 (user):** also emit the recurring **cheap pre-scan** fields a strong-turn `handoff&review --all` needs per confirmed `own` repo — unaudited-commit count since last ckpt, ROADMAP open-`[ ]` count, TODO open-`[ ]` count, dirty-state — **resolving repos+paths from relay.toml (honoring `# path:`), NOT a `~/src/*` glob**. This session a strong turn improvised exactly that glob scan and missed the nested `zkm/plugins/*` repos; the fix is to make the tested scanner the only path so no per-run improvisation is needed (cf. [[feedback-use-existing-tools-not-improvise]], [[feedback-mechanize-no-swallow-stderr]]).
  - **(also ✅ SHIPPED 2026-06-15) status-write off the critical path** <!-- id:cb50 --> — the Haiku `write-relay-status` agent was `await`ed between discover→dispatch and at round end, so the next discover/dispatch blocked on a pure visibility side-effect (user caught the pool sitting on just a write-relay-status when discovery could already proceed). Now `scheduleStatusWrite` snapshots the content and queues the write on a serialized `statusTail`; the pool proceeds immediately and the run flushes the tail once before returning. `tests/test_relay_status_offcrit.sh`.
  - **Build deliberately, NOT into a running pool** — discovery is the single most critical step; each lever lands with its red test, relay-loop.js edits affect only the NEXT launch, and the current pool finishes on the old code. Sequence 1→2→3 (cb50 done). <!-- id:9ed4 --> <!-- id:bc39 -->

- [ ] **[DESIGN/meeting] Connectivity-resilient relay — craft a deterministic workflow per session, then run mostly WITHOUT live cloud dependency** — **Motivation (user 2026-06-15): "that incident shows how volatile cloud-AI dependency is."** A 2-hour pool run = hundreds of live `agent()` cloud calls; a single network drop killed discover-shard:6 + a status write mid-run, and a deterministic `new Date()` bug crashed the whole pool. Every per-step cloud round-trip is a failure point. **Direction:** have the STRONG turn *craft a deterministic workflow per session* (plan/decide once, cloud-side), then *execute* it with as few live cloud `agent()` calls as possible: <!-- id:a778 -->
  - **Mechanize the mechanical steps** → tested shell, no LLM in the hot path: the deterministic `discover-repos.sh` emitting verdict JSON (id:23fe), a deterministic `relay-integrate.sh` (merge→tag→push→prune as shell, frees a slot + removes a cloud call per integration), the HEAD-keyed discovery cache (id:bc39).
  - **Local-model fallback for the irreducibly-LLM steps** when cloud is down/volatile — review/handoff judgment via a local model ([[local-llama-subagent-architecture]] B-spine; spike id:95e3 gates the wrapper). Degrade-not-die: cloud blip → fall back to local, not crash.
  - **Lean on resume** for crash/drop recovery: `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` replays the cached agent prefix; pair with the relay's external-state mutation (resume-safety — fresh-relaunch vs resume tradeoff, noted 2026-06-15).
  - **Open questions** (route to a /meeting): which steps are *irreducibly* cloud-LLM vs mechanizable; the local-model quality bar for discover/review; how "craft once, run deterministically" reconciles with the pool's side-effecting git/worktree mutation; whether a session crafts ONE big workflow or the strong turn keeps emitting smaller deterministic units. Connects: id:23fe, id:95e3, the Date-crash guard (test_relay_no_date_api.sh), the failed-shard surfacing (953cf2e). <!-- id:cfa9 -->

- [ ] **Guard relay-loop.js against the pool's own Workflow-sandbox bugs** — 2026-06-15 the autonomous pool crashed/degraded THREE times from its executor/review children editing the Workflow engine (`relay-loop.js`) with code the static tests can't validate against the LIVE Workflow runtime: a partial id:8c35 (unwired), `new Date()` (id:3826, db5ec43), and `process.env.HOME` (id:3826, a8fe504) — the last two threw synchronously out of `integrate()` and killed the whole pool at the first REVIEW integration. `tests/test_relay_no_date_api.sh` now statically flags Date/process/require/fs/Math.random, but that's per-class whack-a-mole. Deeper fix: either a **runtime smoke check** ("does relay-loop.js start + run one no-op round under the Workflow shim?") gating any merge that touches it, OR treat `relay-loop.js` as a **protected file** only attended sessions edit (executors hand back relay-engine changes instead of committing them). Connects id:cfa9. <!-- id:e37b -->

If it fell through, split the remainder into its own `[HARD]` ROADMAP line so the pool sees it. <!-- id:e0c1 -->

- [ ] **Octopus-merge consolidation for independent parallel worktrees finishing close in time** — when the serialized integrator has ≥2 verified worktree branches that are mutually NON-CONFLICTING and completed within a short window, consider a single `git merge --no-ff branchA branchB branchC` (octopus) → ONE integration commit + ONE checkpoint + ONE push, instead of N sequential `--no-ff` merges + N tags + N pushes. Benefits: less RELAY_LOG/tag noise, fewer pushes, faster drain. Decision-call / constraints: (a) the octopus strategy REFUSES on any conflict, so it's only valid for provably-disjoint file sets — the SAME independence test that licensed running them in parallel; (b) loses per-track checkpoint granularity (relay tags per-track today) — a single bad track can't be cherry-excluded post-merge as cleanly, so prefer sequential when any track is unverified/risky; (c) attribution: the combined ckpt message MUST enumerate each track's id + summary. Heuristic: octopus when N≥2 disjoint + each individually gate-verified + close-in-time; fall back to sequential when tracks share files or need independent checkpoints/bisect points. Observed first-hand 2026-06-17 (zkWhale demo-chain): THEME + emoji-svgs + logo were near-independent and finished within minutes — a 3-way octopus would have collapsed 3 merges/tags/pushes into one. (user request 2026-06-17) <!-- id:8691 -->
  - **Field report — zkWhale demo-chain run, 2026-06-17/18 (~20 background agents, directed `/relay --afk`):** Ran ~20 worktree children in waves of 1–3, integrated sequentially (merge → full gate → ckpt-tag → push) ≈20×. Findings: (1) **Conflicts were NOT the bottleneck** — disjoint file-scoping *in the child prompts* prevented nearly all of them; the real tax was the repeated **per-merge integration ceremony**, dominated by re-running the full gate each time (`pnpm test` ~8–15 s + typecheck + lint) plus a push apiece. Octopus's win here is halving *gate-runs + pushes* for co-ready disjoint waves, more than the tag/log noise. (2) **Octopus opportunities genuinely arose ~4–5×** (THEME+emoji-svgs; spinrot+logofix; the two logo rounds; proofglyph+badgesvg) — each ≥2 branches, file-disjoint, individually green, finished within minutes. (3) **The octopus-blockers that actually recurred were a small set of high-churn shared files:** `strings.ts` (almost every UI agent appends copy — distinct keys so git *auto-merged*, but it's the #1 risk), `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml` (new devDeps: vite-plugin-singlefile, jimp, potrace), hot UI files like `ArtifactScreen.tsx` (touched by demo-mount/spinner/emphasis across waves), and the ledgers (`TODO.md`). Plus genuine **dependency chains** forced sequencing regardless of merge strategy (a8c2-wiring after the spinner work; demo-transparent-drop after demo-polish). (4) **Deterministic eligibility predictor that would've worked:** pairwise-intersect `git diff --name-only main..<branch>` across the co-ready candidates; empty intersection ⇒ octopus-safe. (5) **Granularity downside barely bit this workload** — every track was gate-verified *before* merge, so I never needed to bisect/cherry-exclude a track post-integration; a well-formed combined ckpt message preserved the attribution that per-track tags gave. (6) **Recommended impl:** optimistic octopus — `git merge --no-ff b1 b2 …` (git refuses cleanly on conflict, no half-merge), fall back to sequential for the conflicting subset; gate ONCE after the merged result; run `pnpm install` once if any branch touched the manifest (orthogonal to merge strategy but required before the gate). Net: for this run, a file-intersection-gated optimistic octopus would have cut ~5–7 of the ~20 integration cycles (~30%) with negligible downside. (field report 2026-06-18)

- [ ] **Directed `/relay <args>` front-session should spawn children as BACKGROUND agents by default** — user request 2026-06-17. A directed/scoped/`--afk` run (e.g. `/relay . --afk <directive>`) is driven by the strong front session fanning out via the Agent tool (handoff/review C4), NOT the autonomous-pool Workflow. Those Agent spawns should default to `run_in_background: true` so the session feels like the no-arg autonomous pool front-door: work happens in the background, the front session is purely the COORDINATOR (status, serialized integration, checkpoints, summaries) — the only thing surfaced in the front session is coordinator output, not blocking agent transcripts. Today this depends on the operator remembering to background each Agent call; make it the documented default in `references/handoff.md` + `references/review.md` (and the orchestrator invariants §4 "Spawn waves"). Keep foreground only when a child's result is an immediate hard dependency of the very next coordinator step. - [ ] **Pre-scheduled "days-off" → spend the 7-day quota faster on known-idle days (with a reserve floor)** — user request 2026-06-17. The 7-day rolling bucket's whole-window pacing (`RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_7D` front-loads early, backs off late; `RELAY_QUOTA_THRESHOLD_SEVEN_DAY`/`_SONNET` cap it) assumes the operator might come back any time and want quota left. But the user often KNOWS in advance they won't use Claude Code (e.g. "this weekend I'm away") — on those days the conservative back-off just wastes 7d budget that nobody is competing for. WANTED: a way to **pre-declare idle days/intervals** so during them the pool is allowed to burn the 7d bucket harder (raise the 7d threshold / suppress the decay back-off), while STILL leaving an **adequate reserve** sized to expected usage after the operator returns — never draining to 0 right before they come back. **Design hinge:** the reserve floor is the real parameter — given a known idle interval `[start,end]`, relax the 7d cap *inside* it but keep enough that the window-after-`end` (until the bucket's next reset) still has working budget; the saving is "don't reserve quota for an operator who's provably absent." **Sketch:** a small calendar/intervals source (e.g. `~/.config/relay/days-off.toml` or iCal-ish: `2026-06-20/2026-06-22, reserve=0.20`), read by `quota-stop.sh`'s gate; when `now ∈ an off-interval`, use a relaxed 7d threshold (e.g. burn to `1 - reserve` instead of the decayed cap), reverting automatically outside the interval. **Design qs for a likely `/meeting`:** (a) carrier/format — a TOML intervals file vs a `/relay off <date-range> [--reserve R]` CLI that writes it vs reading the system calendar; (b) how the reserve floor composes with `RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_7D` (override it inside the interval vs blend) and the 5h bucket (probably untouched — 5h refills fast); (c) per-bucket scope (7d + 7d-Sonnet only) and whether the relaxed cap is absolute or still decays toward the reserve as `end` approaches; (d) auto-expiry + a guard so a stale past-dated off-interval can't silently relax a live run; (e) interaction with the autonomous-campaign id:af30 (the natural consumer — a multi-day unattended campaign over a declared days-off window) and the patient-stop/STOP sentinels (id:d0bc/id:3b1e). Relates to `RELAY_QUOTA_DECAY_7D`, `RELAY_QUOTA_THRESHOLD_SEVEN_DAY[_SONNET]`, `quota-stop.sh`, id:af30 (timed cross-window campaign), id:219b (burnup data to size the reserve empirically). (user request 2026-06-17) <!-- id:2904 -->

- [ ] **Statusline cost should include workflow + subagent token totals (folded in, or a 2nd entry)** — user request 2026-06-17. The Claude Code statusline cost figure appears to count only the main loop, not the tokens spent by spawned `Agent`/Workflow subagents — so a session that fans out many background agents (observed: a directed `/relay --afk` run spawned ~16 background Opus children) badly UNDERcounts true spend. WANTED: the statusline reflects total spend = main loop + all spawned agents + workflows, either (a) folded into the existing `$` cost number, or (b) shown as a second segment (e.g. `$<main> +$<agents>` or `Σ$<total>`). Note the relay already has a live statusline segment (id:15bd: `🔁<round> ✓<done> ⚙<in-flight> Δ$<burn>/h` from RELAY_STATUS.md) and `relay-burn.sh`/`relay-econ.py` already attribute per-agent cost from `profile-run.sh` records — so the data exists; this is about surfacing the AGGREGATE in the always-on statusline, not just during relay runs. Design qs: where the per-agent token usage is readable for the statusline script (agent JSONL transcripts? a running tally file?); main-loop-only vs session-total semantics; how it composes with the existing relay segment so they don't double-count. (user request 2026-06-17) <!-- id:c0bc -->

So a heavy directed session is invisible to the cost/quota tooling. WANTED: a measurement path that works for Agent-spawn sessions. **Reusable recipe proven this session** (works with zero new infra): aggregate `message.usage` (`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` + `message.model`) from (a) each spawned agent's transcript `…/tasks/<id>.output` JSONL **and** (b) the main session JSONL `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session-id>.jsonl`; price per-tier (Opus $15/$75 per Mtok in/out, cache-read 0.1×, cache-write 1.25×; Sonnet $3/$15). Also: have a directed run call `relay-burn.sh sample` at start+end so the actual `seven_day`/`seven_day_sonnet` utilization delta IS captured (the only way to get a TRUE % of weekly quota vs an API-$-equivalent estimate). **Seed data point (this session — zkWhale demo-chain, ~20 Opus agents + 1 octopus merge, 2026-06-17/18):** measured **≈ $817 API-equiv** (agents ~$408, main loop ~$409; ~$806 Opus + ~$10 Sonnet); **~395 M tokens processed of which 384 M (97%) was cache-read** at 0.1× — only ~10.5 M fresh, ~1.55 M generated output; **prompt caching saved ~$5 k (~7×** vs no-cache ~$5.8 k); est. **~15–25% of a Max-20× weekly Opus allowance** (≈ 4–6 such sessions/week to drain it). This is the kind of number the tooling should produce automatically. **Per-project breakdown (extension, user request 2026-06-18):** the report must also attribute cost/tokens PER PROJECT/REPO, not just a session total — essential for multi-project sessions like the autonomous `/relay` no-args pool (one run fans agents across many repos). The main-loop (orchestrator) cost is shared overhead — report it as its own line, optionally amortized across the projects it served. Output shape: `session-cost.sh` → per-repo rows + an "orchestrator/shared" row + grand total, so a `/relay` run shows "repo A $X, repo B $Y, … orchestrator $Z". - [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **Write-scope the LLM tier by uid: separate OS users for the relay supervisor/reviewer vs. the executors, so an executor CANNOT write `main` even if it tries** (user 2026-07-17) — the ratified sandbox cluster (id:9d97/b3d0/13ae/02c7/8e7a) scopes only the **mechanical daemon** tier (`relay-ro` discovery producer, `relay-svc` recipe-exec); the **LLM executor** tier is currently unscoped and runs as `tobias` with full write access to every repo's main working tree, refs, and push credential. Proposal: executor uid may write ONLY its own worktree; supervisor/reviewer uid owns `main` + integration. **Motivating instance — VERIFIED 2026-07-17 from the transcript** (`~/.claude/projects/-home-tobias-src-loderite/79ab5449-350a-4a26-9e59-fdb02f2ed3cf.jsonl`, session 11:49, following relay run `relay-20260717-100452-13146`): the agent self-reported *"I initially edited `src/material-field.ts` directly in the main checkout (`/home/tobias/src/loderite`) instead of the worktree"* and flagged it to the integrator. **Threat-model nuance the meeting MUST NOT skip: this was agent ERROR (wrong path), self-caught and self-corrected — NOT adversarial intent and NOT a prompt injection.** So the case for uid-scoping here rests on **error frequency**, not on an attacker model; it is a guard against fat-fingering the canonical tree, which DAC would have made structurally impossible (the agent could not have written it to notice-and-fix in the first place). Do not let the meeting silently upgrade this into an adversarial-containment argument — that argument may also be valid, but it is NOT what this instance evidences. Corollary for cost/benefit: the observed blast radius was ~zero (self-corrected), so the honest question is how often it happens UNcaught. **Evidence base already in hand:** the id:5937 deny-tail probe measured that `permissionMode=auto` denies NOTHING on the executor surface (write-outside-repo, `git push`, network egress all approved) and that **OS-level DAC was the ONLY boundary that actually held** — so this is the one control class with evidence behind it, not a speculative guard (relates id:e2b1/453a — and note `--disallowedTools` is explicitly NOT a boundary, the model routes around it). **Design questions for the meeting — do NOT assume any of these are settled:** (1) git worktrees SHARE the `.git` dir, so file-DAC on main's working tree does not by itself stop `git branch -f main` / a ref write — `refs/heads/main` (and the objects dir the executor must write to commit at all) live in the shared dir; scoping may need ACLs on refs, a per-executor `--separate-git-dir`, or a push-only model. (2) DAC does not stop `git push origin main` — that needs remote-side branch protection or a **credential split** (executor holds no push cred), which is the D5/id:38bf ssh-push model's territory. (3) **This is NOT purely additive: the current executor contract has executors commit AND push** (verified today — the id:521f executor pushed to GitHub + `fievel` itself), so scoping the executor tier REWRITES the contract's integration step; cost is real and belongs in the decision. (4) Interaction with the id:dc5b ledger-collision fix — if executors stop writing shared ledgers at all, dc5b's collision class may partly dissolve structurally rather than need a guard (cf. "prefer dissolving a problem structurally over guarding it"). Relates id:af30 (containment ≠ authorization; this authorizes nothing about the self-relaunching loop shape), id:38bf (the `relay-pool` sandbox tier spec + ssh-push repo-write model — closest sibling, likely merges with this), id:13ae, id:5937, id:d5e0. **CANDIDATE MECHANISM (user 2026-07-17): btrfs CoW-copy each executor's repo and treat executor repos as REAL REMOTES** — i.e. replace the shared-`.git` worktree model with an independent per-executor repo, integrated by an ordinary `git fetch` from the executor's copy. This DISSOLVES design-question (1) structurally rather than guarding it: with its own `refs/heads/main`, an executor writing `main` is *harmless* — it writes its own copy — and uid-scoping collapses to "executor owns its copy, cannot touch the canonical repo" (cf. "prefer dissolving a problem structurally over guarding it"). **Two SEPARABLE claims — do not conflate at the meeting:** (i) *real-remotes topology* is the architectural win and needs NO btrfs (`git clone --local` already yields an independent `.git`; these repos are small — `.git` measured 19M dotclaude-skills / 21M loderite 2026-07-17); (ii) *btrfs reflink as the copy mechanism* earns its place on two specific grounds, NOT raw speed: **(a) `git clone --local` HARDLINKS objects (same inode) = a supervisor↔executor aliasing hazard; `--no-hardlinks` is safe but re-materializes everything — reflink gives independence AND metadata-cost, beating both**; **(b) warm working trees** — a clone checks out COLD (an executor on loderite must `npm install` before vitest can run), whereas `cp --reflink=always -r` copies the whole workspace incl. `node_modules`/`.venv`/build caches at O(metadata), retiring a per-dispatch cost the current worktree model already pays. **Verified 2026-07-17:** `/home` IS btrfs (subvol `@home`, /dev/nvme0n1p2) and `cp --reflink=always` succeeds within `/home` (fails only cross-fs to `/tmp`, tmpfs — expected). **Caveats to carry into the meeting:** `btrfs subvolume snapshot` does NOT work directly — `~/src/<repo>` is a plain dir inside `@home`, not its own subvolume; the cheap path today is reflink-`cp` on plain dirs, UNLESS repos are converted to subvolumes (which additionally buys atomic point-in-time + cheap discard, attractive for parked orphans / id:689c). Copying the whole workspace also copies DIRTY state (executor inherits uncommitted junk) → likely gate on a clean tree. And it COUPLES the relay to btrfs + same-filesystem placement — true on zomni, but `fievel` (Raspbian) likely is not, so a `git clone` fallback is needed if the relay ever runs there. Supersedes nothing; folds into the D5 worktree-per-session model (relates id:d5e0) and may partly dissolve id:dc5b. <!-- id:d03d -->

Feasible today and partly in use: `agentType` resolves from the `.claude/agents/` registry; `echo-runner` (Tools: Bash) already exists and `relay-loop.js` already pins `discover-shard` to `model:'sonnet'`. **TWO SEPARABLE value props — do NOT conflate:** **(a) BUILD — declarative defaults:** move the scattered imperative `model:`/`effort:` opts in `relay-loop.js` into named agent defs (`relay-execute`→sonnet, `relay-review`/`relay-hard`/`relay-handoff`→opus-apex, `relay-mechanical`→echo-runner/haiku, `discover-shard`→sonnet), so per-subcommand tier/tooling is ONE declarative source instead of imperative sprawl; also shrinks each agent's accidental tool surface. The real enforcement boundary is the OS-DAC/uid work (id:13ae/02c7/d03d) — agent types are COMPLEMENTARY to it, never a substitute, and must never be recorded as "the sandbox." **Decision for the meeting:** ratify building (a) as declarative defaults + record the (b) non-containment invariant; sequence against d03d (if executors move to real-remotes/uid-scoping, the executor agent def changes anyway). - [ ] **`actionable_routine_open` ignores `(DEP: …)` gating → pool burns empty executor rounds (RECURRENCE)** — observed twice on yinyang-puzzle. Run relay-20260710-105732 dispatched FIVE `execute` units at it; only the round at `relay-ckpt-20260710-1319` did work (`5eb8`/`2150`/`292c`, 108/108 green). The rounds at `-1327`, `-1334`, `-1341` produced **checkpoint-only commits, no merge, no change**, yet the pool reported `substantive: true` for each. Cause: `classify-repo.sh`'s `actionable_routine_open` predicate excludes `@manual` and `🚧`/`BLOCKED on`, but NOT the `(DEP: <ids>)` form. yinyang-puzzle's `id:a034`/`id:12b9`/`id:5107` are `[ROUTINE] (DEP: 72ae…6ae2)`, gated on seven `[HARD]` Archimedean tilings that have not shipped, so no RED specs exist for them — the executor correctly refuses, writes nothing, and the classifier re-emits `execute` next round. Verified 2026-07-10: `classify-repo.sh --emit unit` still returns `verdict=execute, reason="Open executor-actionable [ROUTINE] ROADMAP items present"` on a repo whose only open `[ROUTINE]` items are `@manual`, `🚧`-blocked, or `(DEP: …)`-gated. **The 2026-07-08 run already surfaced this as a handback** ("stale classifier verdict … no `[ROUTINE]` work was actually available this round") — it was diagnosed and not fixed, so it recurred. Fix: teach the predicate that `(DEP: <unshipped-id>)` gates an item (resolve the dep's checkbox; open dep ⇒ not actionable), and make the re-dispatch breaker treat a checkpoint-only round as non-substantive so a repo cannot be re-dispatched into the same no-op. Mapping: **(1) unit lifecycle maps BEAUTIFULLY** — executor pushes its branch at START (empty commit = claim, commits = progress): claim becomes visible/timestamped/attributable and survives OOM/crash for free (the 2026-07-08 evidence: island-1 agent blocked by a fresh-mtime/dead-pid claim needing timing forensics to attribute; same-day partial-staging ledger dance); orphan-worktree reaping dissolves (id:a4e9 refs-are-the-registry → the REMOTE branch is the registry); pairs with sandbox D5's ssh-push write boundary (id:d916 — this item is its claim-side half). **(2) pre-merge review maps AT REAL COST** — review-after-merge is a deliberate economic decision (cheap executors land continuously, scarce apex audits async via the substantive_unaudited verdict); gating merges on apex serializes the pool on quota; zero logged gaming incidents (id:2909 deferred the refuter fleet on that evidence) and 23ab moves high-stakes modules to ungameable acceptance anyway — keep post-merge audit unless gaming evidence appears; draft-PR-then-merge-then-audit is the valid hybrid. **(3) two claim consumers DON'T map:** resource claims ([INTENSIVE] GPU run-alone = machine mutex, nothing to merge) and shared-ledger writes (TODO/ROADMAP single-file edits; af04 REJECTED branch isolation for exactly this — checkbox merges non-unionable; md-merge/flock stays). Reconcile half-maps: dead-work reaping trivializes under claim-as-branch; dirty/diverged normalization is orthogonal. **Substrate:** GitHub PRs only cover github-remote repos + id:de4e rejected GitHub as orchestrator hub; Forgejo-on-fievel = new infra; PREFER PR-as-convention on bare git (`refs/relay/units/<id>` + existing REVIEW_ME/RELAY_LOG as the thread) — zero new infra, works on both remotes, lever-first. **Meeting must decide:** adopt claim-as-pushed-branch for execution units? (folds/advances id:d916 — evaluate together); ref namespace + lifecycle (open/progress/done/abandoned-TTL); what claim.sh keeps (resources, ledgers, /meeting advisory); integrator changes (--no-ff merge from remote ref instead of local worktree); does this satisfy d916's trigger or wait for it. ## semver / CHANGELOG cluster 2026-07-23 (meeting `2026-07-23-2320-semver-changelog-enforcement-cluster`)

- [ ] **[ROUTINE] `changelog-append.sh` misorders a same-day entry made AFTER a release — post-release work permanently reads as pre-release** (meeting 2026-07-23 D5-A1; found by the Fable closing pass, verified) — bucket lookup is first-match **anywhere** in the file (`relay/scripts/changelog-append.sh:115`, `hdr_idx = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if matches(ln)), None)`) and a NEW bucket is inserted before the **first** header. Same-day sequence: (1) an internal close creates `## YYYY-MM-DD` at the top; (2) a release inserts `## vX.Y.Z — YYYY-MM-DD` **above** it; (3) a second internal close that same day matches the existing date bucket, which now sits **below** the release bucket, and appends there. In a newest-first file whose own preamble forbids reordering ("never hand-edit or reorder past buckets"), that entry is now permanently misfiled as pre-release. **Second, related gap:** standing date buckets between releases never fold into the next release, so a reader cannot tell which version ships a date-bucketed change — the standard remedy is an `## Unreleased` bucket the next release absorbs, and deciding that is IN SCOPE for this item (the meeting deliberately did not pre-decide it). Both only bite semver repos; this repo is version-less (id:8ef3) and date-buckets exclusively, so it never hits case (2). Contract a test would verify: after a release bucket exists, a later same-day non-release entry must not land in a date bucket positioned below it. Relates D5 (keep the mix — internal closes date-bucket), id:b8fa (the deriver), id:f6d5. <!-- id:010c -->

## relay human triage 2026-07-23 (filed by `/relay human .`)

- [ ] **[ROUTINE] Install-drift lint: LOUD-fail when a repo file has no `~/.claude` symlink** (relay human 2026-07-23, observed live) — `make install` creates per-file symlinks, but a file added to an already-installed skill dir is NOT picked up until someone re-runs `make install`, and **nothing detects the gap**. Live instance: `relay/scripts/inbox-scan-repo.sh` (id:ce50) merged to `main` (18df6c0) and its ROADMAP box was ticked `[x]`, yet the installed tree had no symlink — so `~/.claude/skills/relay/scripts/inbox-scan-repo.sh` exited **127** and this very `/relay human .` run's mandated human.md §2 inbox scan silently did not run. Four other scripts had the same drift (`auto-integrate-orphan.sh`, `discover-chunk.sh`, `discover-prelude.sh`, `relay-spawn-bench.sh`). This is the *"a check nothing invokes isn't a check"* class (id:de36) one level up: a check that IS invoked but resolves to a missing path. **Build**: extend `make status` (or a new `tools/install-drift.sh` it calls) to diff every installable repo file against its expected `$DEST_DIR` symlink and exit non-zero on any missing/stale/dangling link; wire it into `tests/run-tests.sh` so the suite red-lights the drift, and into `relay-doctor.sh` so `/relay health` surfaces it. Ignore `__pycache__`. Note the *tick* was not wrong (the code did ship) — the gap is that "shipped" ≠ "reachable by its documented caller". **SHARPENED 2026-07-29 (id:18ed FOLDED IN and deleted — owner-decided; it was a triple-duplicate of this item and of a REVIEW_ME box).** Live recurrence: `relay/scripts/fable-config.sh` was committed 2026-07-28 (9695c5b) with no symlink, and the `meeting` SKILL.md step 0f `--fabled` availability check hit `exit 127` on 2026-07-29. The sharper framing that instance gives this item: relay-doctor's install-drift check (id:1102) **ALREADY DETECTED this drift and reported it in a REVIEW_ME box on 2026-07-28** — yet the symlink stayed missing until the exit-127. **So the gap is NOT detection; it is that nothing ACTS on the detection.** That is the "loud detection whose resolution silently no-ops" anti-pattern (global CLAUDE.md, mechanize-first) — which argues this item should auto-run `make install` (or **fail the suite**), not merely lint. Build accordingly: a lint that only reports reproduces the exact failure it is meant to prevent. <!-- id:ba27 -->

## ledger substrate

### DECIDED 2026-08-10 — tracker pilot (resolves id:4a5c; meeting `docs/meeting-notes/2026-08-10-0906-tracker-substrate-replacing-markdown-ledgers.md`)

Owner ratified: adopt a real work-tracking substrate, **piloted**. Explicit **amendment to `id:2840`**
("markdown is SSOT, index is a cache") on premises it never weighed plus one now refuted — archiving
does NOT bound ledger size (measured: `ROADMAP.md` 254 KB / 69 open **after** archiving 100 done items,
~25 lines of prose per open item), git-archaeology for issues is **not wanted**, and dashboards /
assignee / labels / typed dependencies are SSOT properties a read-only cache cannot meet. `id:2840`
stays OPEN as the named fallback (with `id:75db`, the live successor to the closed `id:659c`).
Evaluate **Plane and Vikunja** via one common intermediate JSON + thin adapters; shadow-import all
~60 repos with **loderite** as the deep-fidelity pilot; markdown stays SSOT and **no relay script
writes to the tracker**. A `--fabled` closing pass forced 5 amendments (all accepted) — see the note.
Fail condition: 4 weeks from first successful full import, measured against a **control-arm** board
built over `classify-repo.sh`; expiry 4 weeks from actual start of work (the never-started case is
deliberately left unbounded — see `id:da1a`).

- [ ] [HARD] Write both adapters (Plane, Vikunja) against the intermediate schema. Contract: the same fixture JSON yields equivalent item graphs — relations, labels, assignee, statuses — in both targets. <!-- children-of:2bb1 --> **PARTIAL 2026-08-10 — merged, box deliberately LEFT OPEN.** Both adapters are built and the cross-target *mapping* contract is proven: all three fixtures yield byte-identical item graphs recovered from each adapter's own emitted payloads (not re-derived from the source, which would be vacuous). **Vikunja verified LIVE** against the zomni pilot — 19 items/39 labels/3 relations applied, `verify` PASS 0 problems, idempotent on re-apply, drift visible in BOTH directions on the real board, and the gate proven non-vacuous by deleting a carrier label server-side and watching `verify` fail then repair. **Plane's transport is UNVERIFIED and cannot be verified while `id:02f7` blocks the proxy** — its request shapes come from documented API v1, never an observed response, so the item's own "equivalent in both targets" clause is NOT discharged. Needs its own loud channel: a notification on refusal, or a watchdog check for "no run started in N hours". <!-- gated-on:540f --> <!-- id:554b -->

Downstream damage: each 404 produced a handback reading `integrate.sh produced no merged= line (unparseable integrator output)`, which reads like an integrator PARSING bug and sent this session's first analysis hunting one — the misleading-reason cost is real, not hypothetical (see id:2c2a's correction). A per-hop shape check remains the missing assertion. **ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-26 (delegated diagnosis, claims independently re-verified).** The rejecting rule is `mechanical-proxy.py:578` — `if "$(" in command or "`" in command or "<(" in command or ">(" in command: return False` — a BARE SUBSTRING scan with NO quote-awareness, unlike its siblings `_has_unquoted_sequence_operator` / `_has_unquoted_redirection`. relay-loop.js embeds the executor's FREE-TEXT `--summary` (and `--label`) as a single-quoted shell argument in the integrate hop's fenced command. Executor summaries routinely contain MARKDOWN BACKTICKS — the two live failures were git-annex's `added `toc` subcommand` and lean4btc's `` `lake exe bench` `` — and a backtick inside single quotes is fully inert to real bash, but line 578 refuses on its mere presence. **So ANY unit whose summary happens to quote a command name 404s its own integrate.** This explains the apparent intermittency: git-annex integrated FINE at 13:09 and 14:03 with differently-worded summaries, and failed only when its summary contained a backtick — it is content-dependent, not repo-dependent, so it will recur fleet-wide at an unpredictable rate. **A quote-aware fix was implemented, tested, and then REVERTED** because it broke `tests/test_mech_stdin_channel_33b2.sh:77-78` (id:a05c, owner-ratified 'Option B'), which explicitly asserts that even a SAFELY single-quoted backtick/`$(` must stay refused — the predicate is deliberately paranoid and the ratified answer for 'a hop needs to carry free-text data' is the separate `relay-mech-stdin` payload channel (`STDIN_ALLOWED_SCRIPTS`), NOT loosening `_command_allowed()`. That decision STANDS; `mechanical-proxy.py` is byte-identical to its committed state. The fix therefore belongs on the EMITTING side (relay-loop.js), and its direction is an owner call — see the A/B options recorded below. <!-- id:2e7a -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Route the integrate hop's FREE-TEXT fields through the `relay-mech-stdin` payload channel instead of inline shell args** (owner decision 2026-08-26: sanitize now, migrate durably — this is the durable half; the sanitize half landed as `17b4e4e0`). `mechArg()` now neutralises backtick / `$(` / `<(` / `>(` so a markdown-backticked executor summary can no longer 404 its own integrate (id:2e7a root cause). That unblocks the pool but is explicitly a WORKAROUND: the structural problem is that free-text prose is embedded as a shell argument at all, so **the next free-text field added to a fenced command reintroduces the bug** — and it will fail the same way, silently failing OPEN to the real API and 404ing on `model:"bash"`, which reads as an unrelated integrator-parsing bug (it cost this session's first analysis a wrong diagnosis). The RATIFIED answer already exists: `relay-mech-stdin` / `STDIN_ALLOWED_SCRIPTS` (id:a05c 'Option B'), the channel created precisely so a hop can carry free-text data without loosening `_command_allowed()`. `relay-status-publish.sh` already uses it — copy that pattern. **Scope:** (a) confirm `integrate.sh` treats stdin as INERT DATA (never evals/sources it) — that is the standing obligation on every `STDIN_ALLOWED_SCRIPTS` member and MUST be verified, not assumed, before adding it; (b) add `integrate.sh` to `STDIN_ALLOWED_SCRIPTS`; (c) emit `--summary`/`--label` via the stdin fence in `relay-loop.js`. **Keep the mechArg sanitisation as defence-in-depth** even after this lands — a future caller that forgets the channel then degrades to cosmetic loss instead of a silent 404. **Do NOT loosen `_command_allowed()`** — that was attempted 2026-08-26 and reverted; it breaks `tests/test_mech_stdin_channel_33b2.sh`, and the paranoia is the contract, not the defect. <!-- id:76fd -->

- [ ] [HARD — meeting] **Mid-run scope change: `--exclude` / `--priority` (and `--only`) against an ALREADY-RUNNING pool** (owner-requested 2026-07-31, directly out of the id:31ce incident) — today all three are **launch-time only**: the front door folds them into `args.excludeRepos` / `args.priorityRepos` / `args.onlyRepo` and `relay-loop.js` applies them at discovery. Once a pool is live there is **no supported way to say "stop touching repo X" or "do repo Y first"**. The owner hit this on 2026-07-31: he asked to exclude lodelore mid-run, and the only options were (a) graceful-stop and relaunch — which cost a round and then failed anyway because the stop was stolen (id:31ce), or (b) hand-hold a `claim.sh` lease on the repo so every child aborts at the `relay-loop.js:1956` acquire. **(b) is a real but leaky workaround worth recording**: it costs a wasted child dispatch per round (the child spawns, fails the acquire, hands back), and it silently lapses after `CLAIM_TTL` (1800 s) unless the worktree carries commits. Net effect on the day: lodelore was re-dispatched `mode:hard` at 18:08 and integrated at 18:19, ~25 min after the owner asked for it to be left alone. **What exists and does NOT solve it**: `/relay inject` (id:354f) enqueues a unit consumed by the next discovery round — so *a* mid-run lever already exists and the plumbing (an inbox the prelude drains each round) is the obvious substrate — but inject **creates** a unit rather than reordering a naturally-discovered one, which is explicitly NOT what `--priority` means (id:d530 is careful that priority "creates no unit and can never double-dispatch"), and there is no exclude-shaped counterpart at all. **Design questions for the meeting, not settled here**: (1) does mid-run scope ride the existing inject inbox (one more record kind the prelude drains) or a separate scope-override file the prelude reads each round — the former reuses tested plumbing, the latter keeps "what to work" and "what not to work" from sharing a consume path; (2) **what happens to a unit already dispatched to a now-excluded repo** — let it finish and integrate (cheap, but the owner asked for it to STOP), or abort and park the worktree (respects intent, costs the work and risks a dirty tree); (3) does a mid-run exclude persist for the rest of the run only, matching `--exclude`'s deliberate never-writes-relay.toml scoping (id:d530's rationale: a registry mutation surviving a session-kill is a silent permanent exclusion); (4) whether this should just be **`/relay stop --run <id>` + relaunch with new flags**, now that the stop is aimable (id:cd94) — the cheapest answer, and possibly the right one, since a relaunch re-reads the ledger anyway and loses nothing but a round. Weigh (4) seriously before building anything: it may dissolve the item. <!-- id:4823 -->

## relay reconcile 2026-07-30 (a NINTH stale literal, hidden by expected-red)

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **A NINTH file carries the stale `model:'bash'` literal, and it was invisible because it is EXPECTED-RED — the real lesson is that expected-red can mask a failure unrelated to why the file is red** — `id:362f` was ticked after the eight named files were migrated, but its count was wrong. **`tests/test_roadmap_scope_table_consistency_c480.sh:59`** does `grep -E "label: *\`release:" "$LOOP" | grep -qE "model: *'bash'"` as a **PRECONDITION**, carrying exactly the same stale literal `490ac6e` replaced with `MECH_MODEL` everywhere else. **Why nobody saw it:** `id:c480` is unticked, so the harness reports the file `EXPECTED-RED`, its failure never counts, it never appears in the `failed:` list, and it never drew an eye — including mine, across three full-suite runs today that I read as clean. **THE HAZARD IS NOT THE STALE GREP.** It is that an expected-red file can fail for a reason having nothing to do with why it is red, and the harness cannot distinguish the two. This one now dies at its precondition with a FALSE alarm — *"no 'release:'-labelled model:'bash' dispatch in relay-loop.js — id:f7d3 appears to have been reverted"* — which is wrong (f7d3 was not reverted; `490ac6e` moved that hop to `MECH_MODEL`), and it fires BEFORE the test exercises the behaviour it exists to spec. So whoever implements `id:c480` will meet a failure unrelated to their work, and red-is-the-spec quietly stops holding for that item. **Two pieces of work, and the second is the valuable one:** (a) ~~apply the same substitution as the other eight (accept `MECH_MODEL` at the dispatch site)~~ **— (a) DONE 2026-07-31** (commit `263b9f4`): the §1 precondition now accepts EITHER a literal `model: 'bash'` OR `model: MECH_MODEL` at the `release:`-labelled dispatch, and still fails on a genuine f7d3 revert (a literal `model:'haiku'`, or no mechanical dispatch at all). With it unblocked the file reached its real assertions, the orphan was integrated (`relay-ckpt-20260731-1147`) and **id:c480 is now closed and GREEN 6/6** — so this file is no longer expected-red at all. **(b) IS THE REMAINING WORK and is the owner's call:** decide whether `tests/run-tests.sh` should distinguish *"red for its own roadmap item"* from *"red for an unrelated reason"* — a file dying at a PRECONDITION is a different animal from one whose assertions are legitimately unmet, and today the harness calls both `EXPECTED-RED`. A cheap first cut: require an expected-red file to fail at an ASSERTION, and surface a precondition/setup failure as a real failure even when its roadmap item is open. **HOW IT WAS FOUND, which also matters:** trial-merging the parked orphan `relay/orphan/relay-20260729-142725-13077-execute` (a 2026-07-29 context-death salvage) into a scratch worktree. **That branch CONTAINS the `id:c480` implementation** — 130 lines of SCOPE-TABLE-DRIFT logic for `roadmap-lint.sh` that main does not have — so main holds c480's SPEC and the orphan holds its IMPLEMENTATION, and the two had never met (the branch is 34 commits behind main and predates the spec). The salvage therefore could not be verified and was PARKED, not merged. Fixing (a) is the prerequisite to verifying and then integrating that orphan — see `relay-reconcile.sh --integrate`. Relates id:362f (which this amends), id:c480, id:4239, id:1f8e (why the orphan was never parked in the first place: `worktree-retire.sh` is absent from `ALLOWED_RELAY_SCRIPTS`, so the dead run's retire hop could not run). <!-- children-of:362f --> <!-- id:6a15 -->

PROBLEM: a status claim written as prose into a durable/cross-repo ledger is true when written and false soon after, but keeps being read as current. - [ ] [HARD] [INBOUND routed:99f3 from loderite 2026-07-30] **LSP is RECOMMENDED by executor-contract rule 5c but its failure mode is a SILENT FALSE NEGATIVE — the contract must never let a negative LSP result stand as evidence of absence** (the index-corruption CAUSE is id:03a1; this is about the CONTRACT's treatment of LSP results and its cost claims, separable and applicable even with a healthy index). **Obs 1 — a negative is not an absence, and is indistinguishable from one.** `findReferences` on `setActiveInputModeSource` (`src/editor-core.ts:381`) returned *"No references found. The ~600-tok figure evidently came from a small flat file; cost scales with nesting depth and function count, not just length. **Fix:** re-scope 5c — `documentSymbol` for "what is the shape of this unfamiliar file", `grep -n` for "where is symbol X", `goToDefinition` for "where is this defined"; drop or re-measure the 5-6x claim and state that it degrades on large/deeply-nested files. So position LSP as a cheap HINT that must be corroborated before it decides anything, never as an authority. Relates id:6f1c (rule 5c itself), id:03a1, id:c74e. <!-- id:5e9c -->

## pool silent-exclusion cluster 2026-08-10 (found investigating "1 unit across 55 repos")

- [ ] [ROUTINE] 🔴 **`roadmap-lint`'s DEAD-GATE check INVERTS its diagnosis for an archived-and-TICKED gate, and its recommended remedy destroys a correct dependency edge** — found 2026-08-10 reconciling this repo's lint output against a parallel session's `id:1f8e` work. **The disagreement, both verified by command:** `resolve-gates.sh:36` resolves gate tokens over `ROADMAP.md ∪ TODO.md ∪ TODO.archive.md` (its `:31` comment states this deliberately — "the executor gate must see a resolution in the archive"), so a gate whose id is `- [x]` in the archive is **SATISFIED**. `roadmap-lint.sh` instead reports `DEAD-GATE … it is RETIRED — archived in TODO.archive.md and not a ROADMAP item, so the gate is PERMANENT and can never open; drop or re-target the marker (id:49e0)`. **Live case**: open item `id:2b49` is `gated-on:ac7f`; `ac7f` is `- [x]` at `TODO.archive.md:428` (the single `id:ac7f` hit in `TODO.md` is not an ac7f item — it is 2b49's own gate marker on line 264). So 2b49's gate is **already open** and the item is a ready-to-run `[HARD — meeting]`, while lint has been reporting it as permanently blocked. **Why this is worse than a noisy warning:** the remedy it prescribes is to DROP the marker. Following it deletes a satisfied, correct provenance edge and converts a resolvable dependency into no dependency at all — the lint actively recommends data loss. It also inflates the DEAD-GATE count that `relay-doctor` surfaces, training the reader to ignore the class. **The same false positive already produced a wrong recommendation in this repo's own REVIEW_ME** (Review 2026-08-10 box, since corrected). **Fix**: make `roadmap-lint` use the SAME resolution span as `resolve-gates.sh` — ideally by calling it rather than reimplementing the lookup (two implementations of one predicate is the drift that caused this). Distinguish three states, never conflating them: gate **satisfied** (ticked anywhere in the span → not a warning at all, and the item may be READY — worth surfacing positively); gate **open** (untricked and present → normal); gate **unresolvable** (id exists nowhere in the span → the only genuine DEAD-GATE). The `id:540f`/`id:c179` warnings are a DIFFERENT and possibly-legitimate case (gate `b0b1` lives only in `TODO.md`, never promoted) — do not fold them into this fix without re-checking them separately. Relates id:49e0 (the DEAD-GATE check), id:46f6 (typed edges), id:eb63 (sibling: done-but-unticked items are not detected either — same "ledger state is not what the tooling believes" family). — **SCOPE SET 2026-08-18 (meeting `docs/meeting-notes/2026-08-18-1052-meeting-backlog-selector-948c-788f.md`, D3 as AMENDED).** This item now carries the narrow gate fix, and the meeting's first ratification ("roadmap-lint consumes resolve-gates") was **WITHDRAWN** as broader than this defect and contradicting it. **Do NOT merge the two tools:** `roadmap-lint.sh:348-354` documents the three-map split deliberately and names `resolve-gates.sh` as "correctly" merging for "its own, different question" — resolve-gates answers *is this dispatchable now* (satisfaction), the DEAD-GATE rule answers *can this gate ever open through the execution queue* (location). Merging erases the never-promoted class, which is LIVE (`d4ca`→`09e4`, `e405`→`09e4`, `540f`→`b0b1`, `c179`→`b0b1`). **The actual root cause, verified:** `roadmap-lint.sh:532` tests archive-map EXISTENCE (`${RL_GATE_ARCHIVE[$_dg_t]+x}`) and never the stored checkbox STATE — and since `archive-done.sh` archives only `[x]` items, essentially EVERY archive hit is a false PERMANENT verdict (`2b49`, `540f`, `c179` today, not just the one). **Fix:** share the satisfaction predicate/state-map (ticked-anywhere-in-span ⇒ SATISFIED, never a warning); KEEP the three-way location taxonomy. **Acceptance:** a fixture whose gate target is `[x]` in `TODO.archive.md` yields SATISFIED with no warning, AND a fixture whose target lives only in `TODO.md` still yields the never-promoted warning — assert BOTH, since a positive-only test passes against a lint that warns on nothing. **Also files here (not under id:7877):** the resolve-gates-vs-roadmap-lint disagreement is "two persistent implementations of one predicate drifting", which this item already names. **AMENDED 2026-08-18 (`/relay human .`, action item 2 of meeting `2026-08-18-1052`; carries D3 as AMENDED, which SUPERSEDES that meeting's first ratification).** The withdrawn wording made `resolve-gates.sh` the source of truth with `roadmap-lint` consuming it; that is **not** the decision — the two tools answer different questions by documented design (resolve-gates: *is this dispatchable now* / satisfaction; DEAD-GATE: *can this gate ever open through the execution queue* / location), and consuming one from the other would erase the never-promoted class that is live today (`d4ca`→`09e4`, `e405`→`09e4`, `540f`→`b0b1`, `c179`→`b0b1`). **The amended fix is NARROW:** share the satisfaction predicate/state-map (ticked-anywhere-in-span ⇒ SATISFIED, never a warning) and KEEP roadmap-lint's three-way location taxonomy. **Root cause, re-verified in code 2026-08-18:** `roadmap-lint.sh:532` tests archive-map *existence* via a `+x` parameter-expansion test, never the stored checkbox *state* — and since `archive-done.sh` only ever archives `[x]` items, essentially every archive hit yields a false PERMANENT verdict. **Acceptance (BOTH directions, or the test is vacuous):** a fixture whose gate target is `[x]` in `TODO.archive.md` yields SATISFIED with NO warning, AND a target living only in `TODO.md` still yields the never-promoted warning — a positive-only test passes against a lint that warns on nothing. **OWNER DECISION 2026-08-22 (`/relay human`, REVIEW_ME.md tier (b)) — this item now ALSO owns the DEAD-GATE check's ledger-scope bug, and the chosen fix is to change the CHECK, not the ledger.** `roadmap-lint.sh` reports DEAD-GATE for an open ROADMAP item whose `gated-on:` target lives only in `TODO.md`, reasoning that "nothing in ROADMAP.md can ever clear the gate". But `resolve-gates.sh:36` already resolves gates against `ROADMAP.md ∪ TODO.md ∪ TODO.archive.md` — so such a gate IS resolvable, and the two tools simply disagree about what the resolution set is. Make lint agree with the resolver. That clears all four live WARNs (`d4ca`, `e405`, `540f`, `c179` — all gated on `09e4`/`b0b1`) without touching a single gate marker. The alternative (promote `09e4` + `b0b1` into ROADMAP) was explicitly REJECTED: `b0b1` is a deliberate OWNER gate, and promoting it would put it in the execution queue's line of sight. **Routing correction made while filing this:** the REVIEW_ME box AND `roadmap-lint.sh`'s own WARN text both tell the reader to resolve this via `id:49e0` — but `id:49e0` is `- [x]` CLOSED and archived (`TODO.archive.md:515`, `ROADMAP.archive.md:3488`), so that pointer is dead. Fix the WARN string's `(id:49e0)` reference to name this item in the same change, or the next reader is sent to an archived item again. <!-- id:8de9 -->

The trap is CIRCULAR, not missing: the only channel that publishes the counter is a SUCCESSFUL status write, so when the failing hop IS the status write, its own failure can only appear if a LATER status write succeeds. If they keep failing, the file stays frozen at its last good state — `agent-failures=0`, no gap, no marker — and reads as current. So the fix is not "wire it up" but "give the status-write failure a channel that does not depend on the status write": e.g. append a `status-write-refused` event to `relay-events.jsonl` (already append-only and independently written), and/or have the NEXT successful write render a Blocked row naming the gap. (2) **`MECH_FALLBACK='fallback-haiku'` (mode-a, no proxy)** leaves `MECH_MODEL='haiku'`, so the payload still crosses a model and the classifier exposure remains in that mode only. **Reporter's verification is worth preserving**: the classifier's accusation was checked and found FALSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — all five claimed checkpoint tags exist (`relay-ckpt-20260818-2103/2113/2132/2137/2146`), the ids it called invented are real closed+archived ROADMAP items, and the Workflow demonstrably ran (103 agents, 6 rounds, suite 78/78). Compounds `id:0f9e`. <!-- routed:1f32 --> <!-- id:a8a4 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] [INBOUND routed:c3f7 from csgebra 2026-08-18] **`todo-conformance.sh --fix` mints a DUPLICATE id on a multi-line TODO item whose `<!-- id:XXXX -->` sits on any line but the first** — it reads the item's first line only, sees no id, and appends a freshly-minted one, so the item ends up carrying two. This is the exact P1/P2 duplicate-id anti-pattern the relay guards against, produced by the tool meant to prevent it, and it fires silently under `--fix` (reported as a normal "auto-fixed N missing-id item(s)"). **Minimal repro**: two-item `TODO.md` where item 2 spans 3 lines with its id on the last → `--fix` injects a second id onto line 1. **Observed 2026-08-18** on csgebra's 4D north-star item (already `id:0502`, got `id:02b4` appended); reverted by hand. **Fix direction**: scan the whole item block (up to the next checkbox/heading) for an id before classifying it missing-id, matching how `resolve-gates`/`lib-typed-edges` anchor on comment markers. Note the "own id is the LAST id-comment" convention when picking which id wins. <!-- routed:c3f7 --> <!-- id:ee2e -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] [INBOUND routed:83cf from csgebra 2026-08-18] **The relay front door's EXIT-trap teardown (`id:54be`) assumes a PERSISTENT SHELL front door and silently does nothing when the front door is a Claude SESSION — so `heartbeat.sh stop` + `claim.sh release --run` never fire on their own** — SKILL.md step 3b specifies `trap _relay_exit_teardown EXIT` installed in the front-door shell "immediately after minting `$RUN_ID` and before invoking the Workflow", with the explicit rationale that it must fire whether the Workflow RETURNS or DIES, because "a stderr line is the only signal left when the Workflow is SIGKILLed". But when the orchestrator is a Claude session, each Bash tool call is its OWN shell: a trap installed in the call that mints `RUN_ID` is gone before the Workflow tool is even invoked, and the Workflow runs in the harness, not under that shell. The trap therefore protects NOTHING in the session-driven path — which is the NORMAL path for every `/relay` a human types. **Observed 2026-08-18** (run `relay-20260818-200205-25179`, csgebra): the model had to run both teardown actions manually as an explicit post-step; had the session been killed mid-run, the run's heartbeat marker and every lease it held would have been left to expire on TTL alone, with no stderr line and no RELAY_STATUS row — exactly the SIGKILL case the trap was designed for. This is the `id:98f0` outage-watchdog's blind spot too, since a stale heartbeat is what it keys on. **Fix shapes**: move the two teardown actions into a small wrapper SCRIPT the front door invokes (so one shell spans mint→launch→teardown and the trap is real); or have the Workflow itself register its teardown so it is independent of the caller's shell lifetime; or make SKILL.md state plainly that in a session-driven front door the trap is inert and the two actions MUST be run as an explicit post-step. <!-- routed:83cf --> <!-- id:b4e8 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] [INBOUND routed:b1e9 from csgebra 2026-08-18] **The relay integrator ticks the ROADMAP checkbox but NOT the TODO twin, so every closed item leaves cross-ledger drift that only a separate backstop scan reports** — the single-id-two-views invariant (D2) is asserted but never maintained. **Observed 2026-08-18**, csgebra run `relay-20260818-200205-25179`: after three items closed, `orphan-scan.sh --cross-ledger` reported all three as `TODO:[ ] ROADMAP:[x] (checkbox state disagrees across ledgers)`; the TODO mirror line `- [ ] Relay: N open ROADMAP items` had also drifted (said 15, actual 12). All four fixed by hand. The fact that `orphan-scan --cross-ledger` EXISTS as a backstop concedes the drift is expected rather than prevented — but a backstop that only reports leaves the ledgers disagreeing until a human happens to run it, and TODO.md is the DESIGN ledger a human reads first, so it is the one that misleads. The integrator already writes to the main checkout at this point (the `id:15d5` path: `chore(roadmap): tick worked items` + `chore(roadmap): archive done items`), so it holds the lease and the context — ticking the twin is the same write, one file over, with the ids already in hand from `worked_ids`. **Fix shapes**: extend the integrator's existing tick commit to also flip the TODO twin via the flock'd `meeting/md-merge.py update-ids` (line-scoped, the sanctioned concurrent-safe path) and recompute the mirror count; or leave the write manual but make `orphan-scan --cross-ledger` run automatically at end-of-run and SURFACE the drift in RELAY_STATUS.md; or drop the TODO twin's checkbox entirely and let TODO reference ROADMAP state instead of duplicating it. <!-- routed:b1e9 --> <!-- id:3652 -->

- [ ] [INPUT — decision] [INBOUND routed:1385 from csgebra 2026-08-18] **`@owner-gated` is a DISPATCH exclusion but not a ROUTING exclusion — `unpromoted-scan.sh` honours neither the `@owner-gated` marker nor the `id:356f` parked-section heading vocabulary, so a deliberately parked item keeps generating the `human` verdict through the back door** — `hard-lanes.md` (`id:7517`) states `@owner-gated` IS a dispatch exclusion and names the predicates that carry it (`gather-repo-state.sh`, `classify-repo.sh`, …); `unpromoted-scan.sh` is not among them and sources no section lib — its ONLY suppression is a decision-queue record. But its output feeds the routing chain: an untagged open TODO item with no ROADMAP twin scans as `surface`, and `surface>0 ∧ promote==0` emits verdict `human`, filing the item for human lane-triage. **Observed 2026-08-18** on csgebra `id:0502`, a 4D-CSG north-star item whose own text says "NOT scheduled, NOT a dependency, reopen only as a deliberate new scoping session": adding `@owner-gated` left it scanning `surface`; ALSO renaming its heading to carry `deferred` (a `ROADMAP_PARKED_HEADING_WORDS` token) left it scanning `surface`; only a resolved decision-queue record with disposition parked/not-an-item suppressed it. So the designed escape hatch works, but it is undiscoverable: the two markers a reader would REACH FOR both silently no-op, and nothing says so. **This may be intended design** (the marker's contract names only the dispatch predicates), hence the decision lane. **Fix shapes (owner decides)**: have `unpromoted-scan.sh` consume the ALREADY-EXPORTED `ROADMAP_PARKED_HEADING_VOCAB`/`ROADMAP_PARKED_HEADING_MARKERS` from `lib-roadmap-sections.sh` (cheap, one source, no new vocabulary); or leave the behaviour and document in `hard-lanes.md` that parking a TODO item requires a decision-queue record, naming `@owner-gated` and parked headings as explicitly NOT sufficient there. <!-- routed:1385 --> <!-- id:16bf -->

## strong-model audit 2026-08-11 (Run 70, id:401c — meeting note `docs/meeting-notes/2026-08-11-2039-strong-model-audit.md`)

- [ ] [HARD] **A strong-EXECUTE checkpoint advances `last_strong_ckpt`, silently starving the recurring strong-model audit (id:401c) — the id:ecce integrate-carve-out was left half-closed** — `relay/scripts/ckpt-tag.sh`'s watermark logic skips advancing the strong-audit watermark only for `integrate*` (id:ecce) and for model-less `executor*`/`reconcile*` labels. But a `strong-execute (claude-opus-4-8, …)` checkpoint carries a FULL `claude-*` id and is not `integrate*`, so it falls into the `else` branch and advances `last_strong_ckpt` to HEAD — even though a strong-execute child does red-green-refactor on ONE item and performs NO audit (no test-integrity check, no spec-drift, no roadmap re-derivation, no cross-cutting coherence review). The code's own comment already classifies `strong-execute` as "a defect: warn and name it", but that branch is only reached for model-LESS labels. **Observed impact**: the last actual id:401c audit was Run 69 (2026-06-30); every strong-execute/reviewer close since re-pinned `last_strong_ckpt` to HEAD, so id:401c's window has read ~0 for ~6 weeks / 1709 commits (`gather-repo-state.sh substantive_unaudited`=false), and the pass has not fired. The ROADMAP id:401c Run log (stops at Run 4) is a secondary symptom. **Fix direction (owner/reviewer to ratify — mirrors id:c500's reconcile ratification)**: make the carve-out an ALLOWLIST — only `reviewer*` advances the strong-audit watermark; `strong-execute*`/`integrate*`/`reconcile*`/anything-else skips. RED test: plant a `strong-execute (claude-opus-4-8)` label → assert `last_strong_ckpt` unchanged; keep the `reviewer (claude-*)` → advances assertion green. NOT fixed inline in Run 70 by design: (a) fleet-wide watermark-semantics change is the owner's call; (b) self-certification trap — a strong-execute child editing `ckpt-tag.sh` would, under the current bug, mark its own unreviewed change AUDITED. Relates id:ecce, id:c500, id:0a3b, id:365b, id:401c. <!-- id:da95 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`disjoint-greenlight.sh` judges path-sets disjoint by exact-string equality, so a directory-vs-subpath overlap is fail-OPEN in a guard advertised "FAIL-CLOSED"** — `plan` keys a `declare -A seen` on each declared path and flags overlap only on an exact repeat (`disjoint-greenlight.sh:74`); `merge-check` intersects touched-vs-merged by exact line (`:113/:119`), and `drain-integrate.sh` (id:2062) re-enforces via the same `merge-check`, inheriting the blind spot. Two concurrent units with declared sets `{"relay/scripts/"}` and `{"relay/scripts/relay-loop.js"}` (or `{"a/b"}` vs `{"a/b/c"}`) are greenlit "concurrent" despite containment. Both scripts are built-but-UNWIRED (id:ae08 is the wiring child), so this is a latent gap to close before they go live, not an active incident. Severity is bounded by an unverified premise (hence tracked, not urgent): the hole only bites if a declared/touched file-set can contain a directory path — `git diff --name-only` emits leaf files, but the seam `file:` declarations `plan` consumes are not asserted leaf-only anywhere. **Resolve alongside id:ae08**: either (a) document + enforce a leaf-file-only contract on declared sets (reject a directory/extensionless declared path, fail-closed on ambiguity) — smaller and more fail-closed — or (b) make disjointness containment-aware (prefix-normalize sets, treat `a/b` vs `a/b/c` as overlapping). Relates id:5367, id:2062, id:ae08, id:1f4f. <!-- gated-on:ae08 --> <!-- id:ac8a -->

## strong-model audit 2026-08-11 (Run 71, id:401c — meeting note `docs/meeting-notes/2026-08-11-2145-strong-model-audit.md`)

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **The id:33b2 opt-in stdin channel silently MISDIRECTS its payload when the admitted script is a non-leading pipeline stage** — `_mechanical_dispatch` admits a `relay-mech-stdin` fence whenever `_last_stage_relay_script(command)` (the LAST pipeline stage's pinned script) is in `STDIN_ALLOWED_SCRIPTS`, but `_run_mechanical` feeds the payload via `subprocess.run([bash,'-c',command], input=stdin)` — which reaches the SHELL process's stdin, i.e. the FIRST stage of a pipeline, not the last. So a command like `echo x | relay-status-publish.sh` (both `echo` and the admitted script pass `_command_allowed`) with a stdin fence would send the payload to `echo` (which ignores it) while the admitted script reads the pipe (`x`), NOT the payload — a silent wrong-bytes delivery. **NOT an active vuln / LOW**: the command is caller-constructed by `relay-loop.js` (trusted) and the only admitted member (`relay-status-publish.sh`) is invoked bare, never piped; nothing dangerous runs and no data leaks — the payload is merely lost. But it is LATENT: the design intent is documented as "the command stays a single bare allowlisted script invocation", and the gate does not enforce that shape, so the moment an admitted script is used downstream of a pipe its stdin silently receives the wrong bytes. **Fix**: when a `relay-mech-stdin` fence is present, require the command to be a SINGLE stage (no unquoted `|`) — refuse (fail open, log `mechanical_stdin_refused` with reason `stdin fence on a multi-stage pipeline`) otherwise; a bare admitted invocation is the only shape that delivers stdin correctly. RED test: a `relay-mech-stdin` fence on `echo x | relay-status-publish.sh` (admitted last stage) → `_mechanical_dispatch` returns None; the bare-invocation case stays green. Relates id:33b2, id:a05c, id:6b35, id:f9cd. <!-- id:09e4 -->

So: auto-GENERATE the index from the scripts (e.g. parse a standard header/usage line out of each `scripts/*.sh`) and/or a test that fails when a script lacks an index entry — never a hand-kept list. Backlog until that guarantee is designed; link, don't build. Relates id:23fe (deterministic scanner), id:2840 (md-SSOT + derived cache, md wins). <!-- id:10a6 -->
