- [ ] [INBOUND routed:d6be from loderite hand-run 2026-07-17] MECHANIZE the relay's ROLE boundaries with a pre-commit hook instead of prompt-prose (user 2026-07-17: 'a pre-commit hook that rejects RED-specs (or any test modifications) by non-apex agents, and similarly permits executors to only not modify ROADMAP etc — part of the whole permissions complex and maybe easier than the separate users approach'). TODAY'S EVIDENCE THIS IS NEEDED: the relay enforces every role boundary by PROSE ('do not weaken tests to pass', 'tick only if genuinely green', 'never push', 'work in your worktree') — i.e. pure LLM judgment, exactly what CLAUDE.md's mechanize-first rule says to replace. Observed 2026-07-17 in one session: (a) the ORCHESTRATOR collapsed handoff into execute by telling execute children to author their own RED tests — a self-authored spec proves only that the code does what its author decided; caught by the OWNER, by nothing mechanical; (b) 5 of 6 children edited the MAIN checkout instead of their worktree (the id:c6c8 jobAI incident was an actual COMMIT to a target's real main — a pre-commit hook IN the main checkout rejecting commits whose branch/env marks them a relay child kills that whole class); (c) id:4c84 ticked its ROADMAP box while its function was DEAD CODE. THE TIER SIGNAL ALREADY EXISTS — no new plumbing: the branch name encodes the verdict (relay/<runId>-execute-<id> vs -handoff vs -hard), so the hook can read $(git branch --show-current) and apply per-role rules; belt-and-braces via a RELAY_TIER env var. CANDIDATE RULES: execute ⇒ MAY NOT modify tests/ (the RED spec IS the contract it must satisfy, not edit) and MAY NOT rewrite ROADMAP entries; handoff ⇒ MAY write tests/+ROADMAP, MAY NOT touch src/ (it must not implement); review ⇒ MAY write REVIEW_ME/ledgers, MAY NOT touch src/. ***THE HARD PART — a real counterexample from the SAME session, do not design without it***: id:a78b's ENTIRE JOB was to re-pin a wrong test fixture, because the ROADMAP's own prescription ('re-pin to an octant-masked-cell fixture') was FACTUALLY WRONG (octant cut faces are irregular pentagons + right triangles, never rectangles; only octant CUBE PAIRS give literal squares). The Sonnet executor correctly deviated from the spec, modified tests, and was RIGHT — a blanket 'executors may not touch tests' would have BLOCKED a legitimate correct fix. So the rule needs a deliberate escape hatch (an explicit marker commit? a flag that FORCES a review unit? allow-with-loud-surface rather than reject?) — design it, do not just ban. SIMILARLY the ROADMAP rule cannot be a blanket ban: executor contract rule 2 REQUIRES the child to tick its own box, so the hook needs LINE-SCOPED logic (may flip [ ]→[x] on its OWN id's line; may not rewrite the entry or touch another item's line). WHAT A HOOK CANNOT CATCH (say so up front, do not oversell): id:4c84's spec defect (Acceptance vs Done-check disagreeing — a semantic mismatch); and id:e02a's role-collapse, since apex is MECHANICALLY permitted to do everything and the failure was that it did. VS THE SEPARATE-USERS APPROACH (the user's own framing — 'maybe easier'): agreed it is far lighter (no sudo, no user management, works per-worktree, no ownership churn on shared node_modules/caches) — but name the trade honestly: a hook is BYPASSABLE (git commit --no-verify) so it is guarded by prose again at the last inch, whereas Unix file permissions cannot be talked out of. Hook+prose still strictly beats prose alone, and is reversible; consider it the observe-first step (CLAUDE.md observe-before-preventing) and let the separate-users build be gated on the hook's log showing real firings. Relates id:1735 (self-reported summaries), routed:8adf (isolation:c6c8 rescope), routed:6fd5 (orchestrator self-implementation), the D3 anti-gaming invariant, CLAUDE.md mechanize-first + no-silent-swallow. **CONSOLIDATED 2026-07-19 (meeting `docs/meeting-notes/2026-07-19-1212-git-hook-enforcement-substrate-reconciliation.md`):** this is the **SINGLE relay provenance engine** — id:7a05's provenance-of-tick and id:0c86's executor-no-own-RED detector fold in HERE (one branch/tier read, not three parallel hooks). 077d supplies the L2 role-boundary/provenance checks that **plug into the id:7a05 git-hook framework** (L0 install + L1 dispatch), rather than building its own install path. <!-- id:077d -->

- [ ] [INBOUND routed:683a from lodelore] **Relay worktree creation should support a per-repo SEED HOOK for big derived caches (CoW/reflink where the filesystem allows).** `git worktree add` gives a relay child an empty tree for everything gitignored, so any repo with an expensive derived cache makes every child pay a full cold rebuild. Concrete measured case (lodelore, 2026-08-10): `lean/.lake` is **1.9 GB** of Mathlib; `~/src` and `~/.cache` are both btrfs on the same device (`/dev/nvme0n1p2[/@home]`), so `cp --reflink=auto -a <main>/lean/.lake <worktree>/lean/.lake` is near-instant and near-zero space, versus a cold `lake exe cache get` + build per child. GENERALISES well beyond Lean — `node_modules`, uv/venv trees, Rust `target/`, model/index caches — which is why the hook belongs in relay's worktree-creation path rather than in each repo's own scripts. SHAPE: after `git worktree add`, if `<repo>/.relay-worktree-seed.sh` (or a `relay.toml` key) exists, run it with the worktree path; repos without one are unaffected. GUARDS THAT MATTER: `--reflink=always` FAILS on non-CoW filesystems while `--reflink=auto` SILENTLY degrades to a real full copy — for a 1.9 GB cache that is worse than doing nothing, so the hook must detect same-filesystem + CoW support and skip loudly otherwise, never silently duplicate. And **a reflink is a SNAPSHOT, not a live link** (recorded lens, mathematical-writing 2026-07-10 lean-toolchain-pin-ownership): a seeded cache goes stale when the pin moves, so the contract must be "seed, then let the repo's own freshness check re-derive", never "seed and assume fresh". Related: lodelore id:eb79 builds the repo-local half (`lean/scripts/worktree-seed.sh`); this item is the generic relay-side hook only. **TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS from relay-core's id:51c2 build (2026-08-11) — read before implementing.** (1) **The CoW-detection heuristic in the lodelore reference is wrong and would be inherited here.** It requires `fstype == btrfs && same st_dev`; measured live, `cp --reflink=always` from `/@home` to `/@` — two subvolumes of ONE btrfs with DIFFERENT `st_dev` — succeeds, so the `st_dev` test falsely refuses a working case. Use a live one-file `cp --reflink=always` probe instead: definitive, and it also covers `nodatacow` and non-btrfs CoW filesystems. Copy with `--reflink=always` (never `auto`) so failure is always loud. (2) **The per-repo payoff is not uniform, so the hook must not assume it.** relay-core's cold rebuild — the thing seeding avoids — measures **1.78 s** (zero external requires; the 104 MB is a static binary + IR that regenerates immediately), so the CPU saving there is ~1.4 s, essentially noise. The real saving is **disk: ~104 MB exclusive per concurrent worktree** (verified by `btrfs filesystem du -s`: seeded `.lake` 0 B exclusive vs 103.67 MiB for a cold-built one). lodelore's 1.9 GB Mathlib is large on both axes; relay-core is large on only one. Whether a given repo opts in is therefore a per-repo judgement, which argues for the `.relay-worktree-seed.sh`-presence shape already proposed above rather than any fleet-wide default. **UN-BUNDLED from relay-core `id:51c2` — owner call, `/relay human` 2026-08-11 (routed:ca4d)**: relay-core closed its half and will NOT opt in, so it is **not a blocked consumer** of this item and must not be cited as one. `7902` proceeds justified by lodelore's 1.9 GB Mathlib case ALONE (large on both the CPU and disk axes); relay-core's numbers quoted above (1.78 s cold rebuild = CPU noise, ~104 MB/worktree disk only) stand as evidence for the per-repo-judgement shape, not as a second consumer waiting on it. <!-- routed:ca4d --> <!-- id:7902 -->

Pipe the payload below verbatim ... do not retry or write any file yourself", targeting `RELAY_STATUS.md` — a SHARED coordination file other automated relay sessions read as dispatch ground truth. - [ ] [ROUTINE] **`relay-events.jsonl` emits `kind:"verdict"` rows for repos that were never classified — an empty-verdict row reads as a classification and misleads readers** (found 2026-08-13 while auditing a `--only dotclaude-skills` run). No `discover-repo.sh` ran for that repo — the empty `verdict`/`sig` are the tell — but the row's KIND says `verdict`, so a reader tallying `kind=="verdict"` per run counts un-classified repos as classified. **Cost, measured:** this produced a live false-positive diagnosis in an apex session — the rollup rows were read as evidence that `--only` narrows DISPATCH but not CLASSIFICATION, i.e. a scope defect that does not exist. `relay-loop.js:1480-1491` narrows correctly (`scopedOwnRepos = [scoped]` feeds the exclude filter + sig-cache + shard fan-out); only reading the code falsified the claim. **Fix direction (pick one, both cheap):** give the rollup its own kind (e.g. `kind:"skipped"`), or keep `verdict` and add an explicit discriminator field (`classified:false`) so a consumer can filter without inferring from empty strings. Prefer the distinct kind — inferring semantics from an empty string is the same shape as the id:4347 no-silent-swallow anti-pattern. Also worth noting the volume is pure noise under a single-repo scope: 5 paused repos x 4 rounds = 20 rows about repos the run was explicitly told to ignore. - [ ] [HARD] **`inject.sh take` is destructive-on-read with no acknowledgement and no re-enqueue — an injected unit is silently LOST if the consuming pool never works it, and an UNSCOPED pool can swallow a unit meant for a scoped one** (both halves observed live 2026-08-13). Two distinct defects, one root: consumption is irreversible and unacknowledged. **(A) DURABILITY.** `take` moves each shard to `inject.done/` and emits it; from that moment the unit exists ONLY inside the consuming run's memory. If that run hands back, stops, or drops queued-but-undispatched units (`stopReason: blocked-pending-human` / `user-stop` / quota), the unit vanishes: `peek` is empty, the ledger is unchanged, and NOTHING reports it. OBSERVED: `inj-20260813-193234-4091510-24753` (a `routed:f833` handoff) was consumed by run `relay-20260813-180303-4214`, whose 6 rounds ended `blocked-pending-human`; `routed:f833` was never promoted and the loss produced no signal. An empty `peek` is INDISTINGUISHABLE from 'it was worked' — that ambiguity is the actual defect (id:4347 no-silent-swallow). MITIGATION THAT ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD BE NAMED IN THE FIX: the shard is NOT destroyed — it is preserved verbatim in `~/.config/relay/inject.done/<token>.json`, so recovery today is a manual move back into `inject.d/`. The gap is the absent signal + absent re-enqueue, not data loss. **(B) SCOPE-STEAL BY AN UNSCOPED POOL.** `inject.sh`'s own header records it: `--repo NAME` restricts `take`, and *'The pool passes its `--only` scope through discover-prelude.sh and the mid-round take; an UNSCOPED pool still drains globally (today's behaviour).'* So `--only` protects the SCOPED pool from stealing, but protects NOTHING from a parallel unscoped fleet pool, which drains every pending shard regardless of target repo. `--exclude` is strictly worse: excluded repos are dropped BEFORE sharding (no unit is ever emitted), so a fleet pool with `--exclude X` consumes X's injection and can then NEVER work it — a guaranteed loss. Parallel pools are the NORMAL case (id:11c6's singleton guard deliberately exempts `--afk` and every scoped/directed mode), so this is not a rare race. Prior instance cited in-file: run `relay-20260811-221031-22542`. **Fix directions (owner picks; do NOT guess):** (1) make `take` a LEASE rather than a consume — a unit not integrated by run-end returns to `inject.d/` (mirrors the claim.sh mtime-TTL model already in the codebase); (2) have the pool's exit path re-enqueue any taken-but-undispatched unit, and LOG every consume with its runId the way `id:cd94` made the STOP sentinel do; (3) make an unscoped `take` refuse shards whose repo is in the run's `--exclude` set at minimum. (1) and (2) address (A); (3) addresses (B); they are independent. Note the same steal-once shape was already fixed once for the STOP sentinel (`id:cd94`, run-scoped sentinel file) — that precedent is the design to mirror. <!-- id:10ff -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Does `id:cd9c` branch (a) need a stub-pruning or selective-stub companion? Stubs accrue permanently and eat the `id:4f9b` prompt-size headroom the archiver exists to create** **OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-14 (`/relay human .`): SELECTIVE STUBS — emit a stub only when something actually references the id.** Rejected: *prune-later* (a pruner is only as trustworthy as the reference scan, and archive-blindness is a KNOWN LIVE defect in exactly that scan — pruning on a false negative DELETES a live reference, an unrecoverable error in exchange for a recoverable one) and *ship-bare* (leaves `prompt-size-gate.mjs:72` with no effective remedy to name). Rationale: a stub exists to keep a reference RESOLVABLE, so emitting one where no reference exists is pure cost. Deciding ONCE at archive time also avoids re-deciding forever. **Acceptance**: at archive time, emit a stub iff the id is referenced by an open `gated-on:`/typed edge or live prose; assert the no-reference case emits NO stub and the referenced case still resolves; state the scan's blind spot in the output rather than implying completeness. **Scope guard**: this does NOT reopen `id:cd9c` branch (a), ruled 2026-08-13 — it decides only the companion. Revisit pruning only after the archive-blindness cluster lands and the reference scan can be trusted. <!-- id:36f7 --> — **The tension, measured 2026-08-13 (this repo)**: `relay/scripts/prompt-size-gate.mjs:72` prescribes `roadmap-archive.sh` as THE remedy when a child cannot be dispatched because `ROADMAP.md` is too large ("REMEDY: run roadmap-archive.sh … to move the done `- [x]` items into ROADMAP.archive.md"). Under (a) the live file no longer shrinks the same way: ONE stub line accrues per archived item, forever. Numbers: **333** archived top-level items vs a live `ROADMAP.md` of **216,993 bytes / 1,602 lines**; the gate caps the ROADMAP contribution around 100k tok with ~100k working room (`prompt-size-gate.mjs:33`). A full-history stub set is therefore a large fraction of the very budget the remedy is meant to free. **NOT a re-opening of (a)** — the owner ruled (a) on 2026-08-13 and this item does not revisit it; it decides only whether (a) ships bare or with a companion. **Options to rule on**: (i) ship bare and accept the growth, updating `prompt-size-gate.mjs:72`'s remedy text so it stops promising headroom it no longer delivers; (ii) PRUNE a stub once no open `gated-on:`/typed edge and no live prose still references its id (needs the reference scan to be trustworthy — see `id:3262`, `routed:8b21` archive-blindness); (iii) SELECTIVE stubs — emit one only for ids that are actually referenced, so unreferenced history stays fully archived. (ii)/(iii) both make stub emission depend on a reference query, which is a materially bigger build than (a) alone. **Whoever implements cd9c must state which of these they assumed** — leaving it implicit is how the cost becomes invisible. Relates `id:cd9c` (the ruled branch), `id:4f9b` (the gate whose headroom is at stake), `id:3262`/`routed:8b21` (archive-aware reference scanning).
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **The typed-edge engine reads `<!-- children: -->` while 88% of the corpus writes `<!-- children-of: -->`, and the two spellings encode INVERSE directions — child edges are a silent no-op today** **OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-14 (`/relay human .`): support BOTH spellings with explicit direction handling — AND rename the `children-of:` sense to PARENTS.** The root cause is the misnaming, not the corpus: `typed_edges_children_of_line()` (`relay/scripts/lib-typed-edges.sh:19`) greps `<!-- children: -->` while **146** corpus lines write `<!-- children-of: -->` against only **29** `children:` (counts re-measured this pass; the two strings are disjoint, so the split is real). Because the spellings encode INVERSE directions, one extractor cannot serve both. Resolution: `children-of:X` means *X is my PARENT* and gets its own extractor named for that (`typed_edges_parents_of_line`, or equivalent); `children:X` means *X is my child* and keeps the children extractor. Both remain valid grammar — **no bulk corpus rewrite**, which the item itself warns is far harder to undo than the current no-op. This removes the silent 83% traversal gap without a risky one-pass conversion. Callers must be audited for which direction they actually wanted; the misnamed function means some may have been silently getting neither. <!-- id:cf7a --> — **Mechanism**: `relay/scripts/lib-typed-edges.sh:19` defines `typed_edges_children_of_line() { grep -oP '(?<=<!-- children:)[0-9a-f,]+(?= -->)' ...; }`. Note the function is NAMED `children_of` but its regex matches `children:`. Its sole consumer is `meeting/orphan-scan.sh:280` (`children_csv=$(typed_edges_children_of_line "$text")`), which feeds `has_typed` at :283 — so an item whose ONLY typed edge is `children-of:` extracts EMPTY and is treated as carrying no typed edge at all. Fails silently: no error, no warning (the id:4347 no-silent-swallow shape). **MEASURED 2026-08-13, this repo only** — `children-of:` vs `children:` per ledger: `ROADMAP.md` 12 vs 1; `TODO.md` 35 vs 10; `ROADMAP.archive.md` 47 vs 1; `TODO.archive.md` 34 vs 6. Totals **128 vs 18** — about **88% of child edges are invisible to the engine**. `meeting/classify.sh:64` strips BOTH spellings, which is why the drift never surfaced in the bucket summary. **THE DECISION IS NOT A SPELLING FIX — the two forms are INVERSE relations** and that is why this is `[INPUT — decision]`, not `[ROUTINE]`: `<!-- children:a,b -->` on a parent means "my children are a and b" (parent→children, one marker per parent), whereas `<!-- children-of:X -->` on a child means "I am a child of X" (child→parent, one marker per child). Mechanically translating one into the other requires choosing which direction is canonical and rewriting ~146 markers accordingly; picking the parent→children form also means a parent must be edited whenever a child is added, which is precisely the write-contention the child→parent form avoids. **Rule on**: (i) canonical direction, (ii) whether the engine accepts BOTH during a migration window (cf. the `id:4f02`/`id:8111` dual-vocab precedent) or hard-cuts, (iii) whether a ratchet blocks the losing spelling (cf. `hooks/pre-commit-lane-vocab.sh`). **Acceptance once ruled**: `lib-typed-edges.sh` parses the canonical form (and, if chosen, the legacy one), a test asserts a `children-of:`-only item yields a non-empty child set and `has_typed=1`, and the corpus is converted in one pass. **Do NOT auto-rewrite markers before the direction is ruled** — a wrong-direction bulk rewrite is far harder to undo than the current silent no-op. Found 2026-08-13 while filing `id:b30c`, when choosing a child-edge spelling required checking which one the engine actually reads. Relates `id:46f6` (typed edges), `id:2840` (derived ledger index).

- [ ] [INPUT — decision] **Decide whether to MECHANIZE the Bash-first guard, or wait for the steer to prove durable** (filed 2026-08-19 alongside the `id:93b4` CLAUDE.md clause). The clause just added to global `CLAUDE.md` ("Tool choice for file edits") is **prose enforcement**, and this repo's own history says prose fails at exactly this: `routed:29bc`/`id:2419` recorded the same rule stated in three places and violated across multiple sessions and models, which is why it became a blocking Stop hook. The mechanical form here would be a **`PreToolUse` hook** that soft-denies `sed -i` / `python…open(p,'w')` / `cat >>` against a **tracked** file and names the correct path (`meeting/md-merge.py` for the shared ledgers, the Edit tool otherwise) — the same shape as the existing lane-vocab pre-commit ratchet and the `meeting-question-guard` Stop hook. **The argument for WAITING — its PREMISE WAS WRONG, and the branch has now RESOLVED itself:** this originally read "the steer is emitted by a `bashFirst` template gated on an INTERNAL feature flag in the CLI binary, **not by any setting**". That was never checked against the binary, and it was false — `CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC=0` disables it and always did (claude-code#87575). Verified 2026-08-23 against 2.1.237 and now **applied fleet-wide** via `make install-relay-env` (`HARNESS_ENV_DEFAULTS` → settings.json `env`); note UNSET IS NOT OFF, the gate falls through to A/B cohort assignment unless the var is present and spelled `0|false|no|off`. So the steer this hook would counteract is **gone on this fleet by setting**, not by waiting for an experiment to lapse — a hook built as `bashFirst` counter-pressure is vestigial by construction now. Building a guard against a vestige is the **constraint-archaeology** anti-pattern in global CLAUDE.md ("re-justify defensive machinery when its constraint may have lapsed"), and `observe before preventing` says gather evidence first. **The argument for BUILDING NOW:** the measured cost is not speculative — 682 python-as-sed calls in 9 days, a 4x-worse true failure rate, and silent-wrong-outcome failures that no error surfaces (one landed in the filing session itself: id markers written to continuation lines, no error, caught 40 minutes later by `classify-repo.sh`). **Cheap middle option, if you want evidence rather than a coin-flip:** ship the hook in WARN+LOG mode only (the `id:ebd0` privacy-gate pattern — log to `~/.claude/logs/`, exit 0, never block), let it accrue for 2–4 weeks, then decide on blocking from a real count. Note the counter-evidence on warn-only from this repo: `hooks/meeting-question-guard.py`'s own docstring records "a correct warning emitted ~6300 times over 22 days with zero response is a dead CHANNEL", so a warn-only build must have a named review date or it becomes the `id:4347` silent-no-op it is meant to prevent. **STILL LIVE after the flag, and the real question this item should now decide:** the ledger/flock tier and the protected-path tier never depended on `bashFirst` at all — `Edit` bypasses the flock exactly as `sed -i` does — so a `PreToolUse` guard for THOSE stands on its own merits (see `id:5817`, where a missing id marker forced an `Edit` bypass for want of a key). Decide that narrower guard, not the original one. <!-- id:efa7 -->

- [ ] [INBOUND routed:9ff0 from loderite] URGENT — the pool DOUBLE-DISPATCHES items: in-flight de-dup is keyed on the DISPATCH-TIME slot, not on the item the child actually works, so a repo-scoped unit is invisible to item-level de-dup. MECHANISM (code-grounded, relay-loop.js): dispatchItemFor(unit) = unit.inject_item || namedItemsFor(unit)[0] || '' — it falls back to EMPTY when no item can be named; unitKey (id:923b, :2322) = `${verdict}-${itemId || 'repo'}-${attempt}` and that same key drives BOTH the worktree path AND the inFlight sweep (its own comment says so). So a unit with no named item keys as "<verdict>-repo-<attempt>", the CHILD then selects head-of-list itself at start, and nothing anywhere compares that selection against what another in-flight unit was given. Two repo-scoped units differ only by `attempt`; neither key mentions the item either child will work. THREE OBSERVED INSTANCES: (1) loderite run relay-20260819-094422-14889 — unit execute-repo-1 built id:5947 (sun-only wireframe suppression + glow impostor) while id:5947 had ALREADY landed via another unit at ckpt relay-ckpt-20260819-1147; the duplicate then failed to merge with a content conflict in src/render-core.ts, wasting the child and leaving a branch for supervised reconcile (verified duplicate, not lost work: 5947 is [x] on main and tests/celestial-glow.test.ts is 10/10 green; the duplicate's own test file never landed). (2) loderite run relay-20260819-004723-32305 — units execute-4e39-0 AND execute-repo-0 BOTH died with the identical "Prompt is too long", consistent with the repo-scoped unit independently picking id:4e39, which was verified to be actionable_routine_ids[0] at the time; two children burned on one oversized item. (3) historical, recorded in loderite ROADMAP id:b276: "3 wasted executor dispatches in run relay-20260730-120037-1685" on a single item. SECONDARY DEFECT, and it is why nobody noticed: the append-only event log ~/.config/relay/relay-events.jsonl carries NO item id on a "dispatch" event — its keys are exactly [cached, kind, priority_rank, reason, repo, round, runId, sig, ts, verdict]. The one question the event log exists to answer after the fact ("was this item dispatched twice?") is unanswerable from it; the collision is only visible by reading worktree/branch NAMES, which do encode the item. PROPOSED FIX: (a) have the child REPORT the item it selected as soon as it selects it, and de-dup in-flight on that reported item rather than on the dispatch-time slot — a repo-scoped unit whose pick is already in flight should yield rather than build; (b) add the selected item id to the dispatch event so the log can detect this class mechanically instead of by branch-name archaeology; (c) cheapest partial mitigation if (a) is expensive — never emit more than one repo-scoped unit per verdict class per round, since two of them provably converge on the same head-of-list id. <!-- id:8c8d -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **A recurring REPORT-ONLY advisory must never open a `REVIEW_ME.md` box — owner-ruled 2026-08-20 (`/relay human --all`).** Measured that day: **13 of 92** open `review_me` boxes fleet-wide (~14%) were report-only scan advisories — `UNMARKED-GATE`, `DECIDED-LEFT-OPEN`, `GATE-STALE`, mechanical-orphan, dead-letter — across 8 repos. They are not human DECISIONS, and closing one does not stop the next sweep re-emitting the identical finding, so they accrue as permanent fake backlog that crowds out the genuine judgment calls the tier exists to serve. Two live examples of the harm: zkWhale `id:6452` was flagged `GATE-STALE` purely because its gating LINE was 15 days old — the heuristic measures line AGE, never whether the condition is met, and the gate was verifiably still unmet (`package.json` at `0.2.1`, the gating item still `- [ ]`); ai-codebench `id:8bea` carried a box whose own text concluded "false-positive on gate-history prose… No action needed", left open for five weeks over an OPTIONAL cosmetic tidy-up. cyclotomic-projection carried the SAME advisory as two separate open boxes. **Fix:** the advisory classes stay in `relay-doctor.sh` / `roadmap-lint.sh` / `orphan-scan --shipped` OUTPUT (the signal is wanted, and lint stays report-only), but the review/human write-back path must NOT mint a `REVIEW_ME` box for them. A finding earns a box only when it names a decision a human must make. **Scope care:** distinguish a recurring ADVISORY from a genuine one-shot finding that merely happens to come from a scan — a dead-letter naming real unrouted work IS decision-worthy, whereas "this line has gate vocabulary but no typed marker" is not. Re-checkable: run a review pass on a repo with a standing UNMARKED-GATE advisory and assert `REVIEW_ME.md` gains no box while `relay-doctor.sh` still reports it. <!-- id:04e5 -->

Every `model:"bash"` hop naming it failed with *"There's an issue with the selected model (bash). Two defects, both worth fixing: **(a) the error is misleading** — a hop naming a non-existent script should say so, not implicate the model; **(b) nothing verifies install completeness** — `mech-preflight.sh` validates the transport and never that the scripts the run will name are present, so its `proceed` was accurate and useless here. Cheap fix for (b): a preflight/doctor check that every script named in the Makefile's relay install sets resolves under `~/.claude/skills/relay/scripts/`, run before dispatch or as a `relay-doctor.sh` item — mechanical, no LLM. This item catches committed-but-not-installed; `78fe` catches uninstalled-but-still-linked. Only both together make "is the live skill tree in sync with the repo?" answerable in both directions — and a dangling link is what makes an install-completeness check ambiguous in the first place, which slowed the `id:6570` diagnosis. <!-- id:16d5 -->

REVIEW_ME boxes are append-only: a box opened weeks ago accumulates dated annotations BELOW its opening text, each superseding the last, so the first ~5 lines a reader sees are the most stale part of the entry. `gather-human-backlog.sh` emits `box_summary` from the box's opening, which makes the stale head the thing triage reads. **Three instances, same session, all caught only by re-measuring:** (1) loderite `id:7ef6` was filed claiming 3 DEAD-GATEs needed an owner call — `roadmap-lint.sh` reported **zero**, all three having been resolved in notes appended below; (2) the loderite `roadmap-lint` backlog box's head listed 10 warnings when the live set had moved to 11 different ones; (3) loderite `id:4f69` was dispositioned against blocker `id:b0bb`, which had been **closed the day before** — the box had corrected itself TWICE below the annotation that was read, and typing that gate would have created an instantly-dead gate of exactly the class being cleaned up elsewhere in the same pass. **Fix (mechanical, no model):** have the collector extract the LAST dated annotation rather than the opening, or emit both as `head` + `latest` columns so a reader cannot see only the stale half. A `- [ ]` box whose newest annotation says "CLOSED"/"RESOLVED"/"SUPERSEDED" is also a cheap tick-ready signal worth surfacing. **Scope care:** do NOT auto-tick on a discharge-shaped marker — `id:1e21` literally opens "DO NOT re-pick" and is legitimately open; this is about what the READER is shown, not about deciding for them. Re-checkable: `gather-human-backlog.sh <repo>` on a box with dated annotations shows the newest, not the opening. <!-- id:99da -->

It is no longer in the Makefile at all, yet survived ~3 weeks of installs, **including a `make install-relay` run earlier the same day**, because the install target only ADDS. Removed by hand this pass; the skills tree now has 0 broken symlinks. **This is the exact INVERSE of `id:16d5`** — that one catches *committed-but-never-installed* (which left the `id:dd7d` guard inert fleet-wide for a day); this catches *uninstalled-but-still-linked*. Together they make "is the live skill tree in sync with the repo?" answerable in both directions, which is the property neither has alone. **Fix:** teach the install target (or a `make status`/`relay-doctor` check) to detect and prune symlinks under `~/.claude/skills/**` whose target no longer resolves. **Scope care — do NOT blanket-delete every dangling link:** a link may dangle because a source file is legitimately absent mid-rebase, or because a DIFFERENT repo owns it; prune only links whose target path lies inside this repo AND is absent from the Makefile's install sets. Blast radius is `~/.claude`, so fail loud and list before removing rather than deleting silently. **Impact is low but the ambiguity is not:** a dangling link makes every future install-completeness check ambiguous, which is precisely what made the `id:6570` diagnosis slower. Re-checkable: `find ~/.claude/skills -xtype l` stays empty after a retirement + `make install`. <!-- id:78fe -->

- [ ] 🔴 **[HARD] The safety classifier BLOCKED the relay integrate hop — if it fires on every run, the autonomous pool can dispatch but never merge, which breaks `--afk`.** OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-21, run `relay-20260821-170128-5042`: the `integrate:dotclaude-skills` hop was refused with `[Self-Approval]` — the call would merge/bump/changelog/tag/PUSH a sub-agent's own `id:0384` commit to the PUBLIC repo with no human ratification, and the refusal cited the owner's own CLAUDE.md delegated-verdict rule. The classifier sits at the `agent()` DISPATCH layer, UPSTREAM of `mechanical-proxy.py`'s HTTP interception (re-confirms `id:e62c` branch-1), so no proxy/allowlist fix can reach it. **WHY IT IS NEW:** until `19fcf63` (2026-08-21) the integrator was an ~11-step Sonnet AGENT PROMPT; today it became a LITERAL `integrate.sh … --verdict review` command dispatched as `model:"bash"` — far more legible to a classifier as a publish action — and it was UNREACHABLE until `make install-relay` ran at ~17:01, so this was the FIRST dispatch of this call in the relay's history. **HYPOTHESIS (untested):** the block is CONTEXT-specific, not intrinsic — this session contained a self-approval chain (an agent spawned here wrote `id:0384`, and the same session tried to publish it) and the refusal text reasons explicitly about "this transcript"; a normal `--afk` run integrating work no in-session agent authored may pass. **TEST:** the next ordinary `--afk`/pool run is the free experiment — if integrate lands, the hypothesis holds; if it blocks, unattended mode is CONFIRMED broken and needs an owner decision on the integration model (e.g. pool merges locally and a human pushes). Failure shape is SAFE (blocks pre-merge, work preserved on the branch, nothing half-landed) but SILENT — the worst case under `--afk`, where nobody is watching. Contract: a recorded verdict on whether the pool can integrate unattended. — **HYPOTHESIS REFUTED SAME DAY (run `relay-20260821-174757-32436`):** the "execute blocks / review passes" split is WRONG — `review` appears on BOTH sides (`inflownistration` review integrated OK with `ids=[]`; `dotclaude-skills` review returned empty; `linguistic-universals` execute returned empty). Verdict mode is NOT the discriminator. ALSO NOTE: the two empty results are NOT yet confirmed classifier blocks — that attribution was made by ANALOGY to the confirmed earlier block and cannot be checked until the run ends, because a dispatch-layer refusal leaves no trace in any relay artifact (`id:f5d9`(b)); the empty `no merged= line` message is identical for a block, a dispatch failure, and a genuinely mute integrator. Weak surviving candidate (n=3, do not build on it): the OK case published NOTHING substantive (`ids=[]`) while both failures carried real agent-authored work. — **ANSWERED 2026-08-21, run `relay-20260821-174757-32436` (n=5, from the workflow failures field):** the pool CANNOT land substantive work unattended. ALL THREE substantive integrates were blocked `[Self-Approval]` across ALL THREE verdict modes (`execute`/linguistic-universals id:7673, `review`/dotclaude-skills, `hard`/leAIrn2learn id:21ea). BOTH integrates that SUCCEEDED carry `substantive: false` (csgebra workedIds=[940f], inflownistration workedIds=[]). **DISCRIMINATOR = whether the merge publishes substantive agent-authored work**, NOT verdict mode (that earlier hypothesis was refuted, see above). Pool `stopReason: blocked-pending-human`. **THIS IS A DESIGN COLLISION, NOT A BUG — owner-level, do NOT patch around it:** the pool exists to execute+integrate unattended, while the CLAUDE.md delegated-verdict rule requires human ratification before an agent-authored change is settled; both cannot hold. The classifier cited that rule BY NAME and correctly read this session's "test on next real run" as observe-not-authorize. Options are the owner's: (a) pool merges locally and a human ratifies+pushes in batch; (b) an explicit standing ratification mechanism the classifier can see; (c) accept checkpoint-only autonomy. Cost of the observation: 1,097,375 subagent tokens / 62 min / 103 agents. — **OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-21 (interactive, this session): option (a) — THE POOL MERGES LOCALLY; THE HUMAN RATIFIES AND PUSHES.** For a SUBSTANTIVE unit, `integrate.sh` stops before the push: merge `--no-ff`, bump/changelog, ckpt-tag, retire, state-write all still run, but the push does NOT, and the unit is surfaced in a batch awaiting the owner's ratification. Non-substantive units (`substantive:false`) may keep pushing as they do today — they already pass the classifier and carry nothing to ratify. RATIONALE: this removes ONLY the publish — the exact act the CLAUDE.md delegated-verdict rule protects — and keeps every part of the autonomy that already works (dispatch, execute, review, merge, tag). It honours the rule structurally rather than negotiating with the classifier, so it does not depend on classifier behaviour staying constant. Rejected: a standing-ratification mechanism (real design work, and a mechanism whose purpose is to talk a safety classifier out of a refusal needs its own scrutiny about honouring-vs-satisfying the rule) and accept-checkpoint-only (today's steady state was ~1.1M tokens for two non-substantive checkpoints). **IMPLEMENTATION SEAMS (not yet built):** (1) `integrate.sh` already computes the `substantive` flag the gate needs — reuse it, do not re-derive; (2) ordering matters — the local ckpt tag will exist UNPUSHED, so `ckpt-tag.sh`/`relay-state-write.sh` watermarks and `sync-origin.sh`'s diverged-base check must tolerate a local-ahead main across runs; (3) `id:5fe2`'s landedUnfinished discriminator keys on POST-push steps, and with no push there is no post-push failure class — re-check that logic rather than assuming it still applies; (4) the deferred batch needs a durable surface (a ratification queue the next attended session reads) — NOT only `RELAY_STATUS.md`, which `id:4917` shows goes stale under classifier block; (5) this also fixes `id:f5d9`(a) incidentally by making the push a deliberate, verified step instead of a helper exit code nobody checks. — **OWNER AMENDMENT 2026-08-21 (interactive), NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — the gate is PER-REMOTE, not all-or-nothing.** Owner verbatim: *"I want fievel pushes automatically and only non-local pushes (i.e. github mostly) guarded."* So for a SUBSTANTIVE unit, `integrate.sh` must still PUSH the private/LAN remotes automatically (`origin` = `fievel:src/…`) and defer ONLY the non-local/public ones (`github`). The as-built `db59c7b` defers ALL pushes for a substantive unit — that is now WRONG and must be narrowed before or immediately after merge. RATIONALE: the classifier's objection was to PUBLISHING agent work without ratification; pushing to a private LAN host is not publishing, and deferring it needlessly costs the off-machine backup that makes local-only merges safe to leave overnight. **REUSE, DO NOT REINVENT, the private-remote classifier:** `hooks/pre-push-privacy-gate.sh` already classifies remotes and logs `remote 'origin' (fievel:src/dotclaude-skills.git) is a PRIVATE host — skipping leak scan`; `git-lock-push.sh` separately has `is_ssh_url()` and a `no_push` sentinel. Pick ONE existing predicate and share it — a second, drifting definition of "is this remote public" is exactly the class this repo keeps paying for. **CONSEQUENCES to re-check when narrowing:** (1) seam 5's push VERIFICATION must run per pushed remote (compare each remote's ref to `HEAD`), and `push=` becomes per-remote rather than a single token — the stdout contract and `parseIntegrateResult` change again; (2) the ratification queue record should name WHICH remotes are still pending, not merely that the unit is pending; (3) seam 2's local-ahead tolerance now applies only to the deferred (public) remote — `origin` stays in sync, so the `ahead>0 AND behind>0` handback risk shrinks accordingly. **UNTESTED PREMISE, state it as such:** whether an integrate that pushes ONLY to a private remote still trips the `[Self-Approval]` classifier is UNKNOWN — the observed refusals all named "the public dotclaude-skills repo". If it still blocks, the per-remote narrowing does not rescue unattended operation and the design needs revisiting; verify on the first real pool run after this lands rather than assuming. — **OWNER-DECIDED 2026-08-21 (interactive), the two blockers that stopped the per-remote build: (A) ADD A `--remote` FLAG TO `git-lock-push.sh`; (B) EXTRACT the privacy-gate predicate to a shared lib.** Background: the agent tasked with the per-remote narrowing STOPPED rather than guess, correctly, and named both blockers. **(A)** `git-lock-push.sh` pushes to ALL remotes (`for remote in $(git remote)`) with no selection mechanism beyond the `no_push` pushurl sentinel and the SSH-key gate. Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not retried: pushing per-remote directly from `integrate.sh` DROPS the flock serialization that helper exists to provide (parallel-session safety, `id:aa93`); and temporarily setting `remote.github.pushurl=no_push` mutates SHARED repo config mid-run — if the process dies, `github` is silently never pushed again, a worse failure than the one being fixed. So the flag goes on the helper, which keeps one flock'd push path. **(B)** The ONLY correct predicate is inline at `hooks/pre-push-privacy-gate.sh:66-83` — builtin loopback/RFC-1918/`.local` ERE, plus `private-host:` directives from the PRIVATE never-committed `~/.config/dotclaude-skills/privacy-patterns.txt`, plus `PRIVACY_GATE_PRIVATE_HOSTS`. `fievel` matches ONLY via that private file, so no builtin-only reimplementation can classify it. **`git-lock-push.sh`'s `is_ssh_url()` is NOT a substitute and must never be used for this** — it is an SSH-AUTH predicate: it would classify `ssh://github.com/…` as "private" and AUTO-PUBLISH agent work, i.e. it fails in the UNSAFE direction. Grep confirms no shared copy exists (`private-host` appears only in the hook, its test, and `TODO.archive.md`). Extraction constraints: the shared lib must keep reading the private pattern file (never inline its contents anywhere committed — `id:ebd0` class), must preserve the hook's exact semantics so the gate's behaviour is unchanged, and both callers must then use the ONE copy — a second drifting definition of "is this remote public" is the failure class this repo keeps paying for. Downstream of both: the per-remote push verification (compare EACH pushed remote's ref to `HEAD`), the `push=` stdout contract becoming per-remote (so `parseIntegrateResult` + `INTEGRATE_SCHEMA` change again), and the ratification-queue record naming WHICH remotes are still pending (`ratify-queue.sh` consumes it). **STILL UNTESTED PREMISE:** whether an integrate that pushes ONLY to a private remote still trips the `[Self-Approval]` classifier — every observed refusal named "the public dotclaude-skills repo". Verify on the first real pool run after this lands; if it still blocks, the narrowing does not rescue unattended operation and `id:4d44`'s design needs revisiting. <!-- id:4d44 -->

(B) `FAILED` is now a fourth arm of the enqueue gate and a failed remote counts toward `n_missing`, with the aggregate restructured so `FAILED` is computed alongside the others instead of short-circuiting out of the block. **`ratification=none` is now emitted in exactly ONE case — every eligible remote verified.** All six failure modes (helper exits 0 having pushed nothing; helper exits non-zero; helper non-zero but every remote verifies — fail-closed on the disagreement; substantive all-public; partial; no eligible remote) report `pending` AND write a queue entry. **THE SUPERSESSION (owner-ratified 2026-08-22, interactive):** the land marker moved to immediately after step 7's ckpt tag, unconditionally, replacing three partial sites. `id:f5d9(a)` and `id:5fe2` acceptance 4 both asserted `landed=false` on a push failure, on the premise *"the remote is untouched, so a retry is correct"*. **That premise is FALSE as of `id:4d44`**: step 7 tags BEFORE step 8 pushes, so on a push failure the merge AND the ckpt tag already exist; a retry does not redo the push, it is caught by `id:8739`'s isolation gate at exit 21 reporting a FALSE main-checkout breach. `landed=true` is simply what is now true, and `relay-loop.js` needed NO change — it already keys on `landed=true` + `merged=<sha>`, so it takes the `landedUnfinished` branch on its own. Recorded as an explicit AMENDMENT ON A FALSIFIED PREMISE, not a reinterpretation. `id:a726`(b) also taken: `remaining=` gained a real `git-lock-push` arm naming the pushed/pending counts, and deliberately does NOT list `ratification-enqueue`, which now runs first. **Negative controls RUN**: 10 assertions RED pre-change (queue entry existence and `status=pending` for both liar-push and non-zero-exit paths, `ratification=pending`, `ratification=none` absent, `pending_remotes`/`push=FAILED` in the record, both `remaining=` assertions, and `landed=true` non-substantive). The substantive `landed=true` case was green both sides — expected, since a substantive unit already set `landed` via `defer_push`; that is why a NON-substantive case was added, and it is noted in the test. <!-- id:5155 -->

- [ ] 🔴 **[HARD] BLOCKS THE NEXT POOL RUN — `id:4d44` silently DISABLES `verify-isolation.sh` (`id:f682`), the gate that catches a child writing to the MAIN CHECKOUT.** Found by adversarial review 2026-08-21, REPRODUCED (not inferred). `integrate.sh:372` calls `"$VERIFY_ISO" "$worktree"` with NO `--base`, so `verify-isolation.sh:79-80` resolves base to `origin/main`. That gate is built on the stated premise (`verify-isolation.sh:18-22`) that *"base = merge-base(worktree HEAD, main ref) IS the dispatch-time main HEAD"* — and `id:4d44` FREEZES `origin/main`, so the premise is false BY CONSTRUCTION and degrades further with every deferred unit. TWO failure modes, one root cause: **(b2) never fires again** — `main_head = rev-parse origin/main`, which never advances, so `main_head == merge_base` always and the script takes the `empty+main_unmoved` branch reporting "legitimate no-op review (id:8e3e)" forever; **(a) fires spuriously** — a worktree branched off a local-ahead `main` shows the whole unratified backlog as "commits beyond base", so an EMPTY worktree reports `ok: 2 commit(s) beyond origin/main, tree clean`. DEMONSTRATED side-by-side on the shipped scripts: identical breach, pre-`4d44` → `exit 2` (caught), post-`4d44` → `exit 0` (swept in). FAILURE SCENARIO: any substantive unit integrates (push deferred); on the NEXT dispatch a child writes to the main checkout instead of its worktree — the exact loderite/jobAI incident `id:f682` exists for — `verify-isolation` returns 0, `integrate.sh` merges, and the loose main-checkout edits are swept in. NOTE the `RATIFICATION GATE` header block at `integrate.sh:88-99` enumerates FIVE gates it checked (`sync-origin.sh`, `classify-verdict.sh`, `ckpt-tag.sh`, `relay-state-write.sh`, `discover-sig.sh`) and all five claims verify against code — `verify-isolation.sh` is the ONE gate NOT on that list, and it is the one that breaks. That is the seam-audit lesson: an enumeration of what you checked is also a record of what you did not. FIX: pass `--base main` (or the dispatch-time sha) instead of letting it default to `origin/main`; add a test asserting a main-checkout breach is still caught when `origin/main` is frozen. **UNTIL FIXED: do not run the autonomous pool** — the breach detector is off. <!-- children-of:4d44 --> <!-- id:8739 -->

FIX: `--diff-merges=first-parent` (or `-m`), plus a merge-commit case in the test. **CROSS-CHANGE COMPOUNDING:** `id:4d44` accumulates unpushed `--no-ff` merge commits on `main`, and the queue's own remediation string (`integrate.sh:634`, `git -C %s push --follow-tags`) then publishes them ALL in one push — and the gate skips exactly that content. Contract: with an unrelated agent worktree present containing an at-risk site, the suite on a clean main is GREEN; with the same site on the branch under test, it is RED. — **RECURRED THE SAME DAY (2026-08-22) — the fix was FILE-LOCAL and the pattern came straight back in new code.** `tests/test_private_remote_host_anchored_a726.sh`, written hours AFTER `id:b818` landed, used `grep -r "$SRC_DIR" --exclude-dir=.git` for its "exactly ONE file defines the builtin host ERE" assertion. Fixed by adding `--exclude-dir=worktrees` to both sweeps (commit on main, suite back to 484/0/1). **THE LESSON IS THE RECURRENCE, NOT THE BUG:** `id:b818` patched `tests/lint-pipefail-sigpipe.py` alone, so nothing stopped the next repo-walking check from reintroducing it, and the next one was written the same afternoon. Any sweep over the repo tree is wrong by default now that `isolation: worktree` puts full checkouts of other branches under `.claude/worktrees/`. **What b818 actually needs is a SHARED enumerator** — one helper (or one documented incantation) that every linter, test sweep and scanner uses, so "prune nested checkouts" is inherited rather than remembered. FIX: distinguish "hop was blocked/failed to dispatch" from "integrator emitted unparseable output", and surface the dispatch-layer failure text in the handback reason. **(c) `dc4f` MECHANISM IS MISSTATED** — it says "when ssh stalls"; the stalling remote here is `github`, which is HTTPS, and credentials ARE configured (`credential.https://github.com.helper = !/usr/bin/gh auth git-credential` — a per-URL key that a `credential.helper` query does NOT match; that wrong query produced a confident WRONG "no helper configured" claim this session). Re-diagnose before fixing; leading suspect is the pre-push privacy gate, which runs on PUBLIC remotes only (`origin` logs "PRIVATE host — skipping leak scan" and returns instantly) scanning a 10-commit diff against a 927 KB `TODO.md`. <!-- id:f5d9 -->
- [ ] **`git-lock-push.sh` exits 0 without pushing when ssh stalls — and a `github` stall silently costs the `origin` push too** — observed run relay-20260820-180056-4594 (2026-08-20), then REPRODUCED LIVE in the same session's own todo-update push. Sequence: the script pushes `github` first, that push stalls, the shipped id:3273 hard-timeout seam (`GIT_LOCK_PUSH_TIMEOUT`, routed:8a55, archived TODO.archive.md:371) correctly self-terminates it at 120s — and then the run ENDS. It prints only `WARNING: push to 'github' timed out after 120s ... will push next run`, returns **exit 0**, and **never attempts `origin` at all**: verified `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` still showed the commit after a reported-successful invocation, and a plain `git push origin main` pushed it instantly. So the warning names ONE remote while TWO were skipped — the operator reading it has no reason to check `origin`. Measured cumulative consequence: the public `github` mirror had drifted **7 commits** behind (still at pre-run `fddb1be` while local was `b83f88d`), i.e. across MULTIPLE prior runs; nothing ever retried. Fixes needed, in order: (1) attempt EVERY remote independently — one remote's timeout must not abort the others; (2) a skipped push is a LOUD non-zero, not exit 0; (3) name every un-pushed remote in the warning; (4) make "will push next run" a real recorded push-debt the next run drains, not prose. Extra bite: the public-remote push is where `hooks/pre-push-privacy-gate.sh` runs, so a silently-skipped mirror push also silently skips the leak scan for those commits. Verify with `git ls-remote github main` and `git log origin/main..HEAD` after any run. — **CONCRETE LEAD 2026-08-21: `--follow-tags` is implicated on the GitHub remote.** Measured repeatedly this session: `git push github main --follow-tags` produces NO output, exits without error, and pushes NOTHING (mirror stayed at an old SHA across three attempts), while `git push github main` immediately afterwards succeeds and prints the ref update. `git push origin main --follow-tags` to the private fievel remote works fine. So the stall correlates with tag-object push over HTTPS to GitHub, not with the push path in general — which also explains why `git-lock-push.sh` (which pushes both remotes and pushes tags) returns having only completed the fetch half. Investigate whether the tag push is what hangs until the 120 s timeout, and whether pushing refs and tags as separate invocations fixes it. <!-- id:dc4f -->

- [ ] **[ROUTINE] `integrate.sh` test family flakes under FULL-SUITE runs only — now n=2 across TWO different tests** — (1) the id:087b executor hit an unreproduced red on `tests/test_integrate_mechanized_ports_087b.sh` during a full-suite run, then could not reproduce it in 3 standalone runs, an 8-way parallel stress, or 3 clean full-suite runs; it added stderr capture + replay so the next occurrence is diagnosable. (2) On 2026-08-21, integrating id:087b, `make test` failed `tests/test_integrate_sh_mechanized.sh` (the id:9e50 test — a DIFFERENT file); run standalone immediately after it printed `ALL PASS` and exit 0, and the next full-suite run was `453 passed, 0 failed`. So the flake is not one test — it is the integrate.sh family under full-suite conditions, and it is no longer a single unexplained observation. **HYPOTHESIS ALREADY REFUTED — do not re-run it:** shared global state via the `relay-state-write.sh` lock. Both tests isolate `relay.toml` with `FABLES_CONFIG=$TMP/...`, and `relay-state-write.sh:38` derives `BASE="${FABLES_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/relay}"`, so the lock file follows the override and is per-fixture. Remaining candidates to investigate: `ckpt-tag.sh`'s own locking; same-minute `relay-ckpt-YYYYmmdd-HHMM` tag-name generation under parallelism; git operations racing on a shared object store or index; and the suite runner's own parallel scheduling. Note BOTH tests do real merges, tags and (stubbed) pushes in temp repos, so they are the heaviest git users in the suite. Contract a test would verify: N consecutive full-suite runs with the integrate family present are green, or the failure reproduces with a captured cause. — **WIDENED 2026-08-21, same session: this is NOT the integrate.sh family, it is general parallel-suite flakiness.** FOUR distinct tests have now flaked in-suite and passed standalone immediately after: `test_integrate_mechanized_ports_087b.sh` (087b executor), `test_integrate_sh_mechanized.sh` (twice — the 087b integration and the e68f executor), `test_statusline_tokens.sh` (b018 executor), and `test_mechanical_orphan_draft.sh` (the b018+e68f integration; `22 passed, 0 failed` standalone). Suite size crossed 455 during this session. Since the tests span integrate/statusline/mechanical-daemon domains with no shared fixture, suspect the RUNNER or host-level exhaustion under parallelism (fd limits, tmp-dir pressure, process count, git object-store contention) rather than any one test's state. Next step should be to record WHICH tests fail together in a single run and whether the failing set correlates with parallel width — a per-run failure log, not another single-test hunt. — **CAUSE IDENTIFIED 2026-08-21 (observe-first pass, promoted to ROADMAP.md; item stays OPEN because the fix is NOT small).** Instrument: `tests/flake-log.sh`, log at `~/.cache/dotclaude-flake/runs.jsonl` (outside any repo). 12 full-suite runs on zomni (`nproc`=8): j1 0/2 red, j8 2/4, j16 1/4, j32 0/2 — 3 of 10 parallel runs red, 0 of 2 serial. Per-width n is 2-4 and cannot establish a rate difference (the ~10pp-at-n=10 limit applies a fortiori); the correlation is suggestive, NOT measured. Reproduced FIVE flakers total, three new: `test_handoff_produces_mechanical.sh`, `test_git_lock_push_slash_branch.sh` (twice), `test_integrate_mechanized_ports_087b.sh` — each re-run standalone immediately after and each PASSED (all four outcomes logged). **The mechanism is `set -o pipefail` + a producer piped into an EARLY-EXITING consumer (`grep -q`, `head -N`).** When the consumer exits on its first match before the producer has finished writing, the producer dies of SIGPIPE (141); `pipefail` promotes that to the pipeline's status, and the test's `|| fail` / `set -e` fires. Measured directly on the exact failing assertion (`tail -n +35 relay/references/handoff.md | grep -qF '[MECHANICAL]'`): **8 SIGPIPE in 400 iterations = 2%**, on a static 262-line file with no fixture, no lock and no shared state. Parallel width raises host load, which widens the scheduling window, which raises the per-site rate — no test-specific state is involved, which is exactly why the flakers span integrate/statusline/mechanical-daemon/git-lock with no shared fixture. All FOUR previously-recorded flakers carry the same shape (`test_statusline_tokens.sh` `| head -1`, `test_mechanical_orphan_draft.sh` 9 sites, both integrate tests `git log | grep -q`). Sweep: **427 at-risk pipeline sites across 162 of 459 test files**, and all 459 set `pipefail`. Hypotheses KILLED by the log: tmpfs exhaustion (/tmp headroom never fell below 2.27 GiB across 55 samples, though 2132 stale `/tmp/tmp.*` dirs did accumulate and 7 mktemp tests have no cleanup trap); fd exhaustion (system-wide allocated fds ~17.1-17.8k against `ulimit -n` 524288, flat across runs). Recommended fix, NOT applied here because 427 sites is not a small change: mechanically rewrite `X | grep -q P` to `grep -q P < <(X)` (and `| head -1` to a non-pipe form), then add a lint test banning the shape so it cannot return — decompose as a separate ROUTINE item; a hermetic regression test for id:7518 becomes writable at the same time. **AMENDED same session, n now 17 suite runs — two claims in the paragraph above are CORRECTED and the mechanism is CONFIRMED harder.** (i) **Width does NOT separate, and my earlier "suggestive correlation" over-read the rows** — both j32 runs passed at the HIGHEST observed load (20.9→26.4) while a j8 run failed at 15.1. Per-width now j1 0/2, j8 5/9, j16 1/4, j32 0/2; j8 and j16 differ only because the extra j8 runs came later. The driver is **scheduling latency**, which parallel width only correlates with — not width itself. (ii) **The "all failures in the first 6 runs" temporal/first-run/warm-cache reading is DEAD**: runs 14, 15, 16 and 17 each went red after a 6-run green streak. (iii) **The population is WIDE, and that is a PREDICTION of the mechanism, not a problem for it** — 427 at-risk sites across 162 of 459 files means which test trips is a lottery, so a wide, rotating, non-repeating failure set is exactly what to expect; a cause confined to four named tests would in fact have been the wrong shape. Six distinct tests reproduced in 17 runs (`test_handoff_produces_mechanical.sh`, `test_git_lock_push_slash_branch.sh` ×3, `test_integrate_mechanized_ports_087b.sh`, `test_statusline_tokens.sh`, `test_integrate_sh_mechanized.sh`, `test_gaming_scan.sh`) — including THREE of the four banked ones — all passing standalone, all logged. **Two of the reproductions are self-proving, i.e. logically impossible under any cause except a lying pipeline status.** In `test_integrate_sh_mechanized.sh` the un-piped predecessor assertion (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, line 97) PASSED — the merge demonstrably landed — and line 99's `git log --oneline | grep -q 'merge(relay): test close id:test'` for that same commit FAILED. In `test_gaming_scan.sh` the failure message interpolates `$out` and the printed `$out` **visibly contains** the very `DELETED_TEST:tests/test_foo.sh` string that line 52's `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q ...` had just reported absent. `test_statusline_tokens.sh` failed with NO assertion message at all — the `set -e` signature of an unguarded `$( … | head -1 | strip_ansi)`. Isolation probes: the no-pipe control form `grep -qF P < <(producer)` gave 0/400 SIGPIPE where the piped form gave 8/400 under contention (and 0/400, 0/600 when the host was quieter — the rate is latency-dependent, which is why it reads as "temporal"); `git log … | grep -q <first-line-match>` gives **400/400**, i.e. near-deterministic once the producer has more to write than the consumer reads. A dose-response probe at controlled load levels was started and NOT finished — the load-dependence of the rate is therefore inferred from the contention windows, not established by a controlled experiment. Also **not** established: that the SIGPIPE race is the *only* live cause; it is the only one for which I have direct evidence, and it accounts for every failure observed. Separate incidental defect spotted, not filed: `statusline-command.sh:229-230` prints `printf: : invalid number` to stderr whenever the usage cache is absent (jq yields empty, `// 0` does not save it) — harmless today, but it means the test's asserted path runs with empty quota values. **FLAKE IDENTIFIED 2026-08-22 (independent review), plus a consequence that was NOT stated when the flake was first reported.** The `id:a360` implementer saw a first full-suite run report `485 passed / 0 failed / 2 expected-red` and a second `486/0/1`, without capturing which file flaked. The review narrowed it mechanically: only THREE files are maskable (their `# roadmap:` item is open) — `test_dispatch_skill_countermand_9eb7.sh`, `test_dryround_single_definition_6217.sh`, `test_privacy_gate_prepush.sh`. Run standalone, `6217` fails (it is the standing legitimate expected-red) and the other two pass. So the transient second expected-red was **`9eb7` or `privacy_gate_prepush` flaking in-suite**. **The consequence the implementer did not state:** because that flake lands in a *masked* file, it can never fail the suite in either direction — so "the second run was clean" demonstrates NOTHING about it. A flake inside the masked set is invisible to the green/red signal entirely, which is a second, independent argument for `id:86ca` (arm a test the moment it first goes green). <!-- id:7518 -->

(1) `relay/scripts/prompt-size-gate.mjs:116-120`: when `slice_bytes` is set the gate sizes ONLY the slice and returns allow — ledger bytes are never counted. (2) `relay/scripts/relay-loop.js:2543` (the `id:e68f` brief) tells the child verbatim: *"The full ledgers are still on disk at their canonical paths if the slice genuinely does not carry something you need"*. So on this repo a child is approved on a ~4 KB slice and invited to open a **904,586 B TODO.md (~226k tok)**. If it accepts, it dies with `Prompt is too long` — and because `id:61fa` is still OPEN and gated, `integrate()` records the GENERIC `child agent failed/skipped (API error or terminal failure)`, which is precisely the anonymous-failure string `id:4f9b` was built to eliminate. Operator sees a repo that failed for no stated reason. **No detector exists — 4f9b WAS the detector and `id:35b7` exempts sliced units from it.** Blast radius: every sliced unit in every big-ledger repo, indefinitely. **THIS IS THE `--fabled` F5 FINDING MATERIALIZED** (meeting 2026-08-21): the closing pass warned that e68f *"LOWERS the default, it is not an enforcement"* and that the gate *"must budget for what a child MAY pull"*; we recorded that as `id:9663`, a WORDING correction, and the behavioural half was never built. Options, owner's call — **(b) SHIPPED 2026-08-21** (`253d49f`/`a0ef302`; the brief's ledger escape hatch is now conditional on MEASURED headroom, and `id:31c3` then corrected a stale slicer claim inside that same string). **(a) and (c) REMAIN UNBUILT — they are why this item stays OPEN**: the gate still does not price the invitation, and a `Prompt is too long` child death is still re-emitted as the generic anonymous failure. (Re-derived by review `relay-ckpt-20260820-2044..HEAD`, 2026-08-21 — the item text had listed all three as undecided.) Original options: (a) match the harness's `Prompt is too long` string on the child-failure path and re-emit it as a NAMED handback (overlaps `id:61fa`, which is gated on an architecture call); (b) harden the brief — name the ledger's size inline so "still on disk" reads as a cost, not an invitation; (c) budget a bounded ALLOWANCE for optional reads on top of the slice, so the gate prices the invitation instead of ignoring it. NOT a reason to revert `id:35b7` — before it the repo was frozen outright (303,321 tok REFUSED); this trades a hard freeze for a rarer silent death, which is better but not safe. Relates id:35b7, id:e68f, id:b018, id:9663, id:61fa, id:4f9b. <!-- id:7575 -->
- [ ] **[ROUTINE] `statusline-command.sh:229-230` breaks the quota segment when no usage cache exists — and NOTHING tests that segment** — found by the test-integrity review of the 2026-08-21 window, by mutation testing. With no usage cache present, `jq` errors and `SESSION_PCT`/`WEEKLY_PCT` end up EMPTY — the `// 0` jq default never applies because the FILE is missing, not the key — so the quota `printf` receives an empty argument and emits `statusline-command.sh: line 230: printf: : invalid number` on stderr. Observed live 2026-08-21 while the test PASSED. **This is not a masked defect and `test_statusline_tokens.sh` is not gaming anything**: that test (`roadmap:2520`) asserts only the token segments (`58%(115k)`, `(9.5k)`, `(730)`) and never touches the quota segment, so the defect is simply OUT of its scope. The real gap is that the quota segment has NO test at all. A line where `[INPUT — author]` precedes `[ROUTINE]` therefore flips from actionable to human. The DIRECTION is safe (fewer dispatches, never more) — only the comment is wrong, and a future reader trusting it would mis-reason about lane precedence. Relates id:bc2b, id:4a76, id:8123. <!-- id:aa8f -->

- [ ] **[ROUTINE] `tests/lint-pipefail-sigpipe.py` — two false negatives, two false positives with no hatch, and a docstring/code drift** — found by adversarial probing in the transform review 2026-08-21 (the lint itself is otherwise sound: 15 positive + 13 negative controls, three suppression-hatch probes confirming there IS no hatch, and the repo is clean under it). **FALSE NEGATIVES (verified with probe files, neither shape present in the repo today):** (1) a trailing-pipe line continuation — `producer |` then newline then `grep -q x` — is unflagged, because the lint is line-based and a trailing `|` leaves stage-2 empty; (2) `producer |& grep -q x` is unflagged, because `|&` splits into a stage starting with `&`. A future author writing either shape gets a green gate on a live instance of the exact bug this lint exists to prevent. **FALSE POSITIVES, and the lint advertises NO exemptions:** `cat f | sed 's/q//'` and `cat f | awk '{print "exit"}'` are both flagged, because the `sed`/`awk` detectors search the RAW script text for a `q` command or the word `exit` rather than parsing the program — so a `q` inside a replacement or `exit` inside a string trips them. With no hatch by design, an author hitting this must contort safe code, which is how a ban decays into a workaround. **DRIFT:** the module docstring promises a `--heredoc` flag, but `main()` has no argv handling, so `--heredoc` is parsed as a PATH and silently no-ops. Fix all four; keep the zero-exemption posture (the fix is a better parser, not a suppression list). Relates id:81d5, id:7518, id:f211. <!-- id:2e8a -->

The in-code comment claiming the extraction is *"byte-for-byte what the inline loop did before"* holds for the FIRST call only — the pre-change code called it once per round, the new code can call it up to `DEMOTE_MAX_CLASSES` times. - [ ] [INPUT — meeting] **IDEA — a "CREATIVE" mode where the model is ENCOURAGED to hallucinate from the start, as a STANCE rather than a sampling parameter** (owner 2026-08-21) — explicitly **not** a temperature change. Temperature perturbs token sampling: the model still tries to be right and merely wobbles. This is the different axis — a mode that grants PERMISSION TO INVENT: no epistemic hedging, no verify-before-asserting, no "I don't have evidence for that", confabulation treated as the DELIVERABLE rather than a defect. Generate the plausible-but-unfounded on purpose, then filter afterwards. **Why it is worth a session rather than a prompt tweak:** this fleet's entire operating discipline is the inverse — verify before asserting, marker-anchored evidence, kill-criteria per hypothesis, "say UNSURE rather than guessing". A creative mode is that discipline deliberately suspended, so it needs an explicit BOUNDARY, not just an invitation. **The hazard, and it is this repo's own recurring failure mode:** creative output leaking into a ledger, meeting note, or memory where a later reader takes it as established. Today alone produced three derived-doc-drift instances (a closed gate reported open, a file header contradicting its own contents, a bare-token grep matching prose) with NO creative mode in play — an output stream that is confabulated BY DESIGN and unmarked would be far worse. So any design must answer: how is creative output PROVENANCE-MARKED so it can never be cited as fact; what surfaces may it write to (a scratch space, never TODO/ROADMAP/REVIEW_ME/memory directly); and what is the promotion ritual that moves an idea from invented to owner-ratified. **Candidate consumers, to test the N=2 rule:** worldbuilding (`lodelore`/`loderite` — the cosmology and lore work is exactly generative-then-ratified), `/meeting` persona brainstorming and the ad-hoc-persona mechanism, naming/coinage (`inflownistration` is a coinage repo), and adversarial red-teaming where inventing implausible-but-possible failure modes is the point. **Open questions:** is it a SKILL, an agent type (`.claude/agents/*.md`, cf. `id:931c`), an output-style, or a system-prompt stance; does it compose with `--fabled` (which is adversarial-critical, arguably the opposite pole); and is "hallucinate" the right framing versus "generate without grounding obligation" — the former names the failure mode, the latter names the capability. Relates id:931c (custom agent types), the `/meeting` persona registry, [[feedback-verify-delegated-work-independently]] (the discipline this suspends). <!-- id:f967 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Gated `git-read.sh` wrapper — restore frictionless CROSS-REPO git reads after the 11 `git -C *` allow rules were removed as an option-injection hole.** Filed 2026-08-26 when a harness update began warning on every session start: *"`Bash(git -C * status)` has a wildcard before the rest of the command, so it also matches any options inserted at that position and approves them without a prompt. For git, options such as `-c` and `--exec-path` can run arbitrary commands."* **The hole was CONFIRMED LIVE, not taken on the warning's word:** `git -C . -c core.pager=true status --short` executed with NO prompt — the injected `-c` sits inside the wildcard and is auto-approved. `-c core.pager=<cmd>`, `-c core.sshCommand=`, `-c alias.x=!sh -c …` and `--exec-path=<dir>` are all arbitrary-execution primitives, so this was an explicit blessing of a sandbox escape. **There is NO safe way to express it with this matcher** — I checked the obvious mitigation and it FAILS: narrowing the prefix to `git -C /home/tobias/src/* status` does not help, because the wildcard still spans forward to the subcommand and can absorb `x -c core.pager=evil`. Enumerating exact repo paths would take ~660 literal entries (allowlist matching is literal, and both `~` and absolute forms are needed) and still would not close it. **DONE ALREADY: all 11 entries deleted from `~/.claude/settings.json` (allow 795 → 784), owner-authorized.** They were HAND-ADDED and unmanaged — `make print-allowlist` emits zero of them — so `tools/allowlist.py` will not reintroduce them; that unmanaged-entry problem is `id:9320`'s complaint with a live consequence. Practical cost of the deletion is likely near-zero today because `defaultMode` is `auto` (an absent command is auto-approved anyway); it withdrew an explicit blessing rather than adding friction, and stricter modes will now prompt. **THIS ITEM = the structural fix:** a read-only `git-read.sh <dir> <subcommand> [args…]` that REFUSES any `<dir>` beginning with `-`, refuses `-c`/`-C`/`--exec-path`/`--git-dir`/`--work-tree` anywhere in its own argv, and shells out to git only for a fixed whitelist of read subcommands (status/log/diff/show/rev-parse/branch/remote/stash list/config --get). Allowlisted as a FIXED SCRIPT PATH (`Bash(~/.claude/skills/…/git-read.sh *)`) — the trailing-wildcard-after-full-command shape, which is the safe one and which 348 existing entries already use. This is the same "deny the raw form, route through the gated script" pattern as `relay/scripts/force-push.sh` and `worktree-retire.sh`. **Gate on evidence, per observe-before-preventing:** only build it if the deletion actually costs prompts in practice — under `defaultMode: auto` it may cost nothing at all, in which case this item closes as won't-need. Relates id:9320, id:221f, id:9ccd. <!-- id:c80e -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Audit the 5 REMAINING wildcard-followed-by-literal allow entries — decide on EVIDENCE, not on their shape.** Filed 2026-08-26 alongside `id:c80e`. After the 11 `git -C *` rules were removed, exactly five entries of the same syntactic class remain: `diary-append.sh -m * -p * -f .diary-entry.*` (×2 path forms), `meeting/append.sh -t * -e *`, `meeting/append.sh -t * -f *`, and `jq -r * /tmp/meeting-rpg/*/broker.json`. **The harness did NOT flag these, and the initial read is that they are materially safer:** the command position holds a FIXED script or binary rather than `git`, so an injected flag is bounded by what that program accepts, and none of them has an arbitrary-execution primitive like git's `-c`. `jq` cannot shell out at all in its default build. **But that is a shape argument, and the owner declined to settle it on one** — which is right, because it is exactly the reasoning that made the `git -C *` rules look acceptable for months. **The actual question to answer, per script:** can a flag injected through one of those wildcards make `append.sh` or `diary-append.sh` write outside its intended target, execute anything, or bypass its own flock? Both are ours, both parse with `getopts`, and both take a `-f FILE` — so the concrete probe is whether an injected second `-f`, a `--`-terminated payload, or a path traversal in the `-e`/`-m` value changes where bytes land. **Weigh removal against real cost:** these sit on the MANDATORY post-prompt diary/append path, so tightening them adds friction to every session — the reason to leave them if the probe comes back clean. **Deliverable:** a per-entry verdict with the command that proves it, and either a tightened entry set or a recorded "safe, and here is why". Relates id:c80e, id:9320. <!-- id:9ccd -->
