## inbox intake 2026-08-18 (evening) — three relay-pool defects routed from lodelore + loderite runs

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`workCreated` is a DRAIN predicate, not a report of what a handback's branch holds — but handbacks are read as if it were the latter, in both directions.** Filed from the same two inbound reports (see `id:dd7d`), whose shared premise is **wrong in a way worth recording**: `routed:d99c` asked to "fix or re-derive `workCreated` so a handback cannot understate what its branch holds", and the amending report widened that to "unreliable in BOTH directions" after observing a handback reporting `workCreated:true` over branch `relay/relay-20260818-110709-32512-review-repo-0` (`6aebd9e`) with `git rev-list --count main..BRANCH` = 0, `origin/main..BRANCH` = 0, and a clean worktree. **VERIFIED HERE:** `relay-loop.js:2840-2909` derives `workCreated = routeCreatedWork || (verdictClassChanged && !osc.oscillating)` — a `id:c919`/`id:907e` predicate answering *"did THIS ROUND create new dispatchable work for the pool?"*, deliberately **repo-scoped, not per-handback** (clause (ii) says so verbatim) and deliberately over-counting because "under-draining merely runs an extra round, over-draining could strand work". It is **never** derived from the branch. So both observations are consistent with the flag working exactly as designed, and "re-derive it from the branch" would break the drain logic it exists to serve. **The real gap is that there is no field for the question people are actually asking** — *does this handback's branch hold commits?* — and the flag with the work-sounding name gets pressed into that role. **Ask:** (a) add a distinct, branch-derived field to the handback record (`branchCommits` / `branchInsertions`, from `git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` + `--shortstat`) so a reader can tell an empty branch from one carrying 3 files / 199 insertions; (b) rename or document `workCreated` at its emission site and in `RELAY_STATUS.md` so it reads as the drain predicate it is; (c) leave the predicate's semantics **unchanged**. Note the practical consequence is real even though the flag is innocent: a false-looking "no work created" invites discarding a branch that holds real work, and `id:2b4b`'s stranded-branch reporter is currently the only thing standing between that and data loss. <!-- id:55bb -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Isolation gate (`id:7612`) FALSE-POSITIVES on the run's OWN integrate commits — a whole unit handed back and its worktree parked for nothing.** (INBOUND routed:d240 from loderite 2026-08-18.) Run `relay-20260818-110709-32512` (loderite, `--only`, 8 rounds): a review child was handed back with *"isolation failure: worktree has NO commits beyond base 'origin/main', AND main advanced since dispatch with a NON-MERGE commit — likely a child that wrote to the main checkout instead of this worktree"*, citing `7471e51` (`relay: checkpoint 20260818-1116`), `fd47e77` (`chore(release): v0.100.9`) and `e139dd2` (`chore(roadmap): tick worked items [id:41dd]`). Each is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> main` TRUE and each is **this run's own round-1 integrate of `id:41dd`**, which the run itself reported completed (ckpt `relay-ckpt-20260818-1116`). No breach occurred. **VERIFIED HERE, with a sharper root cause than the report's:** `verify-isolation.sh` branch (b2) already carries an `id:88f0` exemption for `id:c144`-sanctioned ledger-only advances — but `lib-ledger-only-diff.sh:30` scopes it to `TODO.md ROADMAP.md REVIEW_ME.md RELAY_LOG.md CHANGELOG.md`, and `ledger_only_diff` is evaluated over the **whole range** `merge_base..main_head`, so a single non-ledger commit poisons it. The integrator itself produces such a commit: `version-bump.sh:136` commits `chore(release): $tag` (manifest + lockfile) directly on main, and `ckpt-tag.sh:85` commits the checkpoint. The roadmap tick alone *would* have passed; the release bump is what fails the range. So the exemption built for exactly this shape misses it whenever a repo carries a version manifest. **Not `--only`-specific** — it fires for any repo that integrates ≥2 units in one run where a later child's worktree is a legitimate `id:8e3e` zero-commit no-op review. **Ask:** scope (b2)'s "main advanced" arm to commits **not produced by this run's own integrates** — the run knows its own ckpt tags, merge commits and bump commits, so the exclusion is derivable without new plumbing and keeps the gate fail-safe against genuine third-party writes. Do NOT simply widen the ledger file list to include manifests/lockfiles: that would exempt the exact files a real breach is most likely to corrupt. Relates `id:7612`, `id:f682`, `id:88f0`, `id:1b13`, `id:8e3e`, `id:76d2`. <!-- routed:d240 --> <!-- id:aa8d -->

  - **NEW TRAP, not in the report, and it defeats a naive `--accept` fix:** `--accept` matches **exactly on the porcelain path field**, but git **collapses a fully-untracked directory** — a first meeting note in an otherwise-untracked `docs/` reports as `?? docs/`, NOT `?? docs/meeting-notes/<file>.md` (verified both shapes: untracked parent ⇒ `?? docs/`; tracked parent ⇒ full path). - [ ] [ROUTINE] **`append.sh -t personas` lossless-union extend concatenates a STALE caller copy verbatim, duplicating the entry's introduction and silently dropping extensions — de-duplicate the shared prefix, and GATE on the result** (defect found 2026-08-22; repaired in place by `e013d9b`, but the mechanism is unfixed and will re-fire). **Measured basis, not speculation:** re-registering an already-listed `**Name**` EXTENDS its entry losslessly as a "union of old + new text" (`routed:81b8`). The union only dedupes when the caller's copy shares an exact prefix with what is on disk. On 2026-08-22 a parallel `mathematical-writing/lean-olean-cow-layer` session passed Hank's FULL line, but its copy predated the `Extended 2026-07-23` and `Extended 2026-08-12` extensions already on disk — so the prefix did not match, the whole head was appended verbatim, and the committed line (`0dcff93`) carried `host-fleet config-management lens; … Introduced 2026-06-26 …: CACHE-vs-DERIVATION topology.` TWICE. **The worse half is the silent one:** the duplicated second copy is a stale snapshot, so it presents an entry that OMITS the two intervening extensions, and a reader taking the tail of the line as current gets a lens that lost 7 months of accretion. Cassi, extended in the same commit, is the negative control — its caller copy matched on disk exactly, so its union deduped and it came out clean; the bug is invisible whenever the caller is current, which is why it survived this long. **(a) FIX the union:** dedupe on the longest common prefix (or, better, require callers to pass only the DELTA and have `append.sh` compose the line), so a stale full-line caller can never re-paste a head. **(b) GATE it (the load-bearing half):** after composing, refuse LOUDLY (non-zero, naming the persona) if the resulting entry contains its own introduction segment more than once — a persona line is append-only prose with no marker syntax to anchor on, so a corrupted one is invisible to every existing lint and propagates fleet-wide via `merge=union`. Note (b) must not ship without (a): a gate alone converts a silent corruption into a hard refusal for a caller that has done nothing wrong. **Test both directions**, including the stale-caller shape that actually fired here — a fixture whose on-disk entry has extensions the caller's copy lacks — and prove the assertion by mutation; a test that passes before the fix is a bug in the test. <!-- id:6a34 -->

- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`id:8c85`'s accounting invariant reports `INCOMPLETE ACCOUNTING … reached NO section … the file reports a false clean` for a unit that is merely MID-TRANSITION between dispatch and integrate — a cry-wolf false positive on the one invariant whose job is to be trusted** (observed live 2026-08-22, run `relay-20260822-154630-17003`). **What happened:** `lean4btc` was dispatched `mode=hard` at 13:52:51Z. The `RELAY_STATUS.md` snapshot written at 13:59:16Z placed it in NONE of `blocked / completed / inFlight / queued / skipped` and emitted the ⚠️ INCOMPLETE-ACCOUNTING banner naming it. The unit was fine — it integrated at 14:04:10Z as `relay-ckpt-20260822-1604`, pushed, `ids=e84c` — so the banner described a 6-minute window between the dispatch event and the integrate event during which the unit belonged to no section, NOT a lost unit. **Why it still matters, stated honestly:** during that window the unit genuinely WAS invisible, so if the pool had died there the work would have been unaccounted — the invariant is not wrong about the hazard. The defect is that it cannot distinguish TRANSIENT in-transition from TERMINAL lost, and reports both in the same alarming language ("a false clean"). An operator who sees this fire benignly a few times stops reading it, which is precisely this repo's own `id:4347` cry-wolf rule; and it cost a real investigation this session. **Prior art — read before designing:** the mixed-temporality problem is already known (`RELAY_STATUS` sections accumulate vs reset at different rates, which is why "every own repo in exactly one section" was already shown false); this is a NEW instance of that class, at the per-unit rather than per-repo level. **Suggested shape (not decided):** give a dispatched-but-not-yet-integrated unit an explicit in-transition state so it reaches a section by construction, OR keep the check but downgrade the wording when the unit has a dispatch event and no terminal event yet, reserving the "false clean" language for a unit with no live claim and no terminal event. Whichever way, the invariant must keep firing LOUDLY for a genuinely lost unit — do not fix the false positive by weakening the true positive. <!-- id:e512 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **An execute child can exhaust its context mid-task and lose FINISHED work at the commit step — the `id:35b7` pre-dispatch gate does not and cannot cover this** (root-caused from transcripts 2026-08-22, run `relay-20260822-154630-17003`, loderite `id:6612`). **Verbatim error:** `Prompt is too long`, `isApiErrorMessage: true`, at `2026-08-22T14:06:33.070Z` (last record of that child's `agent-*.jsonl` in the run's workflow transcript dir). **The gate was NOT at fault and worked correctly:** `ledger-slice.sh --repo loderite --id 6612` produced a **2,703-byte** slice; the same round shows the gate genuinely firing for it-infra (`~132015 tok, over the 100000 tok dispatch budget`) which was never dispatched. **What actually happened:** the child's prompt grew **67,283 → 176,311 tokens over ~18 minutes** of tool results and thinking (123k chars of thinking, 171k of tool_result, with single results of 25.8k and 23.4k chars). **The expensive part is WHERE it died:** it had already finished the work, run the full suite (37 failed / 3182 passed, matching its own stated baseline) and a clean typecheck — the last successful call was a `RELAY_LOG.md` heredoc, and the NEXT request was rejected. So a completed unit was lost at the commit step and survives only as `id:f272` WIP residue on `relay/orphan/relay-20260822-154630-17003-execute-6612-0`. **Not fleet-wide:** exactly 1 of 138 agent transcripts in that run carried an API error; the next-highest peak prompts (147k / 134k / 133k) all completed. **Caveat, do not overstate:** 176,311 is under a nominal 200k window and no `max_tokens` override exists in settings or env, so the exact ceiling is UNESTABLISHED — only the error CLASS (context-length rejection, not rate-limit) is proven. **FIX SHAPE (not decided):** the cheapest real mitigation is to make the child COMMIT EARLIER — commit-before-suite rather than commit-after — so a context death costs the verification, not the work. A context-headroom check before the wrap-up sequence is the alternative. Relates to the long-standing executor prompt-size item, but is a DIFFERENT mechanism: that one is dispatch-time, this one is in-session growth. <!-- id:3242 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **An `agent()` dispatch can be dropped at the harness boundary with NO record anywhere — and when the dropped hop is a lease release, the claim leaks until TTL** (observed twice in one run, 2026-08-22 `relay-20260822-154630-17003`). **What was proven, with evidence:** both `release:leancow:claim` and `release:puzzle-pwa:claim` (the first of two fences in `releaseLease()`, `relay-loop.js:3592`; null/empty branch at `relay-loop.js:1228-1229`) failed as `agent() resolved null/empty`. Neither `claim.sh release leancow` nor `claim.sh release puzzle-pwa` appears in `/tmp/mechanical-proxy.log` for this run, while the SECOND fence of the same call (`heartbeat.sh beat`) DOES, milliseconds later — and all eight other units' claim fences landed (`out=15`). No agent transcript exists for either; neither appears in `journal.jsonl`. **So the proxy is EXONERATED** (pid 3048330, alive throughout, served the surrounding calls): the dispatch was dropped before an agent was ever created. **ROOT CAUSE: UNDETERMINED, and deliberately recorded as such** — nothing in `~/.claude/logs/`, `journal.jsonl`, the proxy log or `relay-events.jsonl` records a reason for a dropped dispatch; `dispatchGuarded`'s own comment block (`relay-loop.js:1204-1206`) says as much. Closing this needs harness-level logging that does not exist: a log written by the Workflow runtime when it refuses or drops an `agent()` call. **The real consequence differs per repo and is the actionable half:** leancow was backstopped by `integrate.sh` step 0 (`integrate.sh:406`, logged `~/.claude/logs/relay-claim.log:8066`), but puzzle-pwa handed back `contract-not-met` so NO integrate ran and NOTHING released it — its claim sat held live with only the TTL to clear it. **Fix the consequence even though the cause is undetermined:** a dropped release must not depend on a later integrate that may never happen; the exit-time sweep (`id:54be`/`id:89d6`) is the natural backstop and did not cover this path. <!-- id:c9e7 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`relay-events.jsonl` timestamps are BATCH stamps, not event times — reading them as event times manufactures phantom correlations** (cost a real investigation 2026-08-22). **Mechanism:** `relay-loop.js:56-59` stamps every event with `state.ts`, and the in-code note explains why — the Workflow runtime FORBIDS `Date.now()`/`new Date()`, so ordering rides on discovery/integrate timestamps. `state.ts` is reassigned at only four sites (`relay-loop.js:1803, 2470, 3272, 3366` — prelude, discovery, integrate results). Every event emitted between two reassignments therefore carries an IDENTICAL timestamp regardless of when it happened. **How it misled, concretely:** lean4btc's integrate, puzzle-pwa's handback and loderite's handback all read `2026-08-22T14:04:10Z`, which looked like a simultaneous multi-unit event worth chasing as a slot/concurrency bug. It was not: loderite actually died at `14:06:33.070Z` (its transcript), released at `14:07:02Z` (`relay-claim.log`), and parked at `14:07:12Z` (the commit). The shared stamp was lean4btc's integrate, nothing more. **Consequence:** any forensic timeline built from `relay-events.jsonl` alone is unreliable, and the file gives no hint of this — the field is named `ts` and looks like an event time. **FIX SHAPE (not decided):** either rename the field to something honest (`batch_ts`) so no reader mistakes it, or carry a real per-event time obtained the way the rest of the system does (a mechanical hop can call `date`; the Workflow sandbox cannot). Either way the live-file read and its not-applicable pass must go. <!-- id:9452 -->

Decide between: (i) build a genuine no-bump branch so a level policy can still decline a refactor-only close, restoring the ratified rule and removing the need for the override entirely; (ii) accept per-integrate bumping as the settled cost; or (iii) narrow the default to the three repos that actually handed back (puzzle-pwa, csgebra, leAIrn2learn) rather than the fleet. Deliberately deferred, not dropped — the override was ratified WITH this consequence stated, so this item exists to keep it visible rather than to re-litigate it. **OWNER RULING 2026-08-22 — the fleet default STANDS at full scope, and the reason CONTESTS the old rule's premise rather than merely overriding it.** Presented with the measured blast radius (63 `[repos.*]` blocks, **zero** explicit policies; ~30 manifest repos under `~/src` plus **16 registered `zkm-*` plugins**, so ~46 repos flip to bumping on every integrate; plus the `zkm` parent-bump→plugin-`uv.lock` cascade that nothing automates) and offered the cheaper-to-reverse narrowing to the three trigger repos, the owner chose to KEEP the fleet default. His stated reasoning, which is the substantive part and should be carried into any doc that restates this: **"even a refactor IS a bump we can't guarantee is functionally identical (except for Lean code maybe?)"** — i.e. a refactor-only close ASSERTS functional identity it cannot actually prove, so minting a version is the HONEST signal, and the 2026-07-17-1541 D1 premise (refactor-only ⇒ no user-observable change ⇒ no bump) is itself questionable. The carve-out he names is formally-verified code, where identity CAN be mechanically established. **This reframes the override:** it is not a throughput-for-precision trade grudgingly accepted, it is a challenge to the ratified rule's factual premise — which is the legitimate way to amend a ratified decision (state the false premise explicitly) rather than reinterpret it. Option (i) build-a-no-bump-branch is correspondingly WEAKER than it looked: a no-bump branch restores a rule whose premise the owner disputes. This item stays open for the `zkm` lockfile-cascade half, which is a real unautomated cost independent of the principle. <!-- id:0832 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] 🔴 **`relay-burn.sh` mis-detects quota-window resets by comparing full `resets_at` strings — the API jitters that field sub-second, so nearly every sample pair reads as a reset.** Found 2026-08-22 while building the quota fit: a first-draft segmentation using the same full-string comparison as `relay-burn.sh`'s jq logic declared a reset on **2770 of 3051** sample pairs; keying on the DATE PREFIX (the approach `tools/quota-report.py` already uses) corrected it to a clean **9 resets / 10 segments** matching the real weekly cadence. Any `%/h` or per-bucket projection `relay-burn.sh report` has produced across segments is therefore suspect. Fix: adopt `quota-report.py`'s date-prefix segmentation as the one definition and have both read it, rather than two scripts disagreeing about when a week begins. <!-- id:9c4c -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Test hygiene from the `id:a360` review: pin the gate ordering, and normalise an inert `# roadmap:` header.** Two gaps, neither blocking. **(a) The dd7d gate's ORDERING is unpinned.** `5643e3f`/`cc4c33e` deliberately moved the stranded-branch gate AHEAD of the `id:e68f` ledger slice and the `id:4f9b` size gate, because both compute from `dispatchItemFor(unit)` and would otherwise slice/size an item that is then skipped. The review confirmed this is correct and a strict improvement — but **no test asserts it**: if the gate moved back behind the slice, the extraction in `tests/test_dd7d_item_scoped_skip_a360.sh` would simply exclude the slice and case (A) would still pass. Add an assertion that the gate precedes both. **(b) `tests/test_dd7d_item_scoped_skip_a360.sh` carries `# roadmap:a360`, which is INERT** — `a360` lives in `TODO.md`, not `ROADMAP.md`, so `item_open("a360")` is false and its failures correctly count today. It fails SAFE, but if `a360` were ever promoted to `ROADMAP.md` unticked, the test would become **silently maskable** — the exact disarm class `id:86ca` is about. Either drop the header (defect-fix tests omit it by convention) or point it at a real ROADMAP item. **THIRD GAP FOUND 2026-08-22 — an existing assertion is VACUOUS against the real incident shape.** `tests/test_orphan_item_binding_branch_name.sh` asserts that `f272` must not leak into the suppressed set. But its fixture keeps `f272` out of the ledger entirely, so pre-fix it hit the `item not in ROADMAP — ambiguous` branch and DID emit a suppress entry — whereas the REAL repo had `f272` as prose inside a ticked `- [x] … the item-0295 marker` body in `ROADMAP.archive.md` and therefore took the *closed ⇒ stale orphan ⇒ do NOT suppress* branch, emitting NOTHING. The observed set never contained `f272` in either world, so the assertion could not have failed for the reason it names — it passes vacuously. The new `tests/test_loderite_starvation_real_shape_a360.sh` covers the real shape (and drives the REAL `stranded-branch-scan.sh` rather than the fake scanner `test_dd7d_item_scoped_skip_a360.sh` uses), so the gap is closed by ADDITION — but the vacuous assertion should still be re-pointed or removed so it stops reading as coverage it does not provide. <!-- id:915b -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`lib-private-remote.sh` emits `printf: write error: Broken pipe` to stderr on its SUCCESS path — noise on the one predicate that decides publish-vs-don't-publish** — observed live 2026-08-22 on a real `git push` to `origin` (a private host), twice in one push. **Verdicts are CORRECT and this is NOT a security defect** — verified by sourcing the lib and calling it directly: a private host returns 0 (PRIVATE) and a public host returns 1 (PUBLIC), and the pattern file parses to 3 patterns. **Mechanism:** `is_private_remote_url`'s source-3 loop (`relay/scripts/lib-private-remote.sh:160-163`) does `return 0` on the FIRST matching pattern, which tears down the `< <(private_host_res)` process substitution while `private_host_res` (line 136) is still `printf`ing the remaining patterns. So the broken pipe fires **only when a host IS matched as private** — the success path — and never on the public path, where the loop runs to completion. **Why fix it anyway:** (a) it is stderr noise on the PRIVACY GATE, so at a glance it is indistinguishable from the gate malfunctioning, and the gate's whole job is to be trustworthy at a glance; (b) it is exactly the SIGPIPE class this repo already lints for (`id:b818`, `tests/lint-pipefail-sigpipe.py`) — a shared, security-relevant predicate should not be the one place it leaks; (c) a future caller that runs under `set -o pipefail` and keys on the pipeline status could read the success path as a failure, which WOULD be a fail-open. Likely fix: drain or close the substitution before returning (capture the patterns into an array first, then loop over the array — no subshell to break), rather than suppressing the message. Done-check: a push to a private remote produces ZERO stderr from this lib, both verdicts still assert correctly, and the sigpipe lint covers the file. Relates `id:b818`, `id:4d44` (the per-remote push gate that consumes this predicate), `id:a726`(c). **INBOUND `routed:d690` from it-infra (2026-08-22) — INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of this exact defect, adopted here rather than filed twice.** A different session on a different repo hit the same stderr noise and diagnosed it identically without seeing this item: `private_host_res()` is a process-substitution WRITER whose consumer at `:160-163` does `return 0` on the first matching pattern, abandoning the writer mid-loop so its next `printf` takes EPIPE. Their added detail: observed **2x per push, 3 times on 2026-08-22**, and they classify it as the same SIGPIPE-race family as the 2026-08-21 `discoveries.md` entry (producer piped into an early-exiting consumer). They independently reach the same conclusion this item does — COSMETIC, because the predicate's return value is correct and no `pipefail` promotion occurs — and the same fix shape: drain the writer before returning (set a flag, `break`, let the loop finish) or read the patterns into an array first rather than streaming. Two independent reports of one defect raises its priority: it makes a clean push look like it errored, on the predicate that decides publish-vs-don't-publish. <!-- routed:d690 --> <!-- id:0842 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`tests/run-tests.sh`: ARM a test the moment it first goes green, regardless of its `# roadmap:` item's checkbox** — owner decision 2026-08-22 (`/relay human`, REVIEW_ME.md tier (b)). Today a test whose `# roadmap:XXXX` item is still unticked is reported `EXPECTED-RED` on failure. That is correct for a genuine RED spec, but it also DISARMS a test that is ALREADY GREEN under an open item: if it regresses, the suite stays green-with-an-expected-red and nobody is told. Live instance at decision time: `tests/test_privacy_gate_prepush.sh` passes standalone while `id:ebd0` (`ROADMAP.md:1252`, `[INPUT — access]`) is open — the warn+log half shipped, the access half did not. A sweep of every `# roadmap:`-headed test found it to be the only unambiguous instance, but the CLASS recurs on any partially-shipped item. **Owner chose the class fix over re-homing `ebd0`'s green half**, so `ebd0` is deliberately left as-is. **This changes a documented convention** — `CLAUDE.md` §Testing's expected-red semantics — so the doc must be updated in the same change. Design note: "first went green" needs a durable record (a state file, or promote-on-first-pass), since a fresh checkout has no history; decide that in the implementation. Supersedes the one-off remedy proposed in the REVIEW_ME box. <!-- id:86ca -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **Parity test pinning `destructive-git-guard.py`'s liveness rule against `heartbeat.sh`'s** — owner decision 2026-08-22 (`/relay human`, REVIEW_ME.md tier (b)). `id:6f62` shared the runId predicate (`lib-pool-runs.py::is_pool_run`) but left the LIVENESS predicate re-derived: the guard reimplements `heartbeat.sh`'s `is_alive` (ts + `3600` TTL) in-process. **The re-derivation STAYS — it is a deliberate latency trade** (shelling to `heartbeat.sh` would add a bash+`jq` fan-out to every single Bash tool call), so this is explicitly NOT a one-definition extraction. What is missing is that nothing MEASURES the divergence. A real one already exists: `heartbeat.sh`'s `hb_ts()` falls back to the marker file's MTIME when `heartbeat_ts` is missing or garbled and can then report ALIVE, while the guard reads a missing field as `ts=0` ⇒ stale ⇒ skip. Both err SAFE today, which is exactly why it will drift unnoticed. Done-check: one fixture set (valid ts, missing field, garbled field, expired ts, fresh ts) exercised through BOTH rules, asserting the intended agreements AND pinning the intended MTIME-fallback difference, so a future change to either side fails loudly. Owner rejected the cheaper alternative (an in-file comment stating intent) — a comment rots, a test does not. <!-- id:5f95 -->
- [ ] [ROUTINE] **`destructive-git-guard.py`: scan `eval` / `bash -c` / `sh -c` string arguments with the existing `_RAW_PATTERNS`** — owner decision 2026-08-22 (`/relay human`, REVIEW_ME.md tier (b)). A wrapped tree-wide reset (`eval '<the reset form>'`, `bash -c '<the reset form>'`) is currently ALLOWED: it tokenises cleanly and `_split_git_commands` only starts a command at a bare `git` token, so the quoted payload is one opaque argument the guard never inspects. Correctly blocked today: the `-C`-redirected reset, `cd sub && git checkout -- .`, `git clean -fdx`, `git stash drop`. **Now load-bearing:** since the owner's 2026-08-22 ruling the five tree-wide forms are an UNCONDITIONAL deny, so an agent that hits the wall has a live incentive to reach for `bash -c` — precisely the routed-around-into-the-tree-wide-form failure the guard's own header warns about. **Scope is deliberately BOUNDED:** the command-substitution form (a `$(...)`-built subcommand) stays an ACCEPTED, documented boundary — the owner explicitly declined the fuller "close every wrapper form" option, because the guard is accident-prevention, not adversarial, and chasing substitution adds false-positive surface. Done-check: the three wrapper forms deny; the substitution form still passes (assert it, so the boundary is pinned rather than merely unimplemented); no regression in the 18 currently-allowed forms, path-scoped reverts included. **Related, observed 2026-08-22 during the very pass that filed this:** the guard fired on a Bash call whose only offence was QUOTING a destructive form inside a heredoc — the `id:9979` false-positive class, live and now twice-confirmed. <!-- id:fb2c -->
  - **Decide before building (this is why the lane is `[INPUT — meeting]`, not `[ROUTINE]`):** (a) ONE skill with three modes or THREE skills — they share a state model but differ in direction (wrapup = *close cleanly*, handover = *write what the next session must know*, resume = *read it back*), and the `meeting-cross`→`/meeting --cross` deprecation (`id:4f5f`) is the local precedent that separate alias-skills rot; (b) what the handover artifact IS and where it lives — a file in the repo, an entry in the diary, `~/.config/`, or nothing durable at all (note the diary already records *what was done*; the gap is *what is still open and what the next session must not re-derive*); (c) what belongs in it — open threads, decisions awaiting the owner, in-flight background agents/pool runs, uncommitted or parked work, and explicitly-rejected paths so they are not re-proposed; (d) overlap with the existing mandatory post-prompt pair — `git-diary-workflow` + `todo-update` already run per prompt and already commit/push/record, so wrapup must NOT duplicate them, and per the standing ctx-budget heuristic these new skills should be **explicitly opt-in, never mandatory-per-prompt** (a per-prompt skill multiplies its SKILL.md size by prompt count); (e) whether `resume` is even a skill rather than just the harness's own context restoration — check before building, since a skill that duplicates a harness feature is a vestige on arrival (constraint archaeology).
  - **Mechanize-first, with the LLM only where it must be:** the sweep is a pure-function check over git/filesystem/log state and should be a tested script that FAILS LOUDLY on each unclean condition; reserve the LLM for composing the handover prose (what is open, what was decided, what was deliberately not done). A detector whose resolution silently no-ops is the recorded anti-pattern — so if the sweep finds a dirty tree or a live agent, it must surface and block the "clean wrapup" claim, not print and continue.
  - **Do NOT auto-act on findings.** Disposal of parked work stays human-invoked (`id:a4e9`), and stopping a pool is an owner decision. The skill reports; the human decides.
